nhl.xg_for.label: Team expected goals for (shot quality created), strength-split and adjusted
nhl.xg_for.mechanism: Expected goals credit the quality and location of shots a team generates, so xGF measures offensive process with far less shooting-luck noise than goals.
nhl.xg_for.rationale: Goals are rare and luck-heavy; xG stabilises much faster and is the best public repeatable measure of offence. Subtle: public xG models omit passing/pre-shot movement and goalie quality, treat all shooters equally, and are biased by rink scorer inconsistency in shot location. Use it split by 5v5 / PP and adjust for opponent and for score effects, since trailing teams inflate volume.
nhl.xg_for.measurement: Per-60 xGF at 5v5 (score-and-venue adjusted) and on PP, as exponentially weighted averages (half-life ~25-40 games) shrunk toward league mean with a prior sized by games played; adjust for opponent by regressing team-game xGF on offence and defence team effects plus home indicator (ridge). Report separate 5v5 and special-teams components rather than one blended number.
free_sources: MoneyPuck free CSVs (moneypuck.com/data.htm: shots, skaters, goalies, teams)
Natural Stat Trick (naturalstattrick.com team/player/line tables with score-and-venue adjustment)
Evolving-Hockey (evolving-hockey.com, free public tables partly gated)

nhl.xg_against.label: Team expected goals against (shot suppression quality)
nhl.xg_against.mechanism: Expected goals against measure the quality and quantity of chances a team's skaters allow, independent of whether the goalie happened to stop them.
nhl.xg_against.rationale: Separates defensive process (what the skaters control) from goaltending outcome; critical for totals, team totals and for estimating what shot quality a goalie will face. Subtle: xGA as published is goalie-neutral, so any goalie-specific adjustment must be layered on top, and defensive effects partly reflect personnel (injuries to top pair) that stale season averages hide.
nhl.xg_against.measurement: Per-60 xGA at 5v5 and on PK, score/venue-adjusted, exponentially weighted with opponent adjustment via the same ridge team-effects model as xG for; recompute with lineup-weighted projection (replace absent defencemen with replacement-level impact) for the specific game.
free_sources: MoneyPuck free CSVs (moneypuck.com/data.htm: shots, skaters, goalies, teams)
Natural Stat Trick (naturalstattrick.com team/player/line tables with score-and-venue adjustment)
Evolving-Hockey (evolving-hockey.com, free public tables partly gated)

nhl.pace.label: Shot-attempt rate / event pace (combined attempts per 60)
nhl.pace.mechanism: A game's total shot-attempt volume (both teams) sets the number of chances available, which scales shots on goal, saves, and total goals.
nhl.pace.rationale: Pace is a team style trait (system, forecheck, trap) and a matchup trait: two high-event teams exceed the sum of their parts, two trap teams undershoot. Subtle: pace changes with score effects and special-teams time, and is partly a coaching-system effect that moves after coaching changes, so long averages lag.
nhl.pace.measurement: Combined Corsi attempts per 60 for team A offence plus team B defence (and vice versa) using opponent-adjusted team effects; track team-level 'event rate' (attempts for + against per 60) with EWMA; include rink-specific scorer bias correction.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick (naturalstattrick.com team/player/line tables with score-and-venue adjustment)
MoneyPuck free CSVs (moneypuck.com/data.htm: shots, skaters, goalies, teams)

nhl.special_teams.label: Power-play and penalty-kill efficiency (xG-based) and special-teams matchup
nhl.special_teams.mechanism: Special teams convert penalties into goals at far higher rates than 5v5, so unit quality and opponent PK structure shift team goals and totals.
nhl.special_teams.rationale: The PP xGF/60 of the unit and the PK xGA/60 of the opponent combine multiplicatively with expected PP opportunities. Subtle: raw PP% is dominated by shooting luck and sample size; xG-based rates plus personnel (injury to PP1 quarterback) are far more repeatable. Use regressed rates and account for aggressive vs passive PK shapes.
nhl.special_teams.measurement: PP xGF/60 and PK xGA/60 from last ~40 games, EWMA, shrunk to league mean; combine as expected PP goals = (team A PP xGF rate adj for opp PK) x (expected PP minutes from penalties model); replace personnel when key unit members out.

nhl.goalie_start.label: Confirmed starting goalie (timestamped) and its pregame probability
nhl.goalie_start.mechanism: The starting goalie determines the goal-prevention quality of the whole game and defines saves-market eligibility, so which goalie plays shifts goals, totals, winners and saves lines.
nhl.goalie_start.rationale: Starter identity is the single largest in-day information event in NHL pricing. Subtle: confirmation often arrives after morning skate (late morning to ~1 hr before puck drop) and some starters are only confirmed via lineup card; markets may be open before confirmation, so any model has to carry a start probability (back-to-back, recent rest pattern) and reprice on the news. A goalie who starts but is pulled early still settles his saves market on partial saves.
nhl.goalie_start.measurement: Record every source's announcement with timestamp; before confirmation model P(starter) from rest days, back-to-back second-game rate, consecutive starts, coach pattern; after confirmation set to 1. Feed downstream models both goalie identity and confirmation time.
free_sources: Daily Faceoff (dailyfaceoff.com line combinations, projected/confirmed starting goalies)

nhl.goalie_quality.label: Goalie quality: goals saved above expected (GSAx), danger-zone save rates, workload-adjusted
nhl.goalie_quality.mechanism: A goalie's ability to save shots beyond what shot quality predicts directly changes goals against and the probability a given shot becomes a goal.
nhl.goalie_quality.rationale: GSAx removes shot-quality noise but is extremely noisy per goalie per season; true talent differences are smaller than they appear and shrinkage is mandatory. Subtle: the signal is mostly in high-danger and rebound control and differs by shot type; a small multi-year prior outperforms single-season numbers, and backup goalies have small samples.
nhl.goalie_quality.measurement: GSAx/60 and sv% by danger bucket over 2-3 seasons with exponential weights, shrunk toward league (Bayesian beta-binomial or empirical Bayes with prior strength ~1000-2000 shots); keep separate 5v5 and PK; adjust for team defence via on-ice xG model fitted with goalie fixed effect.
free_sources: MoneyPuck free CSVs (moneypuck.com/data.htm: shots, skaters, goalies, teams)

nhl.lines.label: Line combinations and defence pairings (forward lines, D pairs, PP/PK units)
nhl.lines.mechanism: Which skaters play together determines each player's linemates, shooting opportunities and quality of competition, which drives individual production independent of team strength.
nhl.lines.rationale: Line deployment explains much of the variation between players of equal talent, and lines change with injuries, scratches, and in-game coaching tweaks. Subtle: projected lines from the morning skate can differ from the puck-drop lines, coaches shuffle after losses and in third periods, and a 'line' list does not give minutes without a coach-specific deployment model.
nhl.lines.measurement: Scrape projected lines at multiple times (day before, morning skate, ~1 hr before) and compare to realized shift data after the game; estimate each player's realised line-mate TOI sharing; keep a shuffle-rate per coach; use confirmed lines only for models claiming pregame knowledge.
free_sources: Daily Faceoff (dailyfaceoff.com line combinations, projected/confirmed starting goalies)

nhl.toi.label: Projected time on ice by strength state (EV, PP, PK, late-game)
nhl.toi.mechanism: TOI by situation is the volume multiplier for every counting stat: more minutes (especially PP) means more shots, points and saves opportunities.
nhl.toi.rationale: Individual shots, points and assists scale nearly linearly with TOI; the key is the split by strength state because PP minutes are worth much more per minute than EV minutes. Subtle: TOI is partly endogenous to the score (stars play more when trailing), to penalties drawn and to coach decisions, so a pregame projection must be from the specific lineup and expected game script, not season average.
nhl.toi.measurement: Rolling EWMA TOI per strength state (last 10-20 games) conditioned on lineup (who is in/out), with adjustments for expected penalties and expected score script; model TOI by state as separate counts then sum; record projected-vs-actual error.

nhl.pp_role.label: Power-play unit assignment (PP1/PP2) and role (shooter/quarterback/net-front)
nhl.pp_role.mechanism: PP1 skaters get most PP time and the highest-leverage shot/assist roles on the man advantage, which produces a disproportionate share of points and shots.
nhl.pp_role.rationale: A PP1 quarterback or bumper position carries high point and shot rates per minute; PP2 players get far less. Roles matter within the unit: the one-timer position takes shots, the quarterback assists. Subtle: PP1 changes on injury/slump and is not announced, PP minutes are drawn opportunistically so the unit's expected PP minutes depend on the referee and opponent discipline.
nhl.pp_role.measurement: From play-by-play shifts, estimate each skater's share of team PP TOI over last 15 games and role via shot/pass positions; project expected PP minutes = opp penalties drawn per game x unit share; combine with player PP shot and point rates per PP minute.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick (naturalstattrick.com team/player/line tables with score-and-venue adjustment) PP unit tables

nhl.shot_rate.label: Individual shot-attempt / SOG rate (per 60) by strength state
nhl.shot_rate.mechanism: A player's shot generation rate is a stable skill/role trait and, multiplied by TOI, gives expected shots on goal.
nhl.shot_rate.rationale: Individual shot rates are among the most repeatable player stats, far more than goals. Subtle: SOG differs from attempts by block and miss rates (shot type, defender, position), and SOG counts vary by rink scorer; rates must be split by EV/PP and shrunk, and recomputed after linemate changes.
nhl.shot_rate.measurement: Individual SOG/60 and attempts/60 by EV and PP, EWMA over last 40 games with shrinkage to position-specific league mean (prior weight ~300-400 minutes), adjusted for opponent (opp shot suppression by position) and home rink counting bias.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick (naturalstattrick.com team/player/line tables with score-and-venue adjustment)

nhl.finishing.label: Shooting percentage / finishing talent (regressed)
nhl.finishing.mechanism: Conversion of shots into goals is a mixture of shooter skill and luck; the skill part is small and persistent, the rest is noise that should regress.
nhl.finishing.rationale: Overweighting a hot shooting% inflates goal and point projections for players on lucky runs and underweights hidden talent for elite shooters. Subtle: true shooting talent is shot-quality adjusted (xG per shot), so compare goals to ixG to identify skill; sample sizes for individual shooters need multi-season data.
nhl.finishing.measurement: Compute goals minus individual xG and shot-quality-adjusted SH%; shrink with beta prior (about 200-300 shots for forwards) toward position mean plus a persistent-skill component estimated from multi-season repeatability; use predicted SH% not raw.

nhl.assist_rate.label: Primary/secondary assist involvement rate
nhl.assist_rate.mechanism: Assists reflect passing roles and linemate shooting; primary assists are more repeatable and skill-linked than secondary assists, which are noisy.
nhl.assist_rate.rationale: Assist markets depend on who is on the ice when a goal is scored and who the passer is; primary assists track playmaking, secondary assists are close to random on-ice presence. Subtle: assist totals depend on official scorer decisions and on linemates' shooting luck, so a playmaker with poor finishing linemates underperforms.
nhl.assist_rate.measurement: Primary and secondary assists per 60 at EV and PP separately, EWMA with shrinkage (primary assists prior ~ 400 minutes, secondary larger); condition on linemates' ixG and on-ice shooting expectation rather than realized on-ice SH%.

nhl.injuries_pit.label: Injury/scratch/return status with point-in-time vintages
nhl.injuries_pit.mechanism: Absences change line composition, ice time, power-play roles and opponent matchups, and a late scratch can void or zero a player prop.
nhl.injuries_pit.rationale: Key-player availability is among the largest and most abrupt drivers of both team and player outputs. Subtle: official NHL injury disclosure is vague (upper/lower body) and often only known at warmups; vintage timestamps matter to avoid leaking after-the-fact knowledge, and return-from-injury games carry reduced minutes and rust. Lineup news timing varies for scratches (coach decisions announced at morning skate).
nhl.injuries_pit.measurement: Snapshot injury and lineup lists with timestamps (day before, morning of, warmups); encode status (out, GTD, probable) and expected-return game; compute team-level WAR/xG impact of absentees using on/off or replacement-level substitution; archive vintage for leak-free backtests.

nhl.opp_supp.label: Opponent shot suppression / goals-against by player position
nhl.opp_supp.mechanism: How many shots and points an opponent allows to a given position type scales the expected output of the player facing them.
nhl.opp_supp.rationale: Opponent adjustment for individual markets must be position-aware: a defence that allows many point shots inflates defencemen SOG, a team that blocks lots of shots reduces SOG per attempt. Subtle: opponent effects are small relative to player and role effects and noisy, so apply as shrunk multiplicative factors, not raw rank.
nhl.opp_supp.measurement: Estimate opponent effect on shots by player position (F/D) via mixed model: player-game SOG ~ player effect + opponent effect + home + TOI; shrink opponent random effects; use rolling window of 40-60 games; include opponent block rate and shot-attempt volume allowed.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick (naturalstattrick.com team/player/line tables with score-and-venue adjustment)

nhl.rest_travel.label: Rest, back-to-back, travel distance/time zone, schedule density
nhl.rest_travel.mechanism: Fatigue and compressed schedules reduce skater performance and shift goalie starts to backups, which changes team strength and saves.
nhl.rest_travel.rationale: The most reliable schedule effects in NHL are back-to-back second games (more backup goalies, slightly worse results) and long road trips. Subtle: market prices largely incorporate rest, so the residual edge is in interactions (backup goalie probability, which team is rested while the other is tired, travel from different time zones) rather than the simple flag.
nhl.rest_travel.measurement: Features: days of rest, games in last 4/6/8 days, back-to-back flag, travel km and time-zone change in last 48 hr, home stand/road trip index; estimate effects via regression on xG differential controlling for strength; interact with starter rotation.
free_sources: Hockey-Reference (hockey-reference.com game logs, team splits) schedule

nhl.venue.label: Rink effects (shot counting bias), home advantage, building specifics
nhl.venue.mechanism: Different arenas record shots, hits and takeaways at different rates, and home teams see small advantages (last change, crowd, referees).
nhl.venue.rationale: Rink scorer bias inflates or deflates shot and SOG counts by arena; since SOG props settle on official counts, this is a pure measurement effect worth several percent. Subtle: bias is estimated from visiting teams' stats across venues and shifts with scorer turnover, and home advantage in hockey is modest and partly driven by last-change matchups.
nhl.venue.measurement: Estimate venue-specific shot-count multipliers via fixed-effects model on visiting teams' SOG per 60 across venues; use team-venue-season random effect; add home-ice indicator and altitude (Denver, Utah) as controls.

nhl.score_state.label: Game-script / score effects on shot volume, quality and pulled-goalie behavior
nhl.score_state.mechanism: Teams trailing push shot volume and risk, teams leading play defensive structures, changing shot totals and shot quality within the same game.
nhl.score_state.rationale: Shot counts for the favourite and for stars depend on expected game script: a heavy favourite often leads and accumulates fewer SOG late, while the underdog trailing generates more attempts but lower quality. Subtle: the pregame uncertainty over script means player-shot distributions are mixtures over win-probability scenarios, not shift in the mean alone.
nhl.score_state.measurement: Estimate shot rate and xG per 60 by score state (down 2+, down 1, tied, up 1, up 2+) per team, then integrate over the game-script distribution implied by pregame win probability and total (simulation); report adjusted rates for 'neutral' state to avoid circularity.

nhl.ot_so.label: Overtime and shootout model and rules
nhl.ot_so.mechanism: Overtime and shootout resolve regulation ties through a different structure (3v3 sudden death, then skill contest), which sets the final outcome for markets that include them.
nhl.ot_so.rationale: Settlement wording decides whether overtime/shootout counts; for including-OT markets the winner is a function of regulation-tie probability and OT/SO win probability (near coin-flip with small team-strength tilt). Subtle: regular-season OT is 5-minute 3v3 followed by shootout, playoffs are full 20-minute 5v5 periods with no shootout, so the same code must branch by season type; OT goal totals contribute to total-goals markets only if rules include them.
nhl.ot_so.measurement: Model P(tie after 60) from bivariate goal distribution, P(OT goal) by 3v3 scoring rates, and shootout win prob from shooter/goalie talent with strong shrinkage toward 50%; attach flags from m.rules_text for whether OT/SO is counted; encode playoff/regular season switch.

nhl.empty_net.label: Empty-net goals and pulled-goalie timing
nhl.empty_net.mechanism: Trailing teams pull the goalie late, generating empty-net goals for the leader and extra shots for the trailer, which moves totals, margins and goalie saves.
nhl.empty_net.rationale: Empty-net goals add to the total in some close games, are strongly correlated with close margins, and affect puck-line (the leader wins by 2) and saves markets. Subtle: pull timing differs by coach (earlier pulls increase both EN goals against and chances), and a goal scored into an empty net may count toward totals but not for goalie stats.
nhl.empty_net.measurement: Per-coach and per-team pull time distribution (seconds remaining when down 1, down 2); probability of empty-net goal conditional on lead by one/two; incorporate into total and margin simulation with explicit EN module; check wording for EN goal inclusion.

nhl.period_split.label: Period-level scoring and shot distribution
nhl.period_split.mechanism: Goals and shots are not uniform across periods: the second period (long change) and third (score effects) behave differently from the first.
nhl.period_split.rationale: Period markets need period-specific rates, not one-third of the full game. Subtle: first periods usually have lower scoring and fewer penalties, third periods have empty-net goals and score effects, and the 2nd period long-change effect increases scoring chances against away team in the middle frame in some analyses; use team-specific period splits shrunk strongly toward league period shape.
nhl.period_split.measurement: Estimate league period shape of goals/shots by season; team-specific multiplicative deviations via hierarchical model with heavy shrinkage; produce Poisson/negative-binomial period distributions and joint period correlation.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick (naturalstattrick.com team/player/line tables with score-and-venue adjustment)

nhl.stat_dist.label: Per-stat count distributions and correlations (Poisson/NB, joint)
nhl.stat_dist.mechanism: Counts (shots, points, saves) are overdispersed discrete variables whose full distribution, not just the mean, determines threshold-rung probabilities.
nhl.stat_dist.rationale: Threshold markets depend on tail probabilities, which are controlled by dispersion and by correlation with game total and team results. Subtle: simple Poisson underestimates variance for shots driven by script and TOI uncertainty; zero-inflated or mixed distributions fit points better; correlation across a player's goals, assists, shots matters for combined markets and parlay legs.
nhl.stat_dist.measurement: Fit per-stat count models (NB or compound Poisson with TOI uncertainty) to player-game history with covariates; estimate dispersion via likelihood; compute joint correlation matrices by simulation within games; validate against realized rung frequencies.
free_sources: NHL web API api-web.nhle.com (/v1/gamecenter/{gameId}/play-by-play, /boxscore, /v1/schedule/{date}, /v1/club-stats/{team}/now) boxscore history

nhl.ratings.label: Team ratings, standings and season simulation
nhl.ratings.mechanism: A calibrated team rating system turns game-level strength into win probabilities and into season simulations for futures.
nhl.ratings.rationale: Futures and series prices depend on the distribution of team strength and its uncertainty, not just point estimates; ratings must update for injuries and trades. Subtle: points standings contain heavy luck (OT, shootouts, shooting%), so xG-based or goal-differential ratings are preferable and tie-break rules (regulation wins) affect seeding.
nhl.ratings.measurement: Elo or Bradley-Terry/Poisson ratings fit on score-adjusted xG differential with home and goalie terms, exponential time decay, shrinkage to preseason priors, then Monte Carlo season simulation using actual remaining schedule and NHL tie-break rules.
free_sources: MoneyPuck free CSVs (moneypuck.com/data.htm: shots, skaters, goalies, teams) (team ratings)

nhl.award_stats.label: Awards/season-stat candidate production to date and projection
nhl.award_stats.mechanism: Award and season-stat markets resolve on accumulated production plus voter perception, so current totals, games remaining and role determine the likely winner.
nhl.award_stats.rationale: For stat leaders (goals, points, saves) the rest-of-season distribution is the sum of per-game outcomes given health and deployment; for awards, production and team success drive narrative. Subtle: leader races are determined by top-tail variance and games remaining, and a leader's injury risk matters as much as rate.
nhl.award_stats.measurement: Rest-of-season rate projection (EWMA, regressed) x expected games remaining x health probability; simulate leaderboard; for awards, regress historical winners on stats, team rank and positional narrative to produce a voter-score model.

nhl.officials.label: Referee/linesman penalty-call tendencies
nhl.officials.mechanism: Referees differ in penalties called per game, which controls power-play opportunities and therefore goals, shots and PP-related prop volume.
nhl.officials.rationale: Penalty counts have an officiating component with persistent crew-level differences. Subtle: assignments are posted around game day (usually morning) so may be partial pregame, the signal is modest, and playoff officiating shifts to fewer calls; apply shrunk crew effect to expected power plays.
nhl.officials.measurement: Estimate referee effect on total penalties and PP opportunities via mixed model (game penalties ~ team effects + referee random effect), use two-referee crew sum; shrink strongly and refresh each season.

nhl.news.label: Trades, coaching changes, transactions, roster news
nhl.news.mechanism: Trades, coaching changes and signings change team composition and strategy, with a lag before public stats reflect them.
nhl.news.rationale: A coaching change alters deployment, pace and line usage; a trade changes who plays and in what role. Subtle: the effect is easiest to see in role (TOI, PP time) changes rather than ratings, and markets move on the news immediately; value is in timing and in modelling the transition (new coach reshuffles for a few games).
nhl.news.measurement: Event log with date and type (trade, waiver, call-up, coach change); indicator 'games since event'; estimate role/TOI shifts via difference-in-differences against pre-event baseline.

nhl.shots_against.label: Team shots-on-goal against, shot quality, score-effects adjusted
nhl.shots_against.mechanism: A defence's SOG-allowed rate and its shot-quality profile determine how many shots a goalie faces and how hard they are.
nhl.shots_against.rationale: Direct driver of goalie saves volume and of opposing player SOG. Subtle: SOG against differs from attempts against by block rate, and score effects distort raw counts (leading teams concede more shots), so use score-adjusted and lineup-adjusted values.
nhl.shots_against.measurement: SOG against per 60 at 5v5, PK, and total; score-adjusted EWMA (half-life ~25 games) with opponent adjustment via ridge team-effects; project for the specific lineup (missing defencemen).

nhl.penalty_rates.label: Penalties taken/drawn per 60 and referee crew tendencies
nhl.penalty_rates.mechanism: Penalties create power-play minutes, the highest-yield scoring and shot environment, so the expected number of PPs shifts team totals and individual props.
nhl.penalty_rates.rationale: Teams and players differ persistently in penalties taken and drawn; matchup rates (team A takes many, team B draws many) combine. Subtle: penalty calls are partly random and reflect referees and game state; effects strongest for PP-heavy players, and playoff penalty rates drop.
nhl.penalty_rates.measurement: Penalties taken/drawn per 60 at team and player level with EWMA and shrinkage; expected PP minutes for each team = f(team taken rate, opponent drawn rate, referee crew effect, season type); convert minutes to expected PP goals/shots.

nhl.goalie_workload.label: Goalie rest, consecutive starts, recent save-pct and backup identity
nhl.goalie_workload.mechanism: Coaches rotate goalies based on rest and schedule, and the backup is usually lower quality, so workload state predicts both who starts and team strength.
nhl.goalie_workload.rationale: Back-to-back second games frequently go to backups; consecutive-start counts and days since last start inform start probability. Subtle: the backup's talent is estimated on small samples and may differ from the starter by large margins in true skill, but public GSAx for backups is noisy so a prior is essential; recent save% adds little beyond talent.
nhl.goalie_workload.measurement: Features: days since last start, starts in last 7/14 days, back-to-back flag, goalie team's schedule ahead; build start-probability model per goalie/team; separately keep shrunk quality estimates for starter and backup.

nhl.shootout_record.label: Shootout/OT record and shooter/goalie shootout talent
nhl.shootout_record.mechanism: Shootouts depend on individual shooter and goalie skill, with persistent but small differences between teams.
nhl.shootout_record.rationale: Shootout outcomes are close to coin flips, with weak persistence for goalies and shooters; raw team shootout records are mostly noise. Subtle: the model should rely on shrunk individual shooter success (shot-type) and goalie shootout save rates, with weight near zero on team record.
nhl.shootout_record.measurement: Shooter shootout conversion and goalie shootout save% over multiple seasons, empirical-Bayes shrunk (prior heavy, ~50 attempts); team shootout win probability = 0.5 + small tilt; compare to market OT/SO prices.

nhl.shot_location.label: Shot location/danger-zone mix for and against
nhl.shot_location.mechanism: Shots from high-danger areas convert at several times the rate of perimeter shots, so shot-location mix explains goal expectation and goalie save% environment.
nhl.shot_location.rationale: Danger-zone mix helps separate teams that shoot a lot from teams that shoot well and tells whether a team's shot suppression is perimeter-forcing. Subtle: location data depends on rink-specific tracking (public data has coordinates with noise) and public xG models differ in treatment of rebounds and rush shots.
nhl.shot_location.measurement: Per-60 shots by danger zone (e.g. low/med/high or xG bin) for and against, 5v5 and special teams; EWMA with shrinkage; compute expected save% for a goalie facing that team's mix.

nhl.pdo_regression.label: Team PDO (SH% + SV%) and on-ice luck component
nhl.pdo_regression.mechanism: Team shooting% plus save% runs near 100 over long samples; deviations are mostly luck and revert toward the mean, so recent results overstate/understate true strength.
nhl.pdo_regression.rationale: Wins and goal differential in a short window embed PDO luck; a team with high PDO is likely to be priced above its process level. Subtle: some teams hold persistently above-average PDO due to elite finishing or goaltending, so regression should be partial and team-specific, and PDO is strongly correlated with score-effects when leading.
nhl.pdo_regression.measurement: Compute team 5v5 SH% and SV% over rolling 20/40 games, compare to xG-implied expected values (SH% vs xGF/shots, SV% vs xGA/shots-against); regress the difference to zero with weight proportional to sample; use as correction to goals-based ratings.

nhl.onice_shpct.label: Player on-ice shooting% and on-ice goals vs expected (point/assist luck)
nhl.onice_shpct.mechanism: Assists and points depend on teammates converting shots while the player is on the ice; on-ice SH% mostly regresses.
nhl.onice_shpct.rationale: A player with a lucky on-ice SH% has inflated recent points/assist rates that will revert; the opposite for unlucky ones. Subtle: elite playmakers do have persistent on-ice SH% edges (passing creates better shots), so the baseline is not league mean but player-specific shrunk expectation derived from xG on-ice.
nhl.onice_shpct.measurement: On-ice goals-for minus on-ice xGF per 60 at EV and PP over last 40 games; shrink toward player's multi-year on-ice xGF-implied rate; use xG-based expectation for point rate projection.

nhl.ixg_player.label: Individual expected goals per 60 (shot quality of the shooter's attempts)
nhl.ixg_player.mechanism: A player's ixG captures both how often and from where he shoots, predicting goals better than counting shots alone.
nhl.ixg_player.rationale: For goals and points markets, ixG/60 plus TOI gives a lower-noise baseline of scoring chances; combining with finishing skill shrinks luck. Subtle: ixG counts only own shots, so playmakers' value is missing, and PP vs EV ixG must be projected separately.
nhl.ixg_player.measurement: ixG/60 split by EV and PP over last 40-60 games (EWMA), shrink by position-specific prior; project onto game by TOI by strength state and opponent xGA-by-position.

nhl.shot_block_miss.label: Attempt-to-SOG conversion: block and miss rates by shooter type and opponent
nhl.shot_block_miss.mechanism: Only attempts that reach the net count as shots on goal; block and miss rates by shooter (defencemen shoot through traffic) and by opposing defence determine SOG per attempt.
nhl.shot_block_miss.rationale: SOG props settle on shots on goal, not attempts, so block rate of the opponent and the shooter's accuracy convert attempt volume into SOG. Subtle: defencemen from the point have much higher block rates, shot blockers (heavy blocking teams) shave SOG, and both are quasi-stable team traits.
nhl.shot_block_miss.measurement: Per-player SOG/attempt ratio (shrunk) and per-team opponent block%/miss% allowed by shot origin; SOG expectation = attempts x player accuracy x (opponent block factor).

nhl.dman_shot_profile.label: Defenceman offensive role: point shots, PP usage, offensive-zone starts
nhl.dman_shot_profile.mechanism: Offensive defencemen produce SOG and assists mainly via PP point shots and offensive-zone time, quite different from forwards' role.
nhl.dman_shot_profile.rationale: D-man SOG distributions are strongly tied to PP time and offensive deployment, producing more variance than forwards. Subtle: injury to the PP quarterback pushes a second D-man into the role, and blocking/miss rates at the point make SOG/attempt lower.
nhl.dman_shot_profile.measurement: For each defenceman as of date t: SOG/60 and shot attempts/60 at 5v5 and 5v4 over the last 60 games (half-life 30 games) from games before t; PP TOI share = own PP TOI / team PP TOI over last 15 games; offensive-zone start share = OZ shifts starts / (OZ + DZ starts) at 5v5; expected PP minutes = team expected PP minutes (opp penalties drawn per game) x PP TOI share. Shrink each rate to the D-position league mean with prior weight 400 minutes (5v5) and 60 minutes (5v4). Output the four values plus posterior sd.

nhl.linemate_quality.label: Linemate and centre quality (passing partners, finishing around the player)
nhl.linemate_quality.mechanism: A player's points depend on the shooting skill and xG of teammates who convert his passes, so linemate quality is an independent driver of assists and points.
nhl.linemate_quality.rationale: Assist and point projections should be conditional on actual linemates; a top winger with an elite finisher outproduces the same winger with a low-finishing centre. Subtle: linemates change frequently, and measuring 'quality' requires xG-based on-ice impact rather than counting stats, with joint-TOI weights.
nhl.linemate_quality.measurement: Compute TOI-weighted average of linemates' ixG/60 and finishing-adjusted shot quality; model player's on-ice xGF/60 as function of linemates via regularised regression (RAPM-style); project with confirmed lines.

nhl.last_change_matchups.label: Home last change and opponent matchup/shutdown deployment
nhl.last_change_matchups.mechanism: The home coach chooses matchups last, steering stars against weaker lines or shutdown pairs, which changes opposing players' production and line-level shot quality.
nhl.last_change_matchups.rationale: Matchup deployment can suppress an opposing top line's shots and points or free up a star against weak competition. Subtle: coaches differ in how heavily they match, the effect is greater at home, and the signal is in quality-of-competition (QoC) data that is noisy and slow to stabilise.
nhl.last_change_matchups.measurement: Compute head-to-head TOI shares between opposing lines/pairs from shift charts; estimate coach-specific matching intensity and QoC for each player; incorporate as a multiplicative adjustment to shot/xG rates.

nhl.pk_structure_opp.label: Opponent penalty-kill structure and PK shot concession
nhl.pk_structure_opp.mechanism: Passive box PKs concede perimeter shots while aggressive PKs concede high-danger chances; this shapes PP shot counts and goal probability.
nhl.pk_structure_opp.rationale: PP production for specific players depends on how the opponent kills penalties: passive PKs elevate point shooting (D-man SOG), aggressive ones raise turnover/shorthanded-goal risk. Subtle: PK shape is partly coach-system and shifts with personnel; public data gives outcomes (xGA/60, SOG/60 on PK) not scheme.
nhl.pk_structure_opp.measurement: Opponent PK SOGA/60 and xGA/60, shot-location split on PK; the share of PK shots from the point; combine with the player's PP shot role.

nhl.goalie_danger_split.label: Goalie save% by shot danger, rebounds and shot type
nhl.goalie_danger_split.mechanism: Goalies differ in how well they handle high-danger shots, rebounds and shot types; the opponent's shot mix interacts with that profile.
nhl.goalie_danger_split.rationale: A goalie strong on high-danger saves but weak on rebounds faces different expected save% against different teams; relevant for goals against, BTTS and saves prop (volume vs quality). Subtle: samples in danger buckets are very small so only heavily shrunk estimates are usable.
nhl.goalie_danger_split.measurement: Goalie xSV% by danger bucket with beta-binomial shrinkage; expected goals against = sum over the opponent's expected shots per bucket x (1 - shrunk sv%); compare against the generic goalie.

nhl.goalie_start_forecast.label: Pre-confirmation starting goalie probability (morning skate, rest pattern, coach history)
nhl.goalie_start_forecast.mechanism: Before confirmation the market must price a mixture of goalies; the probabilities determine expected team strength and the chance a saves prop's goalie plays.
nhl.goalie_start_forecast.rationale: Markets list before starters are confirmed; a model with a good start probability can capture mispricing on both goalie-specific props and team lines. Subtle: reporters post 'expected' starters hours early with variable reliability, and goalie first-off-the-ice at morning skate is a strong tell but only a few teams follow the ritual.
nhl.goalie_start_forecast.measurement: Regular season: per-team classification of starter rotation rules (b2b second game backup, 3-in-4 rule), logit model of P(starter) using rest, schedule and recency, plus reporter-source reliability weights. Playoff branch (no back-to-backs; rotation rules do not apply): hazard of starter change before game g+1 = logistic(a + b1*(game g save pct - incumbent season save pct) + b2*1[pulled in game g] + b3*goals allowed in game g + b4*(backup minus incumbent season GSAx/60) + b5*elimination-game flag + b6*incumbent injury flag), fitted on 2005-06 onward playoff goalie game logs (NHL API game type 3; Hockey-Reference playoff logs) with games started as the outcome; coefficients ridge-shrunk; a change resets the hazard for the new starter. Output: P(each goalie starts) per remaining game, mixed into team strength as a goalie-quality mixture.

nhl.morning_skate_signal.label: Morning-skate lineup and goalie signals (lines, rushes, first goalie off the ice)
nhl.morning_skate_signal.mechanism: Morning skate reveals which players will play and in which line configurations hours before the game, earlier than official lineups.
nhl.morning_skate_signal.rationale: Late-day lineup changes (scratches, call-ups, returns from injury) are the main source of pregame information asymmetry. Subtle: information comes through beat reporters and is noisy, and markets frequently react; usable only if timestamped and filtered by source reliability.
nhl.morning_skate_signal.measurement: Collect beat-writer-sourced lines and goalie reports with timestamp; compare to the final lineup to estimate per-source accuracy; use as probability-weighted lineup until official confirmation.

nhl.injury_return_ramp.label: Return-from-injury role and minutes ramp
nhl.injury_return_ramp.mechanism: Players returning from injury often have reduced TOI, altered PP roles and lower early-game performance.
nhl.injury_return_ramp.rationale: TOI and shots for a returning player in the first 1-3 games are systematically below baseline; markets sometimes price baseline. Subtle: ramp depends on injury type and team depth, and public data does not give injury type reliably.
nhl.injury_return_ramp.measurement: Count games since return; compute TOI ratio (return game vs pre-injury baseline) for historic returns by injury duration; apply as multiplicative TOI ramp.

nhl.callup_depth.label: Call-ups, healthy scratches and replacement-level depth
nhl.callup_depth.mechanism: When regulars are absent, replacement skaters change line quality, PP units and defensive structure.
nhl.callup_depth.rationale: Team strength differs from the full-lineup rating when depth skaters substitute; call-ups usually carry lower TOI and PP time. Subtle: the effect is nonlinear (losing a top-pair D vs a fourth-liner), so lineup-weighted team strength is required.
nhl.callup_depth.measurement: Replacement-level player value by position from AHL-to-NHL data; compute team xG rating as sum of lineup-weighted player impacts; track call-ups and scratches timestamped.

nhl.game_script_prob.label: Pregame score-script distribution (win probability, lead/trail probabilities)
nhl.game_script_prob.mechanism: The expected game script, derived from pregame win probability and total, determines how much each team leads or trails, and therefore shot volumes, TOI of stars, empty-net and pulled-goalie events.
nhl.game_script_prob.rationale: Player props in games with lopsided script differ from even games: favourites' stars may lose third-period minutes in blowouts; underdogs trailing take more shots. Subtle: the effect enters through conditional distributions, so features are scenario probabilities, not averages.
nhl.game_script_prob.measurement: Derive from team ratings (and the market line) the probabilities of lead/trail states by period through simulation; compute expected fraction of time in each score state; use as covariates in shots/TOI models.

nhl.coach_deployment_style.label: Coach deployment style (TOI concentration, line juggling, PP time allocation)
nhl.coach_deployment_style.mechanism: Coaches differ in how heavily they lean on top lines, how often they shuffle lines and how long PP1 stays on ice, controlling individual minutes.
nhl.coach_deployment_style.rationale: TOI volume for stars depends on coach tendencies as much as on talent; a coach change or a juggling streak changes minutes quickly. Subtle: effects interact with score script (leading, trailing) and with injuries; use coach-level aggregates with shrinkage.
nhl.coach_deployment_style.measurement: Coach-level: share of EV TOI by top line, PP1 share of PP time, line shuffle rate per game, third-period TOI in close games; EWMA with decay at coach change; project player TOI with coach random effect.

nhl.standings_stakes.label: Standings stakes and motivation (clinched, eliminated, seeding)
nhl.standings_stakes.mechanism: Teams with clinched or eliminated status may rest players or change deployment, altering strength in late-season games.
nhl.standings_stakes.rationale: Late-season games have heterogeneous effort and rest. Clinched teams rest stars (last 2-5 games); eliminated bottom teams sell veterans at the deadline, play call-ups and backup goalies, which lowers their points rate below the pre-deadline rating; the lottery incentive is weak since the worst team only has 18.5% first-draw odds and the 10-spot cap guarantees it a top-3 pick, so the effect must be estimated and shrunk, not assumed.
nhl.standings_stakes.measurement: Clinch/elimination status per team and date from 10,000 standings simulations (status fixed when P(playoffs) is 0 or 1 to the simulation's resolution). Tanking adjustment for points rates after the trade deadline: for team-games 2005-06 onward after the deadline, residual = actual standings points minus expected points from the team rating frozen at the deadline (home, rest, opponent adjusted); regress residual on eliminated flag, bottom-5 rank flag, net deadline man-games value traded away (TOI-weighted RAPM per 82 games of departed minus arrived players) and marginal lottery value of one extra loss = change in P(top-2 pick) per rank place from nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing under the format in force that season (3 draws 2016-2020; 2 draws with 10-spot move-up cap from 2021, worst team 18.5% first-draw odds). Coefficients shrunk toward 0 with a normal prior sd 0.05 points/game. Clinched-team rest effect: star participation rate in final 5 games versus season rate.

nhl.playoff_context.label: Playoff vs regular-season environment (tighter benches, fewer penalties, continuous OT)
nhl.playoff_context.mechanism: Playoff hockey shortens benches, concentrates TOI on top players, lowers penalty rates and eliminates shootouts, shifting every count distribution.
nhl.playoff_context.rationale: Calibration from regular-season data transfers poorly to the playoffs: top-line TOI and PP time shifts, scoring slightly changes, OT is 20-minute 5v5 sudden death. Subtle: sample sizes for playoff-only parameters are small, so priors must be hierarchical and anchored to historic playoff versus regular-season ratios.
nhl.playoff_context.measurement: Historic playoff/regular-season ratios of TOI by line position, penalties per game, goals per game; apply multiplicative adjustments; mark the playoff flag in all models.

nhl.ot_3v3_rate.label: 3v3 overtime scoring rate and star-driven OT deployment
nhl.ot_3v3_rate.mechanism: Three-on-three overtime rewards stars and puck possession, producing a distinct scoring rate per team and distinct TOI patterns for top players.
nhl.ot_3v3_rate.rationale: OT outcome in regular season splits between a 5-minute 3v3 period and shootout; teams with elite skating talent score more. Subtle: sample is small so team 3v3 rates are heavily shrunk; for player props TOI in OT adds a few minutes to stars in tied games.
nhl.ot_3v3_rate.measurement: Team 3v3 goals-for/against per 5 minutes over multiple seasons with empirical Bayes shrinkage; star-player OT TOI shares; feed into P(OT win) before shootout.

nhl.reg_tie_model.label: Regulation tie probability (bivariate Skellam/Poisson model)
nhl.reg_tie_model.mechanism: P(tie after 60) is determined by team goal expectation and correlation, and sets the weight of OT/SO in all settlement variants.
nhl.reg_tie_model.rationale: Regulation-tie probability varies with total and spread: lower-scoring close games tie more. It converts regulation-winner prices to full-game prices and sizes overtime and shootout markets. Subtle: independent Poisson misses overdispersion and empty-net correlation; calibration must be on historical tie frequency.
nhl.reg_tie_model.measurement: Fit bivariate Poisson or Dixon-Coles style model with team attack/defence and goalie terms, estimate dependence parameter and empty-net adjustments; calibrate P(tie) by total/spread bucket against historic frequency.

nhl.total_goal_dispersion.label: Goal-total dispersion and home/away goal correlation (incl. empty-net contribution)
nhl.total_goal_dispersion.mechanism: Total-goal outcomes are more dispersed than Poisson because of score effects, special teams and empty-net goals, and home/away goals are weakly correlated.
nhl.total_goal_dispersion.rationale: Threshold probabilities on total/team total depend on the variance and correlation, not just the mean. Subtle: dispersion differs by environment (high-event vs low-event teams), and quarter-point style ladders mean the tail rungs are pricing dispersion.
nhl.total_goal_dispersion.measurement: Fit negative-binomial or bivariate Poisson to team-game goals with covariates; estimate overdispersion and correlation by season; backtest calibration of tail rungs.

nhl.goalie_pull_risk.label: Probability the starter is pulled early/replaced and pull timing
nhl.goalie_pull_risk.mechanism: If a goalie is pulled after a bad start, his save count is truncated and the backup's workload rises, affecting saves markets and totals.
nhl.goalie_pull_risk.rationale: Pull risk rises with weak goalies facing strong offences and with coach style; it is not knowable pregame but its probability is. Subtle: pulls are uncommon but the lopsided cases dominate the lower tail of saves distribution and may be affected by settlement rules for a goalie who does not finish the game.
nhl.goalie_pull_risk.measurement: Per-goalie and per-coach pull rate (goals allowed threshold, time of pull); logistic model of P(pull) using opponent xGF, goalie quality and team win prob; integrate into saves distribution and total.

nhl.joint_outcome_correlation.label: Cross-market correlation (player stat with team result/total, between players)
nhl.joint_outcome_correlation.mechanism: Outcomes in the same game are correlated: team goals drive points of its skaters, and total goals drive both teams' markets, making parlays and combos non-independent.
nhl.joint_outcome_correlation.rationale: Combo and parlay pricing and head-to-head markets require a joint distribution rather than products of marginals. Subtle: correlation differs by position and role (PP1 forwards correlate more with team goals), and simple multiplication will mis-price combos.

nhl.scratch_void_risk.label: Scratch/DNP risk and settlement treatment (void, zero or loss)
nhl.scratch_void_risk.mechanism: Whether a player who does not play voids the market or settles as zero changes the effective probability of the contract.
nhl.scratch_void_risk.rationale: Settlement wording on DNP or goalie not starting can turn pregame uncertainty into a void rather than a loss; combined with lineup timing (markets open before confirmation) this changes optimal pricing. Subtle: must be read per ticker; do not assume.
nhl.scratch_void_risk.measurement: Parse the contract rules_primary into dnp_rule in {void, zero, loss} and record rule vintage. P(play) = 1 - P(scratch or injury absence) from nhl.injuries_pit status (out/GTD/probable) mapped to historical rates by status (shrunk k=30 cases) and, on game day, from confirmed lineups; use only vintages before decision time. EV under void = P(yes | play), under zero/loss = P(play) x P(yes | play) (leg counts as not occurring). Output P(play), both EVs and the rule vintage.

nhl.offfield_base_rate.label: Reference-class base rate for off-ice/office markets
nhl.offfield_base_rate.mechanism: Off-ice markets (trades, announcements, personnel) are driven by organizational decisions, not on-ice performance, so base rates and news flow dominate.
nhl.offfield_base_rate.rationale: These markets are largely unpredictable from sports statistics; value is in reference-class frequency and the announcement calendar. Subtle: information leaks via reporters precede official announcements, and the rules define what counts as official.
nhl.offfield_base_rate.measurement: Compile historical frequency of similar events per season and calendar window; compare against the contract's time horizon; track insider-report timestamps.

nhl.announcement_calendar.label: League calendar of scheduled events (draft, free agency, deadline, awards)
nhl.announcement_calendar.mechanism: Scheduled league events (trade deadline, draft, free-agency opening, awards show) give a hard timeline for transactions and awards markets.
nhl.announcement_calendar.rationale: Event timing bounds when a market can resolve and concentrates probability on specific dates. Subtle: dates shift year to year and a market may close before the event.
nhl.announcement_calendar.measurement: Maintain calendar of league dates per season; map to market close/expiry; compute fraction of historical transactions occurring in the window.

m.quote_history.label: Kalshi bid/ask/last time series (pre-game through close)
m.quote_history.mechanism: The traded price aggregates every participant's information about this contract, including injury and lineup news that moves faster than public stats.
m.quote_history.rationale: A price series is both a feature (the late price is usually a strong prior that model inputs must add to, not replace) and the reference for any edge claim. Subtle: the same last-trade price can be stale on thin NHL prop rungs, so bid/ask midpoints with timestamps matter more than last, and price movement after lineup/goalie/pitcher confirmation is information about what the news was worth.
m.quote_history.measurement: Store per-ticker candlesticks (bid, ask, last, volume) at 1-minute or finer resolution, align to scheduled start and to timestamps of lineup/starter confirmation; derive mid, spread, move since open, move since confirmation. Never use post-close values as pregame features.

m.orderbook_depth.label: Order-book depth and spread
m.orderbook_depth.mechanism: Depth and spread determine whether a modelled edge can be executed and how much the quoted price reflects informed versus noise flow.
m.orderbook_depth.rationale: Wide spreads and thin depth on NHL prop and long-tail rungs mean the midpoint is a noisy probability estimate and the edge after crossing the spread may be negative. Subtle: historical depth is only available if captured live, so the pregame view is whatever was snapshotted; reconstructing it from trades is approximate.
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Snapshot the book (top-N levels both sides) at fixed intervals before start; compute spread, depth within 2 cents of mid, imbalance. Compare model edge to half-spread plus fee to get executable edge.

m.volume_oi.label: Volume and open interest
m.volume_oi.mechanism: Volume and open interest proxy for how many participants have priced the contract and therefore how efficient the price is likely to be.
m.volume_oi.rationale: High-volume markets (game winners, totals) are typically priced by more informed flow than thin player props; a model needs a different shrinkage toward the market in each regime. Subtle: volume surges in the final hour often coincide with lineup news and are not directional by themselves.
m.volume_oi.measurement: Cumulative and last-hour volume, open interest, number of distinct trades from the trade tape; bucket markets by liquidity tier and estimate market-vs-model weight per tier.

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder (monotonicity, implied distribution)
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: Rungs of a threshold ladder (e.g. 4+, 5+, 6+) must imply one coherent count distribution; deviations expose stale or mispriced rungs and reveal the market's implied mean and variance.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Ladders for the same player/game are strongly correlated, so edges on adjacent rungs are not independent bets and exposure must be sized per ladder. Subtle: because each rung is a survival probability P(X>=k), monotone non-increasing is a hard constraint, and fitting a Poisson/negative-binomial to the rungs gives an implied mean that can be compared to a model mean on a like-for-like basis.
m.ladder_structure.measurement: For each event/player collect all live rungs at one timestamp; check P(k) non-increasing; fit a discrete distribution (Poisson, negative binomial, or free-form isotonic) to mid prices; compare implied mean/variance and per-rung residual to the model; track which rungs the market lags when news arrives.
free_sources: Kalshi public market-data API (api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2: /markets, /markets/trades, /series/{series}/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks) (all markets sharing an event_ticker)

m.settlement_truth.label: Settled result, settlement value and timestamp
m.settlement_truth.mechanism: The settled value is the only ground truth for calibrating every other input and exposes rule-edge cases (overtime, voids, delayed games).
m.settlement_truth.rationale: Without exact settlement values, hit rates and calibration are computed against a proxy (box score) that may differ from Kalshi's source (official stats, correction windows). Subtle: stat corrections after the game (scoring changes, hit/error changes, assist reassignments) can flip a threshold, so the settlement timestamp and source matter.
m.settlement_truth.measurement: Join Kalshi settled result and settlement_value to the official box score by game id; flag disagreements and post-game scoring changes; keep settlement time minus game end time.

m.rules_text.label: Versioned rules_primary / settlement wording (OT, ties, postponement, void)
m.rules_text.mechanism: The settlement wording defines which events count (overtime, extra innings, shootout goals, delayed games, DNPs) and therefore changes the true probability of the same real-world sport.
m.rules_text.rationale: Identical-looking contracts can differ: whether overtime/extra innings counts, whether a player who does not play voids or settles at zero, how postponements and shortened games resolve, which official stat source governs. A model that ignores the wording mis-prices the tail. Subtle: wording changes between series/seasons, so it must be versioned per ticker rather than assumed.
m.rules_text.measurement: Pull rules_primary/rules_secondary per market and hash it; extract flags (counts_overtime, counts_shootout, void_if_dnp, postponement_rule, source) by pattern matching and manual review of each new template; join to every training row.

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook / exchange reference prices with timestamps
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sharp sportsbook and exchange lines are a competing aggregation of information and the standard benchmark for fair probability.
m.external_lines.rationale: Using a de-vigged external line as a feature or benchmark is often a stronger baseline than any public-stats model, and disagreement with Kalshi flags either a stale Kalshi quote or a rule-wording difference. Subtle: books price different settlement terms (e.g. regulation vs including overtime, 'action' rules on postponements) so lines must be mapped to the Kalshi rule before comparison, and the timestamp of the line matters.
m.external_lines.measurement: Capture timestamped lines per book; de-vig (power or Shin method) per market; map to the Kalshi contract's rule (regulation vs full game, push handling); compute Kalshi minus consensus and closing-line value relative to the latest pregame consensus.

m.fees.label: Fee schedule and maker/taker rules in force
m.fees.mechanism: Fees reduce realized edge and depend on price level, so the break-even probability differs by rung and by maker/taker role.
m.fees.rationale: Because the fee is price-dependent, a fixed edge in cents is worth less near 50 than at the tails or vice versa depending on schedule; a model signal must clear fee-adjusted breakeven, not raw midpoint difference. Subtle: fee schedules change over time and by market type, so the version in force at trade time must be used.
m.fees.measurement: Version the fee formula from Kalshi's published fee schedule; compute breakeven probability per price and role; subtract from model edge before any threshold decision.
free_sources: Kalshi fee schedule PDF/help center (kalshi.com/fee-schedule) and /exchange/schedule API

m.lifecycle.label: Open/close/halt/postponement lifecycle events
m.lifecycle.mechanism: Market open, close, halts and postponement events determine when information can be traded on and which pregame snapshot is the last valid one.
m.lifecycle.rationale: Markets may close at scheduled start, on delay, or be extended; late-news windows (confirmed lineup/goalie) may fall before or after the close. Subtle: delayed or postponed games shift the effective decision time and can leave stale quotes, which also mislabels the 'closing' price used for CLV.
m.lifecycle.measurement: Record open_time, close_time, status transitions, and actual first pitch/puck drop from the league feed; define the last-valid-pregame timestamp as min(close_time, actual start); flag delayed/postponed games.

m.strike_hit_rates.label: Historical realized frequency by strike/rung per family (from settlements)
m.strike_hit_rates.mechanism: Realized frequency by rung gives the unconditional base rate that every conditional model must beat, and reveals persistent biases in how thresholds are set.
m.strike_hit_rates.rationale: Markets often over- or under-price specific rung shapes (round-number thresholds, longshot tails). Base rates by rung, season, venue and liquidity tier reveal where the market is calibrated and where it is not. Subtle: settled history is selection-biased by which strikes Kalshi chose to list, so rates are conditional on being listed.
m.strike_hit_rates.measurement: From settled markets compute hit rate by family x strike x price bucket with confidence intervals; compare to implied price; keep season and rule-version splits.

m.trade_tape.label: Executed trades (price, size, taker side, time) for slippage and flow
m.trade_tape.mechanism: Executed trades reveal where size actually transacted, the taker side, and the speed at which price reacts to news.
m.trade_tape.rationale: Trade flow around lineup/goalie/pitcher confirmation shows how quickly information is incorporated; sustained one-sided taker flow can indicate informed trading. Subtle: only executed prints are observable, resting orders are not, so slippage estimates from the tape understate the cost of crossing a thin book.
m.trade_tape.measurement: Pull trades per ticker with timestamps; compute signed volume (taker side), VWAP in windows around news timestamps, post-trade price drift as an informed-flow proxy; estimate slippage by size bucket.

nhl.season_sim_distribution.label: Season simulation distribution (points, playoffs, division)
nhl.season_sim_distribution.mechanism: Season markets are tails of an 82-game simulation including overtime-point rules and injury uncertainty.
nhl.season_sim_distribution.rationale: NHL standings points are 2-1-0 with overtime-loss points, so points markets need a bivariate result model, not just win probability. Subtle: goalie injuries and back-to-back starts alter win probability game by game.
nhl.season_sim_distribution.measurement: Monte Carlo from own expected-goals ratings with goalie-state uncertainty, regulation/overtime split and wildcard tiebreakers; report points and playoff distributions.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick / Moneypuck public tables

nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.label: Late-game equalizer and empty-net hazard by team and coach
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.mechanism: Converts a one-goal late deficit into tie or two-goal-loss outcomes using 6v5 rates and the coach's pull time.
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.rationale: The existing empty_net input is a single bucket for 'pulled-goalie timing'; for tie probability the two competing outcomes of a pull (equalizer vs empty-net goal against) and their dependence on pull time are what move the diagonal of the score distribution. Pull time has drifted earlier league-wide and differs by coach.
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.measurement: From play-by-play, for every regular-season and playoff game since 2015-16 find states with the trailing team down exactly one goal and the goalie pulled; per team-coach compute (a) median pull time in seconds remaining, (b) equalizer rate = goals for per 60 minutes of 6v5 time, (c) empty-net goals against per 60 of 6v5 time. Shrink each to league with k=20 pulls, weight seasons with 2-year half-life, and reset on a coaching change. Output pregame P(equalizer | trailing by 1 at T-3:00) and P(EN | trailing by 1) per team pair.

nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.label: [Playoff-only, dormant for KXNHLOT] 5v5 sudden-death overtime goal hazard (playoff OT)
nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.mechanism: Hazard of a goal per 20-minute playoff overtime period at 5v5 given tied score, fatigue and style.
nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.rationale: Playoff overtime is 5v5 sudden death in 20-minute periods, not the 3v3 of the regular season, so the existing 3v3 rate does not transfer; double-OT markets depend on the first period producing no goal, which has a different hazard than 60-minute rates imply.
nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.measurement: Pool all playoff OT minutes since 2005-06 (about 450 games) at 5v5 and compute the goal rate per 60 for tied score; model hazard h(t) = h0 x tied-game 5v5 multiplier x team-pair factor, where the team-pair factor is the geometric mean of both teams' tied 5v5 xG rate shrunk to league with k=500 minutes. Fatigue multiplier estimated from period index (OT1 vs OT2) and rest differential. P(no goal in OT1) = exp(-h x 20/60). Do not use regular-season 3v3 minutes.

sources.name: NHL web API (api-web.nhle.com play-by-play, boxscore, schedule, standings, shiftcharts)

nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.label: [Playoff-only, dormant until KXNHL2OT/KXNHLSERIESOT list markets] Within-series dependence of overtime occurrence
nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.mechanism: Intraclass correlation of per-game tie indicators within the same playoff series.
nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.rationale: Games in one series share goalies, coaches and defensive structure, so OT counts are overdispersed relative to independent Bernoulli; a binomial series-OT price is too thin-tailed.
nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.measurement: Fit a beta-binomial to the count of games reaching OT in each historical playoff series (2005-06 onward, series lengths 4-7 handled by conditioning on length), estimate overdispersion rho; then per series set p_game = reg_tie_model pregame tie probability and apply rho to get the pmf of OT-game count. Update rho with a prior of 0.05 and k=40 series.

nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.label: Tied-game closing posture (late risk aversion when a point is banked)
nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.mechanism: Change in late 5v5 attempt share and danger in tied games relative to earlier tied-game play.
nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.rationale: A tied third period guarantees a standings point, which may lower risk-taking; if present it raises P(OT) above what 60-minute rates give. It is a hypothesis to measure, not an assumed effect.
nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.measurement: For each team and season compute shot-attempt share and high-danger attempts per 60 at 5v5 in the final 5:00 of regulation when the score is tied, minus the same team's rate in minutes 40:00-55:00 when tied; shrink to league with k=60 tied-late minutes and report per-team posture index; interact with standings leverage (points pct within 4 of a cutoff). Add the minimum of two teams' indices as the pair posture.

nhl.ratings_script_distribution.label: Ratings-only pregame score-path distribution (lead/trail/tied time shares and entering-state matrix)
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.mechanism: Simulated from team goal rates alone, the distribution of score states by period and the share of 60 minutes spent leading, trailing or tied shapes shot volume, star deployment, pull timing and empty-net goals without ever touching a price.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.rationale: The catalog nhl.game_script_prob derives its win probability from ratings AND the market line, so it is contaminated by the benchmark. This replacement is built only from market-free inputs: it keeps the useful scenario-probability content (conditional state mixtures, not a single win probability) while leaving the market line as a comparison target. The subtle point is that the object needed is a distribution over states, not one number.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.measurement: For each team, set expected 5v5 and special-teams goal rates for the game as lambda_i = league mean x (attack_i x defence_j adjusted xG ratings, shrunk with prior_to_current_blend where available, or ratings built from score-adjusted xGF/xGA per 60 over a 40-game EWMA with 20-game half-life shrunk 25 games toward league mean) x goalie factor (confirmed or probability-weighted starter GSAx per 60 shrunk 1000 shots) plus a home-ice constant estimated from the last 5 seasons. Simulate 20000 games with a negative-binomial goal process with the fitted dispersion, event times drawn from a time-varying rate with score effects, a pull rule at the coach-specific trailing time, and OT 3v3 play. Output per game: P(lead/tied/trail) entering each period, expected minutes in each score state, P(margin>=2 entering the third), and expected 6v5 minutes per team. As-of timestamp: latest ratings and confirmed or probabilistic starter before puck drop; never include any sportsbook or Kalshi price.

nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.label: Settlement-adjusted final-margin distribution (regulation, OT, shootout, empty net)
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.mechanism: Maps team goal-rate parameters to the full pmf of final margin under official scoring rules.
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.rationale: Moneyline, spread and regulation-winner contracts read different functionals of one distribution; building each from its own ad hoc model creates inconsistent prices. The pmf must apply: regulation bivariate counts, late empty-net transitions, an OT goal as a one-goal margin, and a shootout as a one-goal margin with a near-even winner.
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.measurement: Simulate or enumerate: regulation (H, A) from fitted bivariate overdispersed counts at 55:00 plus a final-5-minute jump process using team pull-time and 6v5 rates; if tied at 60:00 draw OT with 3v3 goal hazard (regular season) giving +/-1 margin, else shootout winner with p = 0.5 + shrunk team SO talent (k=60 attempts) giving +/-1. Output P(margin >= m) for m=1..6 per team and P(regulation tie). Validate by reproducing the league margin histogram (about 25 percent one-goal games) per season.

nhl.lineup_impact_delta.label: Lineup impact delta from player value model (skater and goalie)
nhl.lineup_impact_delta.mechanism: Converts who is in or out into a change in expected goal difference using per-player impact estimates.
nhl.lineup_impact_delta.rationale: Injury status flags tell who is missing but not what it costs; a top-pair defenceman, a first-line centre and a starting goalie have different values, and replacements play different minutes. The cost must be computed from minutes redistributed times impact difference.
nhl.lineup_impact_delta.measurement: Skater impact I_s = ridge RAPM xG/60 at 5v5 (3 seasons, half-life 1.5 seasons, shrunk to position mean) plus PP/PK impact per special-teams minute. Lineup value V(L) = sum over skaters of proj TOI per game (hours) x I_s in each state + goalie term (GSAx per 1000 shots shrunk k=2000, x expected opponent shots faced /1000). Delta = V(published lineup) minus V(base lineup = last 10 games' modal lineup), in goals per game. Use only lineups published before the as-of time; store vintages.

nhl.prior_to_current_blend.label: Preseason prior blend weight by games played
nhl.prior_to_current_blend.mechanism: Weights current-season data against a preseason prior as a function of sample size.
nhl.prior_to_current_blend.rationale: At this point in the season (early November) a team has played about 12-15 games; xG share has a stabilisation point of several dozen games, so raw current xG overstates differences and ignores roster turnover.
nhl.prior_to_current_blend.measurement: Prior = last two seasons' score-adjusted rating (weights 0.6/0.4) adjusted by net roster change (minutes-weighted impact of arrivals minus departures) and age curve; posterior = (n x current + k x prior)/(n + k) with k in the 25-40 games range fit by minimising out-of-sample log loss of game result; recompute weekly. Report posterior sd to the simulator.
free_sources: Own computation from MoneyPuck/Natural Stat Trick history

nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.label: Power-play termination and unit-time split
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.mechanism: Expected PP goals per penalty given that a minor ends on a goal and PP1/PP2 share the clock.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.rationale: PP time is not additive: a two-minute minor ends when the power-play team scores, so goals per PP are concave in minutes, and the first unit plays roughly the first 60-80 seconds, so PP1 production dominates short power plays. Using PP time x rate overstates multi-goal PP games and misallocates credit among players.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.measurement: From play-by-play, for each team and season compute: (a) conversion per PP opportunity (minor penalties only, excluding coincident and 4v4 states), (b) hazard of a PP goal as a function of elapsed PP seconds in 15-second bins, (c) PP1 share of PP time as a function of elapsed seconds, (d) PP goal share by unit. Shrink team hazard to league with k=150 PP opportunities and 2-season half-life. Expected PP goals = sum over expected penalties of integral hazard x survival; keep major and double-minor cases separate.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play with penalty events and situationCode

nhl.pair_attempt_volume.label: Pair attempt-volume composite (log-additive team tempo model)
nhl.pair_attempt_volume.mechanism: Expected combined attempts from offence-for and defence-against terms fit jointly.
nhl.pair_attempt_volume.rationale: Combined pace is not the average of the two teams' season paces: each team's attempts depend on its own offence and the opponent's suppression and on score effects, and the two teams' counts are correlated through game state. A pair composite avoids double counting.
nhl.pair_attempt_volume.measurement: Fit a Poisson regression of 5v5 attempts per 60 for each team-game: log E = mu + off_team + def_opp + home + score-state adjustment, with ridge penalty and 2-season half-life; game attempts = sum of both teams' predictions x projected 5v5 minutes (60 minus expected PP/PK minutes). Add pair random effect with variance estimated from residual covariance. Evaluate pace-weighted xG, not raw attempts, when converting to goals.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick attempts by team-game

nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.label: Opponent shots-on-goal-for rate by strength state, score adjusted
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.mechanism: Opponent's own shot-on-goal generation per 60 at EV and on the power play.
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.rationale: The draft carries opponent xG (a quality measure) and the defence's suppression, but saves count shots on goal, so the opponent's volume of on-target shots, separate from danger, is the first-order driver. xG weights shots by quality and understates the effect of low-danger volume teams.
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.measurement: Per team compute SOG for per 60 at 5v5 (score-and-venue adjusted via regression of SOG rate on score differential bins) and at 5v4, with 2-season half-life 40 games and shrink to league with k=15 games; project game SOG faced = EV_rate_opp x defence_adjustment x projected EV minutes + PP_rate_opp x projected PP minutes. Use log-additive combination with opponent defence SOG-against: log E = mu + off_opp + def_team.

raw_data: team-game SOG for and against by strength state

nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.label: Goalie minutes-in-net distribution (entry, pull and overtime)
nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.mechanism: Probability distribution of the named goalie's exposure in minutes and the relief goalie's partial exposure.
nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.rationale: The settlement rule makes exposure part of the contract: no entry -> fair-price, entry -> own saves only. Exposure is neither 60 nor zero; pulls and relief appearances create a mass at partial minutes. This is a distribution, not a scalar start probability.
nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.measurement: From box scores since 2015-16 build for each goalie the empirical pmf of minutes, conditional on starting: P(pulled before 40:00), P(pulled in 40-55), P(full + OT). Shrink each goalie's pull rate to team-coach and league rates with k=25 starts; make pull hazard depend on goals allowed in the first period (0, 1, 2, 3+). Combine with P(start | rest, schedule, report) from the forecast to get an overall mixture, and mark the no-start component as fair-price (excluded from the YES/NO distribution).

nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.label: Arena-level SOG recording factor

nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.rationale: Official scorers record SOG; arenas can differ systematically, but the size for SOG is smaller and less certain than for hits or giveaways. A measured factor lets the model decide whether venue matters rather than assuming it.
nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.measurement: Fit a mixed model log(SOG_game) = team offence + team defence + arena effect + season, using all games from 2015-16 on, with the arena random effect shrunk with prior sd 0.03; always use the shrunk posterior mean for every arena (never a significance cutoff, which would bias the retained estimates upward). nhl.ot_shot_exposure.label: Overtime shot exposure given regulation tie probability
nhl.ot_shot_exposure.mechanism: Expected extra shots faced in overtime weighted by probability of a tie.
nhl.ot_shot_exposure.rationale: Overtime is a 3v3 period with high shot density that can add several shots to a goalie's count; its expected contribution is P(OT) times shots per OT period, which can push a goalie across a threshold. It enters only if the contract counts OT, which is not stated.
nhl.ot_shot_exposure.measurement: E[saves by goalie G in OT] = P(tie after 60) x E[shots faced by G in OT | no earlier stop], with shots per 3v3 minute per team from 2015-16 on (pooled mean/sd, team adjustments shrunk k=200 OT minutes) and OT length = min(5, time to first goal) where the goal hazard per shot is 1-save probability of the goalies; estimate by simulation or closed form E[shots] = lambda_shots x E[min(T,5)]; shootout saves counted only if the contract counts shootout attempts. Playoff OT: 20-minute periods at 5v5 hazard.

nhl.period_entry_state_matrix.label: Entering-period score-state distribution and state-conditional rates
nhl.period_entry_state_matrix.mechanism: pmf of the score margin entering periods two and three together with team rates conditional on margin.
nhl.period_entry_state_matrix.rationale: The pregame win probability does not give the distribution of the margin at 20:00 and 40:00, and period-three scoring depends on that margin through score effects. Markets for later periods are mixtures that cannot be priced from unconditional period rates.
nhl.period_entry_state_matrix.measurement: From period-by-period history compute for each team the empirical transition matrix of margin after one and two periods, shrunk to a model-based matrix from the bivariate period count model (prior strength 30 games); compute rates of goals and SOG for and against per period conditional on entering margin in {-2,-1,0,+1,+2 or more} with k=40 team-period minutes shrinkage; output the expected rate in period p as a mixture sum over margins of P(margin) x rate(margin). nhl.period_penalty_intensity_balance.label: Period-level penalty intensity and within-game balancing
nhl.period_penalty_intensity_balance.mechanism: Distribution of the number of minors per period and the tendency to even out calls against the earlier imbalance.
nhl.period_penalty_intensity_balance.rationale: Because one power play can decide a 20-minute period, the count distribution and its dependence on earlier calls matter more here than in full-game markets. Referee balancing is a mechanism where penalties against a team become less likely after the opponent has received more.
nhl.period_penalty_intensity_balance.measurement: From play-by-play compute for each period the pmf of minors called on each team; estimate a logit/Poisson regression of the next penalty on cumulative penalty differential with period fixed effects, using crew effects as random intercept with prior sd 0.1; shrink team taken/drawn rates with k=300 minutes. Forecast per period: expected minors for each side as a function of crew, teams and period; simulate balancing within the game for periods two and three.

nhl.period_pair_count_model.label: Period-level bivariate count model with cross-period dependence
nhl.period_pair_count_model.mechanism: Joint pmf of the two teams' goals in a period with period-specific dispersion, correlation and zero mass.
nhl.period_pair_count_model.rationale: The full-game dispersion parameter cannot be reused for a 20-minute window where zero mass and tie probability are driven by different variances; moreover periods within a game are dependent through game total and score effects.
nhl.period_pair_count_model.measurement: Fit a bivariate negative-binomial or Poisson-mixture model with parameters (mu_home, mu_away, dispersion, correlation) per period index using all games since 2010-11, with covariates team strength and PP expectations; estimate cross-period dependence by a shared game random effect (variance parameter) and a score-effect term; validate on frequency of 0-0, ties and margins of two or more in each period; recalibrate each season.
