nhl.period_home_ice_split.label: Home-ice and last-change effect by period (home flag, period-specific home goal share)
nhl.period_home_ice_split.mechanism: The home team gets last change at every stoppage and the home crowd and scorer effects are modest and constant in size, but their effect on a 20-minute winner or spread contract differs by period because deployment, score state and the second-period long change interact with the home bench position.
nhl.period_home_ice_split.rationale: Period winner and spread contracts are team-versus-team, so a small constant home edge shifts every tie, win and rung probability and is not captured by team ratings alone. A single full-game home constant mis-scales the period effect: it is most visible in match-ups of the first period when coaches can pick the matchup, and it is compressed in the third by score effects. Reviewers noted no home input existed in this record.
nhl.period_home_ice_split.measurement: From team-period goals and 5v5 xG since 2015-16 fit: goal differential in period p = b_s x (strength difference) + h_p x home + season FE. Shrink h_p to pooled home edge h with h_p ~ N(h, (0.5*|h|)^2) fitted by empirical Bayes; fit separately for goals and for 5v5 xG; refresh once per season from games dated before the target date. Last-change is not estimated team-by-team; report h_2 minus mean(h_1,h_3) as league-level long-change effect.

nhl.rest_fatigue_period_profile.label: Rest and back-to-back fatigue profile by period (and its backup-goalie channel)
nhl.rest_fatigue_period_profile.mechanism: A team on the second night of a back-to-back or after long travel plays a higher share of games with a backup goalie, which changes the first-period goal rate, and may fade late in the game, so the rest effect is not constant across periods.
nhl.rest_fatigue_period_profile.rationale: Reviewers argued rest was ignored because the record treated it as a full-game constant. The channel that is certain is goalie identity (backup starts concentrate on back-to-backs), which hits period one; the possible skater fatigue channel would show up as a later-period fade and is unproven. The input keeps the two channels separate so that the certain one is not diluted by the uncertain one.
nhl.rest_fatigue_period_profile.measurement: For every team-game since 2015-16 compute rest days, back-to-back second-night flag and time-zone miles travelled; regress period goal differential and period xG differential on rest differential interacted with period (3 coefficients), with team strength and home controls and season fixed effects. Add the backup-start probability from the goalie start forecast as a separate covariate so the fatigue term is estimated net of goalie identity. Shrink period coefficients to the pooled rest effect with a prior sd of one third of the pooled estimate. As-of: schedule is known weeks ahead, goalie confirmation arrives on game day.

nhl.ipp_by_state.label: Individual points percentage by strength state (points per on-ice goal for)
nhl.ipp_by_state.mechanism: Share of team goals scored while on ice on which the player is credited with a goal or assist.
nhl.ipp_by_state.rationale: Points are credited on team goals, so expected points equal on-ice goals for times the share of those on which the skater is credited; this share is far more stable than assists per game and is role dependent (forwards on scoring lines high, defencemen lower, PP1 shooters very high).
nhl.ipp_by_state.measurement: For each skater and strength state (EV, PP) compute IPP = (goals + assists) / on-ice goals for, using 3 seasons weighted by 0.5/0.3/0.2 and shrunk to position-and-role priors with k=25 on-ice goals; separate primary and secondary assist components, shrinking secondary toward position mean with k=60; apply per-60 conversion: expected points per game = sum over states of (on-ice GF/60 x state TOI/60 x IPP_state).

nhl.onice_xgf_per60.label: On-ice expected goals for per 60 by strength state (RAPM-adjusted)
nhl.onice_xgf_per60.mechanism: Team scoring chances created while the player is on ice, adjusted for teammates, opponents and zone starts.
nhl.onice_xgf_per60.rationale: Individual xG measures only the shooter's own attempts but points depend on all chances the player's line creates; a forward on a top line has points even when he does not shoot much. Linemate_quality is a single-label proxy; a regularised on-ice xGF rate is the measurable form.
nhl.onice_xgf_per60.measurement: Estimate per-skater on-ice xGF per 60 at 5v5 and on the PP with ridge regression on shift data (3-season window, half-life 1.5 seasons, shrink toward position mean with prior sd chosen by cross-validation) controlling for teammates, opponents, zone starts and score state. Projected on-ice xGF for the game uses projected linemates (from lines input) and is multiplied by the opposing team's defence factor and the opposing goalie factor.

nhl.first_goal_scorer_share.label: First-goal scorer share and team first-goal probability
nhl.first_goal_scorer_share.mechanism: Probability that the player scores the game's first goal given team-level first-goal race and his share within the scoring line.
nhl.first_goal_scorer_share.rationale: The first-goalscorer contract is a competing-risk race: either team scores first, and given that the scorer is drawn from the players on ice at that moment weighted by shot share. Early-game deployment and early power plays raise top-line and PP1 chances relative to full-game share.
nhl.first_goal_scorer_share.measurement: P(player p scores team's first goal in game) = P(team scores first or at all) x s_p, where s_p = (first-goals by p over last 3 seasons, weighted 0.5/0.3/0.2) shrunk toward ixG share (p's ixG per game / sum of team skater ixG per game) with prior weight 40 team first goals. P(team scores first) from per-team hazard h(t) over 60 minutes (opposing starter GSAx adjusted) plus OT. Final: P(first goal of game) = P(team first) x s_p x 1[plays]; exclude shootout goals; settle on whichever of the game's goals comes first by clock. Use only games before as-of date.

nhl.skater_en_usage.label: Skater extra-attacker and empty-net usage share

nhl.early_window_goal_rate.label: Early-window (first 10:00 of period one) team goal hazard for the pair
nhl.early_window_goal_rate.mechanism: The event is that either team scores in the first 10 minutes, so it depends on the two teams scoring hazards in the opening minutes at 5v5 and on early power plays, with the opposing goalie and the opening lines setting the level.
nhl.early_window_goal_rate.rationale: KXNHLF10G has no player in it: the probability is one minus the chance that both teams are held scoreless for 10 minutes. Opening-period scoring rates differ from full-game rates (fresh goalies, coach matchups, fewer penalties early), so the full-game goal rate scaled by 10/60 is biased. The tail event of an early power play (penalty in the first minutes) adds a lumpy extra hazard.
nhl.early_window_goal_rate.measurement: For each team compute goals for and against per 60 in minutes 0:00-9:59 of period one at 5v5 and on the power play since 2018-19 (half-life 60 games, shrunk 30 games to league), adjust for the confirmed opposing goalie GSAx per 60 shrunk 1000 shots, estimate the early-penalty rate per team (penalties drawn and taken in the window) and combine: lambda_window = sum over teams of (5v5 hazard x minutes at 5v5 + PP hazard x expected PP minutes in window); P(YES) = 1 - NB zero mass with fitted dispersion. Never use a price. As-of: starting goalies confirmed pregame, otherwise a mixture.

nhl.skater_ot_3v3_exposure.label: Skater overtime 3v3 exposure and point rate
nhl.skater_ot_3v3_exposure.mechanism: Overtime adds a short 3v3 stretch only in games tied after 60 minutes, where stars play very heavy minutes and points come at a much higher rate per minute than at 5v5.

nhl.games_played_hazard.label: Games-played hazard (injury, rest and load management)
nhl.games_played_hazard.mechanism: Distribution of games missed for a player over the season given age, position, injury history and team situation.
nhl.games_played_hazard.rationale: A season total is capped by games played; a 60-goal pace needs about 78-82 games, so the left tail from injuries is the main downside. A distribution (not an expected value) is needed because missing a month removes the contract's chances.

nhl.player_season_points_projection.label: Player season points projection (rate x games-played distribution)
nhl.player_season_points_projection.mechanism: A season points threshold is reached by points already banked plus per-game production on the games still to be played, so the outcome is the sum of a rate (role, time on ice, power-play share, on-ice chance creation and credit share) and an opportunity count (games played).
nhl.player_season_points_projection.rationale: Season-points contracts such as a 110+ points threshold for a defenceman sit in the extreme tail of a rate times games distribution, so both the central rate and its dispersion matter. Rate comes from the same components as the single-game record (role, power-play time, on-ice xGF, individual points percentage); games remaining comes from the games-played hazard. The subtle part is that role changes (power-play unit, line, injuries to teammates) move the rate level for the rest of the season.
nhl.player_season_points_projection.measurement: Points to date P0 plus the sum over remaining games g of expected points per game, where per-game expected points = sum over strength states of (on-ice goals-for per 60 x projected state time on ice per 60 x individual points percentage in that state), using 3 seasons weighted 0.5/0.3/0.2 with half-life 1.5 seasons, shrunk to position-and-role priors (k=25 on-ice goals) and updated for the current season by a gamma-Poisson rate posterior; multiply by the pmf of games remaining from nhl.games_played_hazard; simulate 20000 seasons with negative-binomial per-game dispersion fitted on player-seasons of comparable rate; report P(total >= threshold). As-of: all games before the contract date, with the current power-play unit and line assignment from the latest lineup report.

nhl.sog_share_on_ice.label: Skater share of team shots on goal while on ice, by strength state

nhl.teammate_point_co_credit.label: Teammate point co-credit rate
nhl.teammate_point_co_credit.mechanism: Probability that a goal on which player A earns a point also gives player B a point, by strength state.
nhl.teammate_point_co_credit.rationale: Two linemates are positively correlated in points because the same goal credits both; this co-credit structure is a source of dependence beyond shared script and reduces the variance of D for teammate pairs.
nhl.teammate_point_co_credit.measurement: From goal events compute for each ordered teammate pair the share of A's points that came on goals where B also earned a point, per strength state, over three seasons with k=30 shared points shrinkage to position-line priors; summarise in a pair-level co-credit coefficient used in the joint count model as the shared-goal Poisson component.
raw_data: goal events with scorer and assisters

nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.label: Goal-credit allocation kernel (probability each skater scores or assists on a team goal)
nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.mechanism: Probability that a skater is credited with the goal, primary or secondary assist, conditional on a team goal at a given strength state and lineup.
nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.rationale: A combo mixing team and player legs needs one coherent mechanism linking team goals to individual stats; a kernel based on on-ice shares and credit shares guarantees consistency and the cap of one goal and two assists per team goal.
nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.measurement: For each skater and strength state (EV, PP, EN) compute: P(on ice | team goal) = team goals scored while on ice / team goals in the state, and P(credit type | on ice, goal) from three seasons of goal events (shrunk to position/line priors with k=30 goals); build for the projected lineup a kernel K[skater, role(goal, A1, A2)] with columns summing to 1 for goals, and at most two assists per goal; in simulation draw each goal's state, then allocate credit by K. Recalibrate so that simulated team assists per goal match league and team averages.

nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.label: Joint lineup scenario tree (goalies and key skaters)
nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.mechanism: Joint probability over starter goalie for each team and the status of the three or four most influential skaters.
nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.rationale: A single leg's availability probability is not enough: several legs move at once on the same news, and the joint probability of states (e.g., backup in net and star out) is not the product of marginal probabilities because of shared causes such as back-to-backs.
nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.measurement: Define for each team K key players (starting goalie plus top-4 skaters by impact) and enumerate states; estimate P(state) from the team's historical patterns: goalie rotation (consecutive-start rules, back-to-back), injury reports and morning skate evidence; assume independence beyond shared schedule factors unless data show otherwise; limit leaves to those with probability above 1 percent and merge the rest; store each state with its decision-time vintage.

nhl.copula_tail_dependence.label: Tail dependence between leg pairs (copula parameters by pair type)
nhl.copula_tail_dependence.mechanism: Dependence in the joint upper and lower tails of leg pairs beyond linear correlation.
nhl.copula_tail_dependence.rationale: Hockey legs show stronger dependence in the tails than in the centre: blowout games produce high totals, large margins and many points together. A Gaussian copula with a pooled correlation underprices joint tail events and overprices central ones.
nhl.copula_tail_dependence.measurement: For each pair type (win-total, win-player points, total-player points, goalie saves-total, total-team total) compute from five seasons of game logs the empirical conditional exceedance chi(u) = P(U>u, V>u)/(1-u) at u = 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 using rank transforms with discrete tie handling; fit Gaussian, Student-t and Clayton copulas by maximum likelihood on the pseudo-observations and choose by out-of-sample joint log-likelihood; shrink pair-type parameters with k=400 games.

nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.label: Parlay leg-void payoff map
nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.mechanism: Lookup table mapping each combination of leg statuses (win, lose, void-at-fair-price) to the contract payoff under the rules in force.
nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.rationale: The fair price depends on what happens to the combo when a leg voids: collapse to fair price, drop the leg, or lose. The same probabilities give different prices under different maps, and none is observed in the sampled rules.
nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.measurement: From the rules text of each combo series build a table payoff(status vector); where text is missing mark the map as unknown and carry multiple candidate maps (drop-leg, fair-price collapse, lose) with prior weights; compute price under each candidate and report the range; version by rules_text vintage so that changes are visible.

nhl.leg_logical_relations.label: Leg logical-relations map (implications, exclusions, shared ladders)
nhl.leg_logical_relations.mechanism: Deterministic implications and exclusions among legs of the same game.
nhl.leg_logical_relations.rationale: Nested rungs and mutually exclusive outcomes fix part of the joint probability exactly: points 2+ implies points 1+, a team win excludes the opponent win, the spread leg implies the win leg. A correlation model that ignores this can assign probability to impossible combinations.
nhl.leg_logical_relations.measurement: Enumerate for each pair of legs the logical relation under the game's settlement rules (including shootout credit, third-period OT exclusion, and nested player ladders) and store as a matrix of {implies, excludes, independent-by-construction, free}; the simulator rejects draws violating relations and the pricing uses P(A and B) = P(A) for implied and 0 for excluded.

nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.label: Team rating posterior uncertainty and in-season drift
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.mechanism: Posterior standard deviation of each team's strength and its random-walk drift per game.
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.rationale: A season or title simulation using point ratings is overconfident: the spread of true strengths and the error of the estimate both matter, and title probability is convex in rating so uncertainty raises the probability of mid-tier teams. Early-season data are noisy.
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.measurement: Fit a state-space model: rating_t = rating_{t-1} + eta (sd 0.02 goals/game per game, estimated by out-of-sample likelihood), observation = score-adjusted xG differential and goal differential with measurement sd from game-level residuals; initialise with preseason prior (sd 0.25 goals/game). Output posterior mean and sd per team per day; draw ratings from the posterior in each simulation run. Re-estimate drift variance each season.
free_sources: Own computation from MoneyPuck/Natural Stat Trick game data
raw_data: game xG and goals by team

nhl.loser_point_rate.label: Loser-point and overtime-resolution rate by team
nhl.loser_point_rate.mechanism: Share of a team's games decided after regulation and its conditional win share.
nhl.loser_point_rate.rationale: Standings points include a point for an overtime or shootout loss, so two teams with equal win rates can differ in points by their extra-time frequency; regulation-win tiebreaks also depend on how often games are decided in regulation.
nhl.loser_point_rate.measurement: Per team and season compute: P(game goes beyond regulation) shrunk to league with k=30 games and 2-season weights; P(win | beyond regulation) shrunk to 0.5 with k=40 games (shootout/OT skill slight); regulation win rate from regulation results. Points per game = 2 x P(reg win) + 2 x P(extra) x p_win_extra + 1 x P(extra) x (1 - p_win_extra). Record regulation wins and ROW separately for tiebreak tracking.

nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.label: Playoff bracket path difficulty by seed and division
nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.mechanism: Distribution of first and second round opponents and home-ice status given the final seed.
nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.rationale: The bracket pairs division winners with wild cards and keeps divisional paths, so equal-strength teams have different Cup and conference probabilities depending on their division and seed; the path must be simulated from standings.
nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.measurement: For each simulated final standings compute the bracket (3 per division plus 2 wild cards; division winner with better record faces the lower wild card) and the opponent set per round; record probabilities by team of facing each opponent and of home-ice in each series; use for series win recursion with rating uncertainty draws. Validate that simulated seed frequencies match historical qualifier frequencies by points.

nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.label: Cap flexibility and deadline additions capacity
nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.mechanism: Cap space, long-term injured reserve relief and tradable assets that allow a team to add or replace players before the deadline.
nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.rationale: A team's rating at the playoffs differs from today's rating through deadline moves and injury replacement; teams with cap room and assets can improve, which shifts long-horizon probabilities and is partially public.
nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.measurement: At each date t before the trade deadline compute per team: deadline space = cap ceiling minus current cap hit plus LTIR relief, times (days remaining after deadline-eligible acquisition / 186 season days) as accrued-cap fraction; count of own first-round picks held in the next two drafts; capacity = accrued space. Calibrate on 2015-16 onward: regress the acquisition indicator (contending team adds a skater with 3-season RAPM xG/60 above team median) on capacity, picks held, and points pct rank; shrink coefficients to zero with ridge chosen by leave-one-season-out CV. Snapshot daily; use only data timestamped before t.

nhl.series_goalie_volatility.label: Series-level goaltending volatility beyond binomial
nhl.series_goalie_volatility.mechanism: Extra variance of a series' save percentage and goal differential beyond a Bernoulli game model.
nhl.series_goalie_volatility.rationale: A best-of-seven series with fixed team ratings is binomial, but goalie performance autocorrelates within a series, producing a heavier-tailed distribution of series outcomes and more upsets than a constant p model gives.
nhl.series_goalie_volatility.measurement: From playoff series 2005-06 onward compute the series-level excess variance of goalie save percentage over binomial given shots faced; estimate intra-series correlation of single-game goalie GSAx; add a random effect on the winner's per-game p with sd estimated by maximum likelihood on series results; use in the series recursion. Shrink to league average with k=60 series.

nhl.award_vote_share_model.label: Award vote-share model (electorate-specific)
nhl.award_vote_share_model.mechanism: Historical multinomial-logit model of vote shares for each award using production, team success, position and narrative variables.
nhl.award_vote_share_model.rationale: Hart, Norris and Calder are voted by writers and Vezina by general managers; each electorate rewards different features (points, team rank, goalie wins, shutouts, GSAx), so a single player-quality model does not map to voting outcomes.
nhl.award_vote_share_model.measurement: For each award collect the last 20 seasons' finalists and vote shares; regress log vote share on points per game, goals, team points percentage, games played, position and for goalies wins, save percentage and shutouts; fit multinomial logit with season fixed effects and shrinkage; apply to the projected end-of-season stat line distribution from simulations; output win probability by candidate with draw uncertainty; update with finalists and ballot dates. Source caveat (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the Ted Lindsay Award): full vote shares are not known to be published for player-voted awards (only finalists and the winner), so where shares are missing fit a conditional-logit on winner-among-finalists instead of a share regression; with only a few dozen finalists per award use at most 4 covariates and strong shrinkage. Coach branch (Jack Adams, NHL Broadcasters' Association electorate, 5-3-1 ballot, individual ballots unpublished): a separate coach-level conditional logit over all ~32 head coaches on nhl.coach_expectation_delta (final delta, change versus prior-season delta, first-year flag) as specified in that input; no player production covariates are used for it.
raw_data: award finalists, winners and published vote points by season

nhl.award_eligibility_tiebreak_map.label: Award eligibility and tiebreak rules map
nhl.award_eligibility_tiebreak_map.mechanism: Eligibility conditions and tiebreak rules for each trophy and stat title.
nhl.award_eligibility_tiebreak_map.rationale: Rookie eligibility for the Calder, the way Art Ross and Rocket Richard ties are broken and Kalshi's 1/N payout interact: a tied or ineligible candidate changes the contract value even if production is identical.
nhl.award_eligibility_tiebreak_map.measurement: For each award list eligibility criteria (age, prior NHL games) and the league's tiebreak (fewer games played or more goals for Art Ross) from the NHL rulebook or award page; label each as verified or SOURCE_UNVERIFIED; map to Kalshi tie handling (1/N rounded down) and compute the probability of ties for counting leaders from simulation (points ties at the top occur in a minority of seasons).

nhl.goalie_award_projection.label: Goalie award projection (Vezina: GSAx rate, starts share, team context)
nhl.goalie_award_projection.mechanism: A goalie award is decided on saves above expectation and workload over the season, so the rest-of-season distribution is the goalie rate (GSAx per start, save percentage) times the number of starts he gets, with the team context that shapes the voters narrative.
nhl.goalie_award_projection.rationale: Vezina voters (general managers) reward workload and results; a goalie who splits starts cannot accumulate the case of a clear number one, and GSAx has low persistence so the projection must be shrunk heavily. The subtle part is starts share: it is set by the team depth chart and back-to-back schedule, not only by quality.
nhl.goalie_award_projection.measurement: Per goalie: GSAx per 60 over 3 seasons weighted 0.5/0.3/0.2 shrunk toward the league mean with k=1500 shots faced; projected remaining starts = games remaining x starts share (team goalie rotation pattern, back-to-back share, 2-season average, shrunk to 0.6 for a clear number one); simulate remaining GSAx as normal with sd from shots-faced noise; add wins and save percentage to date. As-of: all games before the contract date, current depth chart from the latest lineup reports.

nhl.rookie_role_pedigree.label: Rookie role and pedigree for Calder candidates
nhl.rookie_role_pedigree.mechanism: Calder voters pick the best first-year player, so the probability depends on eligibility, the rookie role actually obtained (line, power-play unit, minutes) and the production pace, with pedigree (draft position, prior league) setting early expectations.
nhl.rookie_role_pedigree.rationale: A rookie projection has little NHL history, so draft slot, junior or college scoring and age carry weight early while deployment (top-six, PP1, defence pair) dominates once games are played. Eligibility rules (age cap, prior games) also remove candidates, which makes the candidate set itself uncertain.
nhl.rookie_role_pedigree.measurement: Prior points per game = league translation factor for the prior league (CHL, NCAA, European) applied to the last season points per game, regressed 50 percent toward the draft-slot mean; posterior update with NHL games to date by gamma-Poisson with prior weight equal to 20 games; add role terms (share of team forward TOI, PP1 flag) and eligibility flag from the league rulebook; output rest-of-season points projection and eligibility probability. As-of: before each ballot deadline.

nhl.coach_expectation_delta.label: Coach expectation delta (results versus preseason projection, year-over-year change)
nhl.coach_expectation_delta.mechanism: Difference between realised points percentage and the preseason-projected value, plus year-over-year change and coaching tenure flags.
nhl.coach_expectation_delta.rationale: The Jack Adams Award is voted on who coached best relative to expectations, so what matters is the surprise, not the level; a team that finished first as expected earns less credit than one that jumped from the bottom. The expectation must be formed before the season to avoid hindsight bias.
nhl.coach_expectation_delta.measurement: P_exp = 0.6*points pct (season-1) + 0.4*points pct (season-2), plus nhl.prior_to_current_blend roster-change term (minutes-weighted 3-season RAPM of arrivals minus departures, per 82 games, converted at 0.015 pts pct per goal/60-game); computed in-house so no archived preseason projection is required. Delta_t = points pct to date (games before as-of date t) minus P_exp; SE = sqrt(p(1-p)/n_games_played). Final delta per simulation = (banked points + simulated rest-of-season points from nhl.team_season_points_distribution)/(2*82) minus P_exp. Jack Adams choice model (coach branch of nhl.award_vote_share_model): candidate set = every head coach who ran >=41 regular-season games of one team (about 32); U_c = b1*Delta_final + b2*(Delta_final - Delta_prev_season) + b3*first_year_with_team; P(win) = exp(U_c)/sum_j exp(U_j), averaged over simulations (a coach fired before the threshold drops out of that draw). Fit as a conditional logit on winners 2005-06 onward, augmented with a rank-ordered (exploded) logit on the NHLBA top-3 finish order from published 5-3-1 point totals; ridge penalty chosen by leave-one-season-out log loss; at most 3 covariates. Use only games before t.

nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.label: Draft lottery odds by final standing and ownership
nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.mechanism: Probability each team wins the top pick from the simulated final standings and the league lottery format.
nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.rationale: The first pick is not simply given to the worst team: the lottery format gives the worst team a limited chance and caps how far a team can move, so the distribution is flat over the bottom teams and depends on exact standings and on the number of draws.
nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.measurement: Simulate final standings from the ratings posterior (with points ties resolved by league rules), identify the 16 non-playoff teams, map rank to lottery combinations using the current published format (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for 2027) with ranges for odds of first pick and for the maximum movement allowed; combine with pick ownership to get P(team T holds the first pick) = sum over teams of P(team wins lottery) x ownership; output with the standings uncertainty.

nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.label: First-round pick ownership and protection conditions
nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.mechanism: Which team holds each first-round pick with its protections and conditionality.
nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.rationale: Traded picks, top-ten protections and conditional swaps change who benefits from a bad finish; a lottery winner that has traded its pick selects nothing, so ownership multiplies the lottery probability.
nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.measurement: Collect the first-round pick table for the draft year with owner, original team, protection (top-N, lottery), and conditions (swap rights), from PuckPedia/CapWages and official transaction records; version it by date; encode as owner(team) and conditional logic evaluated on the simulated standings; track changes after each trade.

nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.label: Prospect consensus ranking and selection agreement history
nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.mechanism: Consensus ordering of top prospects and the historical probability that the consensus choice is selected at each pick.
nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.rationale: The selecting team's choice follows a board that correlates strongly with public consensus at the very top, with more disagreement later; a clear gap between the first and second prospects makes the top-pick contract nearly a one-candidate event.
nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.measurement: Aggregate public rankings (NHL Central Scouting final list, Elite Prospects consensus, Bob McKenzie/TSN list, others) into a rank-averaged score, compute the gap between first and second; calibrate P(consensus #1 is selected first) from 15 drafts as a function of gap with a logistic fit; for later picks use rank deviation distributions; update with injuries and with team-specific needs flags.

nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.label: Player contract status and movement clauses
nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.mechanism: Contract expiry year, cap hit, no-trade or no-move clauses, arbitration and free-agent status for the named player.
nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.rationale: Destination markets are bounded by the contract: a player under a long contract with a no-movement clause can only move with consent, while a player on an expiring contract becomes a free agent on a known date; the same inputs determine whether any team can acquire him at all.
nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.measurement: For the player compile from cap sites: contract end year, AAV, NMC/NTC status and no-trade list if public, RFA/UFA status and arbitration rights, extension eligibility date, and the signing/trade windows of the NHL calendar; compute months to free agency and an indicator of whether a trade requires consent; refresh weekly and after each transaction; encode a feasible destination set with ex ante constraint flags.

nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.label: Suitor cap space and roster-fit table
nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.mechanism: Cap space, positional need and competitive window of each team relative to the player.
nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.rationale: A destination requires cap room and a lineup need; teams with space and a hole at the position are the likely suitors, and the number of feasible suitors changes the probabilities in a partition over 32 teams.
nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.measurement: For each team compute projected cap space at the next signing window (cap ceiling minus committed salary for the next season, adjusted for LTIR), roster need for the position (depth chart gap in impact score), and a competitive-window score (points percentage and age of core); form a suitor score = space feasibility x need x window with weights fit on past star free-agent decisions (5 seasons, k=15 events); normalise to a probability vector with the player's preference (location, prior team) if known.

nhl.insider_report_credibility.label: Insider report credibility and lag
nhl.insider_report_credibility.mechanism: Reporter- and report-type-specific hit rate and lag between a report and the official announcement.
nhl.insider_report_credibility.rationale: Reports of talks, offers or agreements differ in reliability; the contract only settles on official actions, so the hit rate and lag set how much a report should move the probability within the time window.
nhl.insider_report_credibility.measurement: Collect reports (reporter, timestamp, type in {talks, close, agreed, official}, player/club) for 5 seasons; for each report-type r and reporter j label y=1 if an official transaction matching it occurs within 7, 30 or 90 days. Precision_j,r = (hits+2)/(n+4) (Beta(2,2) prior). Likelihood ratio for a contract event E within its window = precision / base_rate(E class in window), base rate from nhl.offfield_base_rate; also store lag distribution (report to official). nhl.reference_class_hazard.label: Class-specific event hazard (player move by contract class, expansion by process stage, award by finalist)
nhl.reference_class_hazard.mechanism: Each off-field contract belongs to a narrow reference class whose hazard is estimated separately: a player changing teams inside a dated window given contract status and team situation, an expansion announcement given its process stage, an award given its finalist set.
nhl.reference_class_hazard.rationale: The pooled base rate is meaningless for three unrelated generating processes. Narrow classes have small samples, so each hazard needs an explicit estimator and shrinkage, and expansion has so few events that its probability is a stage-transition judgement rather than a frequency.
nhl.reference_class_hazard.measurement: Player move: from NHL transactions since 2005-06, hazard of a trade or signing with a new team within the window = logistic regression on contract class (expiring, term remaining, NMC/NTC), month, team standing and cap space, shrunk to the class mean with k=30 player-windows; status quo probability = 1 minus the hazard. Expansion: stage-transition probabilities between process stages (committee formed, applications, ownership named, vote scheduled) from the 1991-2021 expansion waves (n of about 8), reported with wide intervals and never as a precise frequency. Award: conditional-logit winner-among-finalists from past finalist sets. As-of: latest transaction wire and governance statements; never a market price.

nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.label: [Simulation output, not raw data] Winning-streak extremum distribution (league-wide max run length)
nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.mechanism: Probability distribution of the longest winning streak among 32 teams over the season, and per-team shares.
nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.rationale: The longest streak is an extremum, determined by the best teams' win probability and by streakiness; modelling teams one at a time with independent geometric runs underestimates the maximum when goalie form and schedule clusters create autocorrelation.
nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.measurement: Simulate seasons from the rating posterior (with per-game win probabilities, drift and a goalie-form autocorrelation parameter estimated from historical runs: lag-1 correlation of results controlling for strength, k=600 games); for each simulation record each team's longest regular-season streak counting regulation, OT and shootout wins as wins unless the rules say otherwise; output per-team probability of holding the maximum (with 1/N for ties). Calibrate against 20 seasons of league-max streak lengths.

nhl.league_scoring_environment.label: League scoring environment drift
nhl.league_scoring_environment.mechanism: Current-season league goals per game relative to the prior-season baseline, with shrinkage.
nhl.league_scoring_environment.rationale: League scoring levels shift between seasons by a few percent (rules, enforcement, goalie equipment, shot quality), moving every player's goal expectation together; a 60-goal threshold is sensitive to a three percent level change.
nhl.league_scoring_environment.measurement: As of date t, n = number of team-games completed league-wide before t. Estimate G_hat = w x G_todate + (1-w) x G_prior_season, with w = n/(n+250), G = league goals per team per game (and likewise PP opportunities per game). Multiplier = G_hat / G_prior_season; its sd = sqrt(sd_todate^2 w^2 + sd_prior^2 (1-w)^2) with sd_prior=1.5 percent and sd_todate from the Poisson standard error. Refresh weekly from games dated before t.
raw_data: league goals per team-game by date

nhl.schedule_sequence_profile.label: Schedule sequence profile (home stands, back-to-backs, opponent strength along the path)
nhl.schedule_sequence_profile.mechanism: Winning streaks and division races depend on the order of games, not only on their count: long home stands, runs of back-to-backs and strings of weak opponents raise the chance of long runs of wins.
nhl.schedule_sequence_profile.rationale: A longest-streak statistic is an extremum over 32 teams, so a small schedule-driven lift in the per-game win probability of a strong team over a stretch changes the tail. The same sequence matters for the remaining-schedule strength in a division race. The effect is small but is the only pregame-knowable driver of streak timing.
nhl.schedule_sequence_profile.measurement: For each team build the remaining game list with venue, rest days (back-to-back flag), travel and opponent rating (posterior mean); compute per-game win probability from the rating difference, home flag and rest effect and the cumulative win probability along every window of 8-20 games; output for each team the expected maximum run and the distribution of remaining-schedule strength; refresh daily. As-of: schedule is fixed in advance, ratings as of the contract date.
raw_data: remaining schedule with venues and rest

nhl.team_season_points_distribution.label: Team season points distribution (current points + remaining games with loser points)
nhl.team_season_points_distribution.mechanism: A team season point total is points banked plus the sum over remaining games of two points for a win and one for an overtime or shootout loss, so its distribution follows from per-game win and extra-time probabilities.
nhl.team_season_points_distribution.rationale: Six of the eight live series are team-level; a points threshold, a division title and a streak all need the same team-level layer: a rating posterior turned into per-game outcomes with the loser-point structure. This input states that chain explicitly rather than relying on undefined catalog items.
nhl.team_season_points_distribution.measurement: Per remaining game, P(regulation win), P(OT/SO win), P(OT/SO loss) from the team ratings posterior (score-adjusted xG differential plus goalie GSAx shrunk 1000 shots plus pdo regression, home and rest adjustments) with extra-time probability from the league tie model (about a quarter of games, to be measured); points = 2 x wins + 1 x extra-time losses; add points to date; simulate 20000 seasons drawing a rating from the posterior once per season; output the pmf of final points, P(points >= threshold) and the joint distribution across teams for the division winner using league tiebreaks (regulation wins first). As-of: standings and injuries as of the contract date.

nhl.national_team_roster_strength.label: National-team roster strength from NHL player values (best-on-best tournaments)
nhl.national_team_roster_strength.mechanism: A national team's goal differential per game is the sum of its players' individual contributions weighted by expected ice time, plus its starting goalie's save quality.
nhl.national_team_roster_strength.rationale: Club ratings cannot be reused: national rosters mix players from many clubs, depth is much higher than an NHL team's, and the decisive differences are the top-pair defence and the starting goalie; injury withdrawals after roster announcement move strength materially.
nhl.national_team_roster_strength.measurement: For each announced roster as of the market timestamp: skater value = 3-season RAPM xG differential per 60 (5v5), shrunk toward position mean with prior weight 1,500 minutes; weight by tournament TOI per game (F lines 1-4: 18/16/13/9 min; D pairs 1-3: 23/19/15 min, special teams added from PP/PK unit RAPM). Goalie = 3-season GSAx per 60 shrunk with k=3,000 shots. Team value = sum, converted to expected goal differential per game via the club goal model; recompute on each withdrawal or replacement timestamp.

nhl.short_tournament_format_sim.label: Short best-on-best tournament format simulation (round robin plus final)
nhl.short_tournament_format_sim.mechanism: The champion is determined by a three-game round robin with standings points and tiebreaks, then one final game, so the title probability is a functional of per-game win probabilities under the format.
nhl.short_tournament_format_sim.rationale: Four games make the outcome variance-dominated; the points system (regulation vs overtime wins), the round-robin tiebreak and overtime rules change which two teams reach the final, so a simple strength ranking overstates the favourite.
nhl.short_tournament_format_sim.measurement: Monte Carlo (20000 draws): for each scheduled round-robin game draw regulation result from the bivariate goal model of the two roster strengths with a home-crowd term for the host nation, resolve ties by the published OT/shootout format, award standings points per the published scheme, rank with published tiebreakers, play the final with the tournament's overtime rule; output P(win) per country as of the market timestamp, updated after each played game.

nhl.playoff_round_goal_leader_sim.label: Playoff-round goal-leader simulation (series length x per-game goal rates, tie mass)
nhl.playoff_round_goal_leader_sim.mechanism: The round leader is the argmax of goal counts accumulated over a random number of games by the skaters of the teams in that round, with ties split 1/N.
nhl.playoff_round_goal_leader_sim.rationale: Season leaderboard inputs do not transfer: exposure is a 4-7 game series common to all candidates, opponents are fixed (one goalie dominates conversion), playoff PP rates differ, and with leaders on 3-5 goals ties are common, so the fair price is an expectation over fractional payouts rather than a simple max probability.
nhl.playoff_round_goal_leader_sim.measurement: As of the market timestamp: per game, each skater's goal rate = shrunk playoff+regular ixG/60 x finishing factor (k=150 shots) x projected TOI by state x opposing starter's GSAx adjustment; series-length pmf from per-game win probabilities with the 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern and current series state; simulate 20000 series drawing lineup availability per game, count goals, compute each player's expected payout = sum over sims of 1{max}/N_tied; players who appear in no game are excluded (fair-price leg).

nhl.retirement_hazard_profile.label: Veteran retirement hazard by age, contract status, production and health
nhl.retirement_hazard_profile.mechanism: The probability that a player announces an immediately effective retirement before a season start depends on age, contract status, recent production, injury history and remaining milestones.
nhl.retirement_hazard_profile.rationale: Retirement contracts are about one person, so the base rate must be conditioned on the right covariates; an unsigned 39-year-old with declining scoring is very different from a 39-year-old with a year left, and a farewell-season announcement does not count under the rules.
nhl.retirement_hazard_profile.measurement: Logistic hazard fit on all NHL skaters and goalies aged 33+ per off-season since 2005: outcome = retirement announced before next season start; covariates = age, contract years remaining (0/1/2+), points or GSAx per 60 trend over 2 seasons, games missed to injury last season, career milestone distance (e.g. goals to a record), unrestricted-free-agent status at July 1; apply to the named player with as-of date of the market; shrink player-specific adjustments toward the fitted rate.

nhl.gm_candidate_pool.label: GM vacancy candidate pool and hiring-process stage
nhl.gm_candidate_pool.mechanism: Once a club's GM chair is vacant, the next GM is drawn from a small set of candidates whose probability depends on internal ties, prior GM experience, links to the club president/owner and reported interview stage.
nhl.gm_candidate_pool.rationale: The GM market is a categorical over named people, so the input must enumerate candidates and their stage; a generic hire base rate says nothing about who is hired, and reports of interviews and finalists are the main information events.
nhl.gm_candidate_pool.measurement: Per vacancy (as of the market timestamp): list candidates named in credible reports plus internal assistant GMs; score each with a multinomial logit fit on NHL GM hires since 2005 using features internal (0/1), prior NHL GM (0/1), shared employer history with the club president/owner (0/1), reported stage (none/interviewed/finalist/agreed); residual mass to 'other'; time-to-hire from vacancy date via empirical distribution of search lengths.

nhl.draft_team_need_profile.label: Club organisational need profile at the pick (positions, prospect pipeline depth, window)
nhl.draft_team_need_profile.mechanism: Translates a club's current roster, prospect pool and competitive window into position and archetype preferences when two or more prospects are close on the board.
nhl.draft_team_need_profile.rationale: Early picks are mostly decided by consensus, but between near-tied prospects clubs lean toward centre/defence scarcity or toward a pipeline gap. The subtlety is that NHL clubs historically claim to take best available, so the need effect is small at the top and grows only where the board is flat.
nhl.draft_team_need_profile.measurement: For each club holding a first-round pick compute, as of draft week, (a) count and quality (draft-pedigree-weighted) of signed or drafted prospects aged <=22 by position C/W/D/G, (b) NHL roster age and contract-expiry profile by position over the next 3 seasons, (c) rebuild-vs-contend flag from last-two-season points%. Express as a position-need z-score vs league mean; shrink to zero with k=3 historical picks per club-position cell to avoid noise; freeze at the draft-order-final timestamp.

nhl.draft_board_dispersion.label: Cross-service disagreement on each prospect's rank
nhl.draft_board_dispersion.mechanism: Measures how much independent services disagree about one prospect, which is information the mean consensus rank and the rank-1 vs rank-2 gap (held in prospect_consensus_ranking) do not carry.
nhl.draft_board_dispersion.rationale: Two prospects with the same mean rank can have SD 0.5 or SD 6 across services; the second is far more likely to be taken well away from his mean. This input is only the disagreement measure; the slot calibration lives in prospect_consensus_ranking, so it is not counted twice.
nhl.draft_board_dispersion.measurement: For each prospect at the as-of date take ranks from every service available for that year (NHL Central Scouting split NA/EU lists mapped to a combined rank, TSN/McKenzie, Elite Prospects public list, others where archived; minimum 3), compute the cross-service SD of rank and the inter-quartile range, winsorise ranks at 64. No slot calibration here; used as a covariate in the conditional-logit utility. History limited to years with >=3 archived services (expected ~2012 onward; see d6).

nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.label: Probability a held pick changes club or slot before selection
nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.mechanism: Estimates the chance the slot is traded to another club (or the selection traded post-pick) between the lottery and the selection call, changing which club makes the pick.
nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.rationale: Contracts that settle on which team selects, rather than which player, depend on pick ownership at the moment the pick is announced. Picks are frequently moved on draft day, and top-3 picks move rarely but non-zero, so a static ownership table is not a final answer.
nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.measurement: From the draft-pick transaction history 2005-present compute, per slot bucket (1-3, 4-10, 11-20, 21-32), the share of picks that changed club within the 14 days before selection and on draft day, separated by whether the holding club is a seller or buyer by points% rank. Add a club-level multiplier from past count of draft-day trades per GM, shrunk to league with k=4 drafts. As-of the ownership table timestamp. Settlement is on the player, so the hazard enters only by switching which club's utility applies at the slot.

nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.label: Prospect eligibility, signing-rights and medical availability flags
nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.mechanism: Captures whether each prospect is eligible for the given draft, has no contractual or injury obstacle to being taken at a high slot.
nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.rationale: A top prospect with a major injury, an age-eligibility edge case, or a contract-rights complication can slide by several slots. The slide is asymmetric: clubs seldom move a prospect up for reasons of health.
nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.measurement: For each of the top-40 prospects as-of the draft combine and the week before the draft, record binary or ordinal flags: eligible (born by the cut-off date), over-ager status, injury within last 12 months with games missed share, combine medical concerns reported, and signing-path complexity (CHL vs NCAA vs European contract). nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.label: General-manager and scouting-staff draft behaviour history
nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.mechanism: Learns how often a club's decision-makers deviate from the consensus board and in which direction (upside, size, age, nationality) from their past selections.

nhl.draft_order_playoff_elimination.label: Draft order of playoff clubs (slots 17-32) from round of elimination and regular-season points
nhl.draft_order_playoff_elimination.mechanism: Assigns slots 17-32 to the 16 playoff clubs from how far each advanced and from regular-season points within groups, so it depends on playoff series outcomes.
nhl.draft_order_playoff_elimination.rationale: Before the playoffs end, which club picks at 17-32 is uncertain; a prospect projected in the 20s is more likely to go to a club whose board or need suits him. Cup winner 32, finalist 31 and conference-final losers 29-30 are firm; the ordering of earlier losers (pure points vs division-winner adjustment) must be checked against the current rule (d5).
nhl.draft_order_playoff_elimination.measurement: For each of 10,000 simulated playoff paths from nhl.bracket_path_difficulty with per-series win probabilities from the rating posterior: assign slots 17-24 to round-1 losers, 25-28 to round-2 losers, 29-30 to conference-final losers, 31 to the Cup runner-up, 32 to the Cup winner; inside each group rank by regular-season points (ties by the NHL draft tie-break: fewer regulation wins first). Output P(club holds slot k) for k=17..32. After each completed series fix the observed eliminations. As-of = last completed series, ratings before that timestamp.

nhl.draft_remaining_board_state.label: [Model state, joint simulation] Prospects still available at slot k given picks 1..k-1
nhl.draft_remaining_board_state.mechanism: Simulates the draft pick by pick: each holder chooses among the remaining prospects, so availability at slot k is the result of all earlier choices.
nhl.draft_remaining_board_state.rationale: Calibrating on the unconditional 'rank-k prospect went at slot k' is wrong once an early reach happens, since one off-board pick shifts every later slot. The quantity the contracts need, P(prospect at k) and P(prospect by N), only exists as a joint path probability.
nhl.draft_remaining_board_state.measurement: Conditional logit (or Plackett-Luce) over the remaining top-64 board at each slot: utility = b1*consensus mean rank + b2*cross-service SD + b3*need match + b4*club reach tendency + b5*production/combine residual + medical flag, with club-staff random effects shrunk to league (k=6 picks). Fit on drafts with archived boards (~2012 onward, d6), validate by log-loss of actual picks 1-32. Simulate 20,000 draft paths with ownership and lottery draws; output each prospect's slot pmf and CDF.

nhl.series_game_count_pmf.label: [Model output, not raw data] Joint series winner-by-length pmf (8 cells) from per-game probabilities and home-ice pattern
nhl.series_game_count_pmf.mechanism: Builds the probability that a best-of-seven ends in exactly 4, 5, 6 or 7 games from each game's win probability, with the 2-2-1-1-1 home sequence and between-game dependence.
nhl.series_game_count_pmf.rationale: Games, exact-score, spread and championship-score contracts settle directly on cells of this pmf, and total goals sum over its length. It is computed from ratings, goalies and venue, so it must not be counted as independent information next to them. Shared rating uncertainty makes series more lopsided (shorter) rather than longer; whether game-to-game dependence offsets that is estimated in series_game_dependence.
nhl.series_game_count_pmf.measurement: For each series compute home/away win probabilities from ratings drawn from the rating posterior, goalie, injuries and rest (as of the pre-series timestamp), apply series_state_win_prob_shift in elimination states and the fitted dependence from series_game_dependence, and enumerate or simulate 20,000 paths through 2-2-1-1-1 to get P(winner, length). Calibrate against 2005-06 onward series: historical game-7 share and sweep share by pre-series favourite bucket. Recompute after each game conditional on the series score.

nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.label: Series-state effect on per-game goal rate (elimination, trailing team, game-7 intensity)
nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.mechanism: Adjusts expected goals per game for the series score, since trailing and elimination games change risk-taking, line usage, goaltending changes and empty-net frequency.
nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.rationale: A series that is 3-0 behaves differently from 1-1: the trailing team pulls goalies earlier and the leader sits back, but the state is also what lengthens or shortens the series. The effect on goals is mixed across directions, so it must be measured rather than assumed.
nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.measurement: From playoff games 2008-present tag each game by series score entering the game (e.g. 0-0, 1-0, 1-1, 2-1, 3-0, 3-1, 3-2, 3-3) and elimination flag; regress total goals per game (regulation plus OT) on state dummies, team rating-implied goal mean and venue, with a team random effect. Shrink small cells with k=15 games to the pooled mean; report multiplicative shift factors by state with standard errors.

nhl.series_adjustment_regime.label: Coaching adjustment and matchup learning across games in a series
nhl.series_adjustment_regime.mechanism: Captures how coaches change lines, matchups, special-teams assignments and goalie decisions between games, shifting pace and goals as the series progresses.
nhl.series_adjustment_regime.rationale: Early series games are sampled with the regular-season matchup profile; later games reflect adjustments and fatigue, and the typical drift in scoring across game number is not zero. Home last-change opportunity compounds this.
nhl.series_adjustment_regime.measurement: Compute from playoff games 2010-present the average change in goals per game from game 1-2 to game 5-7 conditioning on round, and the team coach-level adjustment effect measured as residual of scoring versus rating prediction at game index k. Use a team-coach random effect with shrinkage k=20 games, windows over four seasons, and exclude games played after a goalie change from the baseline.

nhl.series_game_dependence.label: Within-series game-to-game dependence of results (sign and size)
nhl.series_game_dependence.mechanism: Estimates whether, beyond fixed per-game probabilities, the result of game g changes the win probability of game g+1 (positive: momentum; negative: bounce-back or loser-adjusts).
nhl.series_game_dependence.rationale: The two candidate mechanisms push length in opposite directions: momentum and shared strength make series shorter, bounce-back lengthens them. Treating any dependence as 'fattening the 7-game tail' gets the sign wrong for shared shocks; it must be estimated after removing the shared-strength mixing.
nhl.series_game_dependence.measurement: On playoff series 2005-06 onward, fit a logit for game g outcome with pre-series rating-implied log-odds, home flag, and lagged result of game g-1 (and series score), with the series-level rating posterior integrated out; the lag coefficient gives the dependence. Shrink toward 0 with a normal prior sd 0.15; compare the predicted game-7 and sweep shares with the observed shares as a check of sign.

nhl.series_state_win_prob_shift.label: Series-state shift in per-game win probability (elimination, trailing 0-3 or 1-3, closeout games)

nhl.series_pair_scoring_rate_uncertainty.label: Shared posterior uncertainty in the pair's combined goal rate (attack plus defence sum) for one series
nhl.series_pair_scoring_rate_uncertainty.mechanism: Posterior SD of the matchup's expected total goals per game (both teams' attack and suppression components summed), a level error shared by every game of the series.
nhl.series_pair_scoring_rate_uncertainty.rationale: rating_posterior_uncertainty describes uncertainty in the strength differential, which moves who wins and the series length but not the combined scoring level. An error in the pair's total goal rate is common to all games, so the variance it adds to series total goals scales with the square of games played, unlike per-game overdispersion, which scales linearly. Ignoring it understates both tails of KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOAL strikes.
nhl.series_pair_scoring_rate_uncertainty.measurement: Fit a bivariate Poisson/negative-binomial team model with separate attack and defence effects on score-adjusted xG and goals (3 seasons, exponential decay half-life 60 games, preseason prior), take the posterior covariance of (attack_A+defence_B)+(attack_B+defence_A) per game, add the playoff_context and league_scoring_environment multiplier SDs, and express as SD of expected goals per game as of the pre-series timestamp; draw one value per simulated series. Validate by comparing the PIT of observed series totals 2005-06 onward with and without the shared term.
