contract_review.settlement_definition: KXNHLGAME pays YES if the named team wins the single listed NHL game on the official final result, which in the regular season includes overtime and shootout; KXNHLSPREAD pays YES if the named team wins by more than the floor_strike (for example over 2.5 goals, i.e. a margin of three or more) in that game. Ties do not exist in the NHL, so there is no push. Games postponed but started within 48h stay open; cancelled or unstarted-in-48h games resolve to a fair price. After the market-universe reconciliation the archetype holds only KXNHLGAME and KXNHLSPREAD; KXNHLPRES and KXNHLSERIES now sit in season_futures and KXNHLMVP in season_awards_and_stats, and no input below claims to cover them.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NHL final score and standings records; Kalshi resolves from the league's final result.
variants_and_edge_cases: Shootout games: the NHL box score awards the shootout winner a one-goal margin, so a shootout win can never contribute to a spread rung of 1.5 or higher; KXNHLSPREAD text does not state this, so the official-score reading is an inference. Corroboration: the sampled KXNHLTOTAL and KXNHLTEAMTOTAL rules state the shootout winner is credited one goal ("If the game is decided by a shootout, the shootout result will be recorded as one goal awarded to the winning team"), which supports the one-goal convention for KXNHLSPREAD but does not prove it for that series; the winner contract counting OT/SO wins remains an inference from silence in KXNHLGAME.

Strike ladder: KXNHLSPREAD rungs are one-sided 'wins by over x' contracts per team (1.5, 2.5, ...), so the underdog 'wins by over 2.5' contract and the favourite's are separate markets with very different tail probabilities.
Empty-net goals count toward the final margin: a one-goal late lead turns into a two-goal margin on an empty net, which matters for the 1.5 rung and for 2.5 via two-goal leads.

Reconciled series: KXNHLPRES and KXNHLSERIES (playoff series winner; rules text now recovered) sit in season_futures and KXNHLMVP (title-only Hart duplicate) in season_awards_and_stats; every input claim here holds for KXNHLGAME and KXNHLSPREAD only.

Playoff games: the same two series cover playoff games, where ties are settled by unlimited 20-minute 5v5 sudden-death overtimes and no shootout; the sampled rules do not distinguish season type, so the regular-season 3v3/shootout resolution model must not be applied to playoff listings.

game_total_and_team_total.label: Game total goals and team totals
game_total_and_team_total.target: Whether total goals (or a team's goals) in the game exceed a threshold under the contract's period and OT scope.
game_total_and_team_total.mechanism: Expected goals for each team equal shot volume times shot quality times goalie conversion, with an additive special-teams component from expected penalties and an empty-net component from late close-game dynamics. Totals are the sum of two overdispersed counts with mild positive correlation through pace, officiating and style; team totals are single-team versions with goalie and opposing defence dominating. Thresholds at integer and half-goal rungs price tail probabilities requiring dispersion estimates.

inputs.why: Joint shot volume determines number of chances.
Chance quality created by each team scales expected goals, split 5v5 and PP.
Opponent's suppression quality reduces expected goals, and lineup-specific values matter more than season averages.
SOG allowed adjusts shot volume against the specific defence and its score-effect behavior.
Starter identity moves expected goals by tenths.
Converts shot quality into goals.
Danger-split of goalie against opponent shot mix.
PP/PK efficiency converts expected penalty minutes into goals above 5v5 rates.
Expected PP minutes each side.
Crew-level effect on penalties.
Empty-net goals add to totals in close late games, and their inclusion depends on the rules text.
Fatigue raises goals against and increases backup-goalie starts, shifting team totals.
Absent skaters change both offence and defence and especially PP units, shifting the totals.
Regress goal luck in recent samples.
Over/under rungs in the tails price variance; dispersion and correlation determine rung probabilities.
Rink environment and counting differences shift scoring and shot-based features.
Total and team-total rungs consistency.
Whether overtime, shootout goals and empty-net goals count changes the target quantity itself.
Opponent shot suppression sets expected attempts.
Danger-zone mix converts attempts to goals.
Totals and team totals read the same pmf with different functionals; the shootout +1 credit and empty-net goals change odd-total mass, which a goals-only model does not reproduce.
Gives the power-play part of totals as a compound count with termination rather than a product of time and rate, which fattens the penalty-heavy tail of the over rungs.
Replaces the single combined pace number with a matchup-specific attempt forecast for the pair, where combined-pace errors are a first-order driver of totals.

interactions.hypothesis: Pace x goalie: pace raises SOG but goals only if the goalie and shot quality convert; use xG-based pace for goals and keep SOG pace for saves/SOG markets.
Penalty expectation: teams' taken rates x opponent drawn rates x crew effect x PP efficiency; each factor is shrunk and the product is a PP-goal expectation.
Team total depends on the opposing goalie confirmed only close to puck drop, so team-total prices should jump on confirmation relative to game total which changes less.
EN and OT inclusion rules change totals: contracts including OT/EN add goals mainly in tied/close games; match the model to wording.

Expected goals equal attempts times conversion, so an extra 5 attempts matter more against a weak goalie than a strong one; additive pace and quality effects misprice games where fast teams face elite goalies and slow teams face weak ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress game goals on log attempts, log quality and their product, and compare with an additive specification by out-of-sample deviance.

interactions.hypothesis: Goals per power play flatten with penalty minutes because a minor ends on a goal, and PP1 does most of the work early, so doubling expected penalties adds less than double the PP goals; the effect is larger for strong PP units that score early.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate PP goal hazard by elapsed PP seconds and compare predicted goals under time x rate versus the hazard-with-termination model.

interactions.hypothesis: The shootout credit of +1 applies only in regular-season games tied after 65 minutes, so it adds mass to odd totals in proportion to P(tie) and to nothing in the playoffs; half-goal rungs at 5.5 and 6.5 therefore have a season-type-specific probability shift.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised over frequency on 5.5 and 6.5 rungs for regular season vs playoffs against a rule-free model and measure the residual.

interactions.hypothesis: When a starter is pulled after several goals, the relief goalie's save rate is lower and the trailing team presses, switching the game into a high-total regime; the right tail of the ladder (9.5 to 11.5) is driven by this regime, not by a larger mean.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit a two-component mixture to total goals with a meltdown indicator and test tail calibration for totals of nine or more.

interactions.hypothesis: Empty-net goals appear only when a one-goal game is still live late; how many arrive depends on the leader score-state mix and on the trailing team pull policy and 6v5 risk, so the count of late goals is a threshold response to the entering lead rather than a smooth function of total pace.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition on games within one goal at 57:00 and compare empty-net goal counts and total-goal residuals by team pull time; check that the 11.5/5.5 tail is not driven by this term.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave in expected penalty minutes
nonlinearities.why: Because a minor penalty ends on a goal and a second unit takes over, expected PP goals grow less than linearly in penalty minutes, so linear penalty features overstate high-penalty games.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex tails above 8 goals
nonlinearities.why: Probability of 9 or more total goals is driven by dispersion and mixture components; a small increase in dispersion raises the far tail multiplicatively while barely changing 5.5 rungs.

nonlinearities.shape: Weak slope with heavy shrinkage
nonlinearities.why: Observed GSAx has little persistence, so the effective effect on goals against is a flat, noisy slope that only becomes steep for goalies with several thousand shots of evidence.

mechanism_review.summary: Total goals are the sum of two overdispersed counts, each equal to shot volume times shot quality times the opposing goalie's conversion, plus power-play goals that depend on how many penalties are called, and a late-game component of empty-net goals. The pair of teams matters multiplicatively, not additively: pace of a game is the product of both teams' tempo preferences and the defensive suppression each applies. After regulation, overtime goals add to the total and a shootout adds a fixed one-goal credit, which moves mass onto odd totals in tied games, a settlement feature that raw hockey goal models omit. Team totals are the single-team marginals, dominated by the opposing goalie, the team's own power-play share and the possibility of a goalie meltdown cascade that pushes counts into the tail. High-strike rungs (9.5, 11.5, team 5.5) are priced from the tail of a mixture, which the mean does not determine.

stages.name: Joint shot-attempt volume of the pair
stages.description: Combined attempt volume comes from each team's offensive tempo and the other team's suppression and is shaped by score effects: trailing teams generate more attempts, leaders fewer. The pair composite is log-additive (offence of A plus defence of B plus home term), so a high-pace team against a defensive structure does not simply add the two paces. Volume also varies with penalties because power plays are higher-volume per minute, and with back-to-back fatigue. Pregame, score_state rates are integrated over a ratings-only script distribution, never over a market-implied win probability or total.
stages.distribution: Poisson-gamma counts of attempts per team with a pair-level shared random effect; combined attempts sd of order 8-10 per game with positive team correlation.

stages.name: Chance quality and goalie conversion
stages.description: Each attempt becomes a goal with probability set by location and type (xG), the shooter's finishing and the opposing goalie. Starter identity moves a team's expected goals against by a few tenths per game, and goalie skill is the hardest rate to measure because it takes thousands of shots to separate. Rebounds and danger-zone share make conversion state dependent on shot mix, not just totals.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per shot with small probability; goals per team approximately Poisson-gamma with mean 2.8-3.2 league-wide and heterogeneity across goalies.

stages.name: Penalties and power-play goal production
stages.description: Special-teams goals are a large and volatile component: the number of minor penalties depends on both teams' styles and the referee pair, each power play converts at roughly a fifth to a quarter of the time, and a minor penalty ends when the power-play team scores, so expected goals per PP minute is concave in PP time. Unit allocation (PP1 vs PP2) changes conversion within a power play. Totals are therefore sensitive to penalty counts, which are high-variance.
stages.distribution: Compound count: Poisson number of power plays times conversion Bernoulli that terminates the penalty; heavy right tail from multi-penalty games.

stages.name: Late game, overtime and shootout mapping to the contract
stages.description: Empty-net goals add a point to the leader's total in close games, regulation ties add an OT period in which goals count, and a shootout adds one credited goal. The mapping therefore transforms the regulation distribution: P(total odd) rises in the regular season relative to the playoffs, and the mass at k+k+1 grows with P(tie). In the playoffs there is no shootout, so the model must branch on season type. Goalie meltdowns (a starter pulled after several goals) create a high-total tail through a weaker relief goalie.
stages.distribution: Mixture: regulation count plus Bernoulli OT/SO additions; tail mixture component for meltdown games with total above nine.

officiating_rules.note: Crew tendencies are folded into nhl.penalty_rates (nhl.officials audited as its duplicate); crew assignment is only partially known pregame (posted on game day), so the crew term applies only after posting and defaults to zero before.

coaching_scheme.note: No input captures coach-level tempo and risk policy for totals (trap vs forecheck systems, line matching to protect leads); the proxy through pace and score effects only partially reflects it.

required_data.dataset: Team-game attempts, xG and minutes by strength state
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Features from games before the as-of date; vendor xG vintages stored.

required_data.dataset: Penalty and power-play event log
required_data.grain: one row per penalty and PP opportunity
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Penalty counts known after games; crew assignments known day of game. Referee crew assignments are posted around game day: the crew term is used only from its posting timestamp (vintage-stamped) and set to zero before it.
required_data.history_needed: 2010-11 onward; referee assignments from game summaries.

candidate_sources.name: NHL game summary HTML (officials)
candidate_sources.note: referees and linesmen listed per game

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Starter confirmation vintages kept; pull events after game.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXNHLTOTAL pays YES if the two teams collectively score more than the floor_strike (for example 11.5) goals in the listed game; goals in regulation and overtime count normally and a shootout is recorded as one goal awarded to the winner, so a shootout game adds exactly one to the total. KXNHLTEAMTOTAL pays YES if the named team scores over its floor_strike (for example 5.5) with the same overtime inclusion and the shootout winner credited one additional goal. KXNHLTOTAL: postponed games remain open if started within 48h, else fair-price resolution; KXNHLTEAMTOTAL's sampled text carries no postponement clause.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NHL game summary (goals by period including OT, shootout winner); Kalshi settles by the league record plus the stated shootout convention.
variants_and_edge_cases: Shootout credit: when the score is level after OT the game total is 2k+1 and the winner's team total is k+1; in the regular season a minority of games (rate to be measured from NHL results, see tt6) go to a shootout, so this +1 can matter for half-goal rungs at 5.5 or 6.5.
Playoffs have no shootout, so the +1 credit never applies and totals are pure regulation plus continuous OT goals; the model must switch rule set by season type.
Ladder tails: strikes like 11.5 and team-total 5.5 are far-tail events whose probability is set by dispersion and meltdown mixtures rather than by the mean.
KXNHLTOTAL carries the 48h postponement/fair-price clause; the sampled KXNHLTEAMTOTAL rules do not mention postponement or cancellation at all (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, tt6).

period_markets.label: Period winner, total, spread and both-teams-to-score
period_markets.target: Outcome within a single 20-minute period (winner including tie handling, goal total, spread, or both teams scoring).
period_markets.mechanism: A period is a short sample from the full-game process with period-specific shape: low-event first periods, long-change second periods and score-state-dominated third periods. Since few goals occur (few per period) the distribution is dominated by zeros and ones and ties are common, so winner markets are heavily affected by tie-handling and the tail shape of Poisson-like counts. Goalie identity and first-minute deployments matter proportionally more than in the full game.

inputs.why: Period-specific scoring shape by team vs league.
Chance quality per 20 minutes.
Chance suppression per 20 minutes drives conceded goals in that period.
Event rate in a given period depends on team style and score state and sets the number of chances.
Goalie identity and warm state.
A single PP in a 20-minute period can decide the period, so special-team strength is concentrated.
Penalty draws in the period give PP time that is a large share of period scoring.
Third-period behaviour changes sharply with lead or deficit, altering shot rates and goal risk.
Probability of lead/trail entering the period.
Empty-net goals concentrate in the last minutes of the third period and affect third-period totals.
Second-period long change is associated with different chance patterns in that frame.
Starting units and early deployment shape first-period scoring chances.
Coaches' line usage and PP time allocation by period affect which players generate chances.
A zero-heavy count requires an overdispersed model to price 0 goal, 1 goal and over rungs.
Period tie handling; does OT count; shootout.
A team's shooting and save percentage beyond expectation regress; period markets inherit the noise.
Provides the entering-state mixture that period 2 and 3 winner, spread and total contracts require.
In the third-period contracts empty-net goals count and overtime does not, so the pull and equalizer rates directly set the last two minutes' goals for both totals and spreads.
Concentrated volatility source for short windows; also tests whether early imbalances change later-period tie mass.
Gives the tie, winner, spread and total functionals in one coherent distribution so period contracts agree with each other.
Gives the contract a market-free script latent (state mixture and entering-state matrix) so that benchmark prices remain an independent yardstick.
Supplies the missing home flag and period-specific home edge to winner, spread and tie contracts of each of the three periods.
Adds period-specific rest effects, especially the first-period backup-goalie channel, that a full-game rest constant would blur.

interactions.hypothesis: Period winner needs the tie probability: with few goals per period, P(tie) is large, so tie-handling in the contract sets the baseline as much as team strength.
Third-period outcomes are a mixture over entering score state; the pregame win probability interacts with pull timing and score-effect shot rates.
First-period goals rely on starting units against the starting goalie, so the interaction of opening deployments and goalie quality is more informative than full-game averages.
Second-period scoring: long change effect interacts with line-shuffle tendencies and team skating depth.

Third period outcomes depend on the margin entering the period: with a one-goal lead the leader sits and the trailer eventually pulls, giving a late burst of goals; with a tie there is no pull until near the end, so the same ratings imply different totals and winner probabilities by entering state.
interactions.how_to_test: Split third-period goals by entering margin and compare scoring rate and EN share against a margin-free model.

interactions.hypothesis: Period tie probability is the diagonal of a bivariate count whose total is small, so a shift in total changes tie mass more than a shift in difference; tie, win and spread markets must be priced from the same joint, not marginals.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised period tie rate by bin of expected team means with the product-of-marginals prediction.

interactions.hypothesis: Hypothesis only: the second-period long change makes defensive-zone line changes harder, so teams that concentrate ice time in top lines may gain or lose more than teams that roll four lines; any effect is conditional on deployment and may be zero.
interactions.how_to_test: Named contrast: the second-period minus first/third-period goal-differential gap for the top versus bottom tercile of teams ranked by forward TOI concentration; reject if the gap difference is within noise across seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: One extra power play lifts the period's expected goals by a fifth to a quarter of a goal, and the effect is convex because a second PP can follow a goal in the same period; the penalty count distribution and PP efficiency multiply, so uncertain counts fatten the upper tail.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin periods by number of minors called and compute realised goals and tie rate relative to the zero-PP baseline.

interactions.hypothesis: First-period chances against a backup goalie depend on his pregame workload and on the opponent chance quality; the interaction is confined to period one, before score state and line matching dominate, and should not be carried to periods two and three.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare first-period goals against for backups versus starters at fixed opponent xG per 60, and confirm no such gap in periods two and three.

nonlinearities.shape: Zero-heavy count: P(0) falls exponentially in the mean
nonlinearities.why: At a mean near one goal per team the probability of 0-0 and of ties changes quickly with small rate shifts, so a linear approximation in period goal rate mis-prices tie contracts near the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in the last two minutes of the third period
nonlinearities.why: Pulled goalies occur almost only in the last 2:00 of the third period; goals scored in that window are a different process, so third-period totals have a thick tail not shared by the first two periods.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in the number of power plays in the period
nonlinearities.why: Each added power play raises goal expectation by a fixed increment and increases the chance of a multi-goal period more than proportionally, so period totals above 2.5 depend on the upper tail of the penalty distribution.

mechanism_review.summary: A period is a 20-minute slice of the same scoring process with its own rates and its own state. Goals per team per period have a mean near one, so outcomes are dominated by 0, 1 and 2 goals: P(period tie) is large and the winner markets are mostly questions about how much mass sits on 0-0 and 1-1. Rates differ by period: the first is shaped by opening deployment and fresh goalies; the second has the long change that tends to lift scoring; the third is dominated by score effects and, at the end, goalie pulls and empty-net goals. Because later periods start from a random score state, period two and three markets are mixtures over entering margin. A single power play can decide a period, so penalty timing and counts are a concentrated volatility source, and referees may balance calls within a game.

stages.name: Period-specific scoring rate for each team
stages.description: Team goal rate per period is the season rate times a period factor: first-period rates are usually the lowest, the second period benefits from the long change that makes defensive-zone line changes hard, and the third responds to score. Team-specific period tendencies (slow starters, second-period scorers) exist but are noisy over 60-80 games. Opposing goalie and the pairing of attack with the defence set the level for each team separately.
stages.distribution: Poisson-gamma goal counts per team with mean about 0.9-1.1 per period; period effects of order 5-15 percent on the mean, team period effects smaller and heavily shrunk.

stages.name: Lineup, goalie and coach deployment inside the period
stages.description: Starting goalie quality and who is on the ice in the first minutes shape period one, while coaches adjust line matching and ice time by period and score. A goalie pulled mid-game changes the second and third periods for that team, and a skater injured in period one changes the rest of the game. Deployment effects are small per period but unlike full-game markets they operate on a short sample where a few shifts matter. Rest and back-to-back status enter here through the backup-goalie probability for period one and a possible late-game fade.
stages.distribution: Discrete lineup states with continuous deployment shifts; mixture over goalie identity before confirmation.

stages.name: Entering score state and late-period control
stages.description: For periods two and three the game starts from a random margin drawn from the earlier periods, so the market is a mixture over entering states; leaders reduce risk, trailers press, and in the last two minutes of the third the trailing team pulls its goalie, adding both an equalizer chance and an empty-net chance in the same period. The third period includes empty-net goals but excludes OT, making its totals fatter than the first two with a larger share of one-sided late goals.
stages.distribution: Mixture over entering margin {-2,...,+2} with state-dependent rates; third-period end process with jump component from pulls.

stages.name: Power plays, penalty timing and referee balancing
stages.description: Power-play minutes are rare and lumpy within a period: zero, one or two minor penalties, with a single PP converting roughly a fifth of the time and lifting that period's goals by a large factor. Referees may even out calls within a game, so the number of penalties in later periods depends on the earlier imbalance. The penalty process interacts with team special-teams quality and with unit deployment.
stages.distribution: Compound count: Poisson penalties per period times conversion Bernoulli, which concentrates heavy-tail mass; counts overdispersed by crew and game state.

stages.name: Joint count model and settlement of the three-way market
stages.description: The market pays on tie, home win or away win in the period, or on the margin or total thresholds. The probabilities come from a bivariate count model with period-specific variance and correlation, and cross-period dependence through score state and game total; the tie probability is the diagonal and is large. The 3rd-period exclusion of overtime must be encoded, and the period markets are NOT independent of one another or of the final result: the periods compose the final score, so cross-period dependence through score state is part of the joint model. KXNHL1PBTTS (title only, settlement assumed from the title) would be P(H1>=1 and A1>=1) = 1 - P(H1=0) - P(A1=0) + P(0-0) from the same period-one bivariate model, so its price is driven by the two teams' first-period rates and their correlation.
stages.distribution: Bivariate overdispersed counts with period-specific zero mass; P(0-0) is about 12-16 percent and P(tie) in the low-to-mid 30s percent range (the Poisson(1,1) benchmark is about 31 percent, overdispersion raises it slightly; both unsourced and to be measured).

environment.note: Rinks are indoors, so weather is irrelevant, but the home flag and last-change edge are team-versus-team effects that differ by period; carried by nhl.period_home_ice_split.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Each period contract settles only on goals scored in that 20-minute period: KXNHL1P/2P/3P are three-way style markets (a team wins the period, or the 'period tie' contract pays YES if neither team wins), KXNHL*PSPREAD pays YES if the named team wins the period by more than the floor_strike (1.5 or 2.5, i.e. a two- or three-goal margin), KXNHL*PTOTAL pays YES if the teams collectively score more than the strike in that period (for example 2.5 or 3.5), and KXNHL1PBTTS (title only, no rules text) covers both teams scoring in the first period. Rules text is recovered for the nine 1P/2P/3P winner, spread and total series; the winner texts add 'Only goals scored during the [n] period ... count', while the spread and total texts define the period only in the primary sentence ('in the 1st period') and carry the templated third-period OT note. Third-period contracts exclude overtime. Postponed games stay open if begun within 48h, otherwise resolve to a fair price.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NHL period-by-period scoring in the game summary; Kalshi resolves from league scoring by period.
variants_and_edge_cases: Copy-paste note: the 1st and 2nd period spread and total rules texts (not the winner texts) repeat 'Note: 3rd period markets do not include overtime', which is irrelevant to those periods but shows rules are templated; the 3rd period series is the only one where overtime exclusion matters.

Period tie markets versus team-win markets: a three-outcome family priced as separate binaries, so the three probabilities must sum to one up to fees and the tie mass is the key quantity at a mean of about one goal per team.
KXNHL1PBTTS is the only period series without rules text (TITLE_ONLY): whether it needs a goal credited to each team in the first period, and own-goal handling, are unseen.

Penalty and period boundaries: a power play that starts late in a period carries into the next period but goals count in the period in which they are scored; no strike construction exists for end-of-period carryover.

game_events.label: Overtime, shootout, multi-OT, BTTS, first goal and early goal
game_events.target: Event occurrence in the game: reaches overtime/shootout/multiple overtimes, both teams score, which team scores first, or an early goal within a time window.
game_events.mechanism: Overtime and shootout markets are functions of regulation-tie probability (a bivariate goal model with total and spread as inputs) and the 3v3 overtime resolution rate; playoffs change structure (no shootout, 20-minute 5v5 overtimes). BTTS depends on each team's probability of not being shut out (goalie quality, chances), and first/early-goal markets depend on opening hazards. These are low-information markets where rules text and base rates by season type dominate.

Base rates by market type and season type.
Team PDO (shooting plus save percentage) luck regresses, so rare-event counts inherit noise a rating cannot predict.
Finishing talent versus luck separates repeatable shooting from variance in rare-event counts.

KXNHLF10G now sits in this archetype: the either-team goal before 10:00 elapsed in period one is one minus the zero mass of the pair's early-window goal count, which this hazard defines without any price.

interactions.hypothesis: Shootout probability = P(tie) x P(OT not decisive): low-scoring tight games raise the first factor, team 3v3 scoring lowers the second; both must be modelled.
BTTS: P(team scores >=1) depends on goalie quality of the opponent and own xG; strong-goalie, low-pace games have a materially higher shutout chance than independent Poisson suggests.
First goal: the race between hazards depends on early PP draws and starting lines; interacting penalties and opening deployment shifts the first-team probability.
Season type changes the contract structure: playoffs remove the shootout and add multi-OT events, so the playoff flag interacts with OT scoring rates.

Tie probability is a joint function of the expected total and the expected gap: for a given gap it falls roughly with the square root of the total, and for a given total it peaks at gap zero; neither alone prices the diagonal.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin historical games by (expected total, expected gap) and compare realised tie rate with the product of marginal tie rates at each bin; test a gap x total interaction term.

interactions.hypothesis: Below roughly three minutes with a one-goal deficit the process flips to 6v5; the same trailing team can produce an equalizer (adds to ties) or an empty-net goal against (removes the tie path), so the sign of the pull effect depends on the coach's pull time and on the team's 6v5 conversion.
interactions.how_to_test: Split one-goal-deficit states at 3:00 left by team pull policy tercile and compare realised tie-at-60 frequency across terciles after controlling for 55-minute score.

interactions.hypothesis: Season type switches the overtime generator: 3v3 five-minute period then shootout in the regular season versus unlimited 20-minute 5v5 periods in the playoffs; the 3v3 rate must not be used for playoff double-OT hazard.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit OT goal hazard separately by season type and test whether team 3v3 rate predicts team playoff OT hazard (expected near zero).

interactions.hypothesis: When both teams are within reach of the playoff line a tied game late may be played for the guaranteed point, lowering shot attempts and delaying pulls; the effect should vanish when a team is eliminated or has clinched.
interactions.how_to_test: Within tied-late states, contrast attempts and pull timing between high-leverage and low-leverage standings situations in the same teams.

interactions.hypothesis: The window mean is low (about half a goal), so one early minor penalty, which gives a power play of up to two of the ten minutes, raises the scoring mean of the window by a large fraction, and a backup starter on either side raises it further; the two shocks compound only when the penalty falls inside the window, so their joint effect is larger than either alone near the median.
interactions.how_to_test: On play-by-play since 2015-16 compare the window goal frequency for games with and without a minor before 8:00 elapsed, split by backup versus regular starter, against the additive prediction.

nonlinearities.shape: Bell-shaped in expected goal gap, decreasing convex in expected total
nonlinearities.why: Tie probability is maximal when gap is zero and falls off with squared gap while higher totals spread mass across more cells; a linear feature in the spread or total mis-orders games near the extremes.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold below about 3:00 left, then steep increase
nonlinearities.why: Pull probability is near zero until the final minutes and then jumps toward one; time-linear or period-level averages hide that tie conversion happens almost entirely in a short window.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex at low totals
nonlinearities.why: At totals below five goals the 0-0, 1-1 and 2-2 cells dominate and small changes in dispersion move tie mass more than at higher totals.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave saturating: P(YES) = 1 - exp(-lambda) adjusted for dispersion
nonlinearities.why: With a window mean near 0.5 the first increments of hazard move P(goal in first 10:00) most; doubling the mean does not double the probability, so additive feature models over-react at high-hazard pairings.

mechanism_review.summary: An overtime market is a binary on the event that regulation ends level. Mechanically: two teams draw regulation goal counts from correlated, mildly overdispersed processes whose means come from shot volume x shot quality x opposing goalie, plus special-teams goals; the tie probability is the diagonal of the joint score distribution, so it rises as the expected total falls and as the expected goal difference approaches zero. Superimposed on that is a late-game control process: a trailing team pulls its goalie, which raises the chance of an equalizer but also of a 2-goal loss via an empty-net goal, so the diagonal mass is moved by coaching policy and score state in the last 3-5 minutes. Only the regulation end state matters for KXNHLOT and KXNHLOVERTIME; for the playoff-only KXNHL2OT the first 5v5 sudden-death overtime must also end goalless. Season type (regular vs playoff) shifts rates, and standings stakes may change late risk-taking when a tied game guarantees a point. KXNHLF10G, reassigned here, is a different process inside the same game: the pair's goal count in the opening ten minutes, set by early 5v5 hazards, the confirmed goalies and whether an early power play occurs, with YES equal to one minus the window's zero mass.

stages.name: Regulation scoring means and the joint score distribution
stages.description: For each side, expected regulation goals = attempts x share that are on goal x goal probability per shot (xG, finishing, opposing goalie) summed over 5v5, PP and PK states, with PP time driven by penalties. The pair (H, A) is not independent: pace, penalty counts and game state make the goal counts weakly positively correlated early and negatively correlated late (leader sits, trailer presses). The tie probability is sum_k P(H=k, A=k) and is a convex function of the expected total and bell-shaped in the goal-difference mean; mis-specified dispersion misprices the 1-1, 2-2 and 3-3 cells most.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed bivariate count (negative-binomial or Poisson-mixture) with game-state-dependent correlation; tie mass concentrated on 2-2 and 3-3 with a thin right tail.

stages.name: Starting goalie and lineup shock before puck drop
stages.description: The expected goals of both teams move by roughly a tenth to a third of a goal when the confirmed starter differs from the presumed one or a top-line forward or top-pair defenceman is out. Because the tie probability depends on the total and on the gap, a goalie change on the weaker side can raise or lower P(tie) depending on whether it closes the gap or lifts the total, so the sign of the effect is not fixed. Confirmation arrives 1-3 hours before puck drop, so the information vintage at trading time matters.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over starter identity (2-3 states per team) with different mean goals; each mixture component has its own tie probability and the market price is the weighted mixture.

stages.name: Late-regulation control: pulled goalie, equalizer and empty-net goals
stages.description: In the last 2-5 minutes a trailing team replaces its goalie; the 6v5 state raises the trailing team's scoring rate several-fold but exposes it to empty-net goals at a much higher rate than it scores. A one-goal deficit is converted to a tie with a modest probability or to a two-goal loss with a larger one, and the coach's pull time and the standings value of a loser point change the policy. Level games late may see more conservative play. Net effect: late dynamics move mass between the diagonal (ties) and +/-2 margins, so a team-specific pull policy changes P(OT) beyond what the 60-minute rates imply.
stages.distribution: Regime switch at about 3 minutes left in a one-goal game; equalizer success is a low-probability Bernoulli (order of 15-25 percent of pulls) whose rate is team- and coach-specific.

stages.name: Settlement mapping: overtime commenced, double overtime and season type
stages.description: KXNHLOT and KXNHLOVERTIME pay when overtime is reached (KXNHLOT defines it as the opening OT faceoff), so the settlement variable is the tie indicator at 60:00. KXNHL2OT adds the conditional that the first 20-minute 5v5 sudden-death playoff overtime ends without a goal, P = P(tie) x exp(-h x 20/60) with h the tied 5v5 playoff hazard of the pair, which depends on tied-state rates and fatigue; in the regular season the 3v3-then-shootout format makes it impossible. Postponement beyond 48h converts KXNHLOT to a fair-price settlement, not a loss; the other two are silent on it.
stages.distribution: Tie indicator is Bernoulli with p about 0.22-0.27 in the regular season; the double-OT event is that Bernoulli times a survival probability that is exponential in the 20-minute 5v5 hazard (roughly a third of playoff overtime games historically reach a second OT; to be measured).

stages.name: Opening-ten-minute window for KXNHLF10G
stages.description: KXNHLF10G pays if either side scores before 10:00 elapsed of the first period. Both teams start at 0-0 with no score effects and no pulled goalie, so the window count depends on each club's opening-minute 5v5 goal rate, the two confirmed starters' save quality and the chance that a minor penalty puts a power play inside the window (roughly a third of first periods see one before the ten-minute mark, to be measured). The answer is one minus the probability that the pair stays scoreless, so mid-range hazards matter most and opening-shift deployment adds almost nothing.
stages.distribution: Pair goal count in a 10-minute window: near-Poisson with mean about 0.5-0.6 and mild overdispersion; P(YES) = 1 - zero mass, so the response is concave in the window mean.

environment.note: Rinks are indoors so weather is irrelevant, rink scoring factors enter through team home/away ratings, and the tie indicator is insensitive to small venue shifts in shot counting.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXNHLOT settles YES iff at least one overtime period is played in the listed NHL game, where 'played' means the opening faceoff of that OT period is taken; i.e. the score is level after 60:00 regulation. Goals in OT, shootout outcome and the winner are irrelevant. Postponed games stay open if they begin within 48h of the original start, otherwise all markets resolve to a fair price (the sampled text is truncated at 'resolve to a fai'; 'fair price' is the reading of the standard Kalshi clause). KXNHLOVERTIME (historical, finalized) settles YES 'If [team] and [team] go to overtime' and KXNHL2OT 'If [team] and [team] go to double overtime'; both are one-sentence rules with no faceoff definition and no postponement clause. KXNHLF10G settles YES if either team scores at least one goal officially credited in the first period before 10:00 elapsed; a goal at exactly 10:00 does not count and NO requires the full ten-minute window to be completed without a goal. Source of truth is the official NHL game record.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NHL game record (period scores, OT flag) as published on nhl.com / the NHL stats API; Kalshi settles from the league result.
variants_and_edge_cases: Regular season vs playoffs: regular-season OT is one 5-minute 3v3 period then a shootout, so a second OT cannot occur; playoff OT is 20-minute 5v5 sudden-death periods, so KXNHL2OT (rules text recovered, sampled on a June 2026 Final game) is a playoff-only conditional on a goalless first OT.

KXNHLOT: a scheduled or announced OT in which no faceoff happens does not count; a go-ahead goal scored before the regulation clock expires means no OT faceoff, so games decided in the final seconds of the third period settle NO.

KXNHLOVERTIME and KXNHL2OT rules are a single sentence ('go to overtime' / 'go to double overtime') with no faceoff definition and no postponement/cancellation clause; treated as the same events as KXNHLOT's definition but recorded as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

Early-goal variant: KXNHLF10G resolves on [0:00, 10:00) of period one only, either team, officially credited goals; BTTS, shootout and first-goal-team families in the blueprint have no live series here.

season_futures.label: Championship, division/conference and playoff series futures
season_futures.target: Team wins the Cup, a conference/division, qualifies, or wins a playoff series.
season_futures.mechanism: Futures probabilities come from simulating the remaining schedule/bracket with team strength distributions: game win probabilities from xG-based ratings adjusted for goaltending and injuries, aggregated through the playoff format. Short series amplify goalie variance and injuries, while long-horizon markets are dominated by rating uncertainty and the information arrival rate (trades, injuries). Settlement rules (tiebreakers, bracket structure) matter in close races.

interactions.hypothesis: Short series amplify variance: the same rating gap yields different series win probabilities depending on goalie quality variance and injuries, so goalie uncertainty interacts with series length.
Regress standings luck before simulation but apply NHL tie-break rules to the simulated points to get seeding right.
A long-term injury changes both rating and its uncertainty; the effect on a championship price compounds across rounds.

Title probability is a convex function of team rating, so rating uncertainty raises the probability of mid-tier teams and lowers that of favourites relative to a point-rating simulation; the effect is strongest early in the season and fades as the posterior tightens.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate with and without rating draws and compare Cup probabilities by seed and across horizons.

interactions.hypothesis: A seven-game series amplifies single-game randomness and goalie volatility compounds with series length: the same rating gap yields a lower win probability than a constant-p recursion would give once goalie autocorrelation is included.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit series outcomes with and without a random goalie effect and compare upset frequency.

interactions.hypothesis: Regulation wins are the first tiebreaker, so two teams with equal points but different loser-point counts have different qualification odds; the effect arises only at ties and is conditional on the points boundary.
interactions.how_to_test: Count playoff outcomes of tied-on-points teams by regulation wins over history and compare with a points-only model.

interactions.hypothesis: A long-term injury to a key player reduces rating, but a team with cap space and assets can replace part of the loss before the deadline, so the effect on a futures price is conditional on capacity and on the date of the injury.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare change in end-of-season rating after star injuries for teams with high and low capacity.

interactions.hypothesis: Seed and division create path differences: a division winner plays a wild card while the other seeds meet inside the division; at the boundary between third seed and wild card, the path regime switches, so marginal points have an outsized effect on conference and Cup odds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute conference and Cup probabilities for the same rating under each of the possible seed placements and compare.

interactions.hypothesis: A long winning run needs a strong team AND a soft stretch of schedule (home stand, few back-to-backs, weak opponents); because the league maximum is driven by the single best realised run, rating uncertainty and an easy schedule window multiply in the tail, so a mid-strength team with a long soft stretch can out-price a stronger team with a balanced schedule.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate league-max streaks with real schedules versus shuffled schedules at the same ratings, and compare both to 20 seasons of observed league-max streak lengths and holders.

interactions.hypothesis: In a four-game tournament the starting goalie's save quality multiplies the effect of skater depth: a deep skater roster with a weak starter loses much of its edge because a single elimination-style final is decided on few goals, so goalie quality carries more weight than in an 82-game season.
interactions.how_to_test: Across historical best-on-best tournaments (Olympics with NHL players, World Cups, 4 Nations), compare champion prediction with skater-only vs skater-plus-goalie strength.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in rating for championship probability
nonlinearities.why: Winning four best-of-seven rounds multiplies four probabilities, so a small rating advantage compounds; the title odds of the top team rise faster than linearly with rating and the odds of weak qualifiers fall faster than linearly.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic around the playoff points cut-off
nonlinearities.why: Qualification is a threshold event: the probability moves from near zero to near one over a range of about 10-15 points around the mid-90s cut-off, so small changes in expected points matter most for bubble teams.

nonlinearities.shape: Decreasing in games played
nonlinearities.why: Posterior sd of rating falls roughly with the inverse square root of games played plus a drift floor, so the uncertainty premium for long-horizon futures is largest now and decays through the season.

mechanism_review.summary: A team future is the output of a two-layer simulation with uncertainty in the inputs. Layer one is the unknown team strength: posterior ratings from xG, goaltending and roster, with a drift and an uncertainty that matter as much as the mean because title odds are a convex function of rating. Layer two is the league mechanism: 82 games produce points through wins and overtime or shootout loser points; the playoff boundary is set per conference (top three in each division plus two wild cards) with league tiebreaks that favour regulation wins; the bracket then fixes opponents and home ice, and best-of-seven series amplify the variance of goaltending and injuries. The reassigned team counting contracts read other functionals of the same season simulation: a points threshold, the argmax of a division or of the league (Presidents' Trophy, with regulation-win tiebreaks), the argmin for the worst record (league tiebreaks then 1/N), and the league-wide longest winning streak, a run-length extremum that depends on schedule sequence and streakiness rather than on totals. Settlement ties (dead heat, 1/N, tiebreakers) alter probabilities near the boundary. Information arrives slowly but with jumps (injuries, trades), so the posterior update is part of the price. A separate branch, the historical KXNHL4NATIONS outright, replaces team ratings with national-roster strength and the season simulation with a four-team round robin plus final.

stages.name: Team strength posterior with drift and uncertainty
stages.description: Each team's strength is a latent rating combining last season's performance, roster changes, age curves, goaltending and current-season xG, with weight on current data growing with games played (early November is about 14 games in). The posterior has an uncertainty of order 0.2 goals per game early in the year and follows a drift because of injuries and trades, so simulating with point ratings would overstate certainty and understate the probability of surprises.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like posterior with sd 0.15-0.25 goals per game shrinking through the season, plus jump components for injuries and trades.

stages.name: Regular-season points accumulation and loser-point structure
stages.description: Remaining games are simulated with rest, travel, home and opponent strength; each game gives two points to the winner and one to an overtime or shootout loser, so a team's points include a loser-point stream that is partly skill and mostly noise. The points distribution across 82 games has sd about 7-8 points; the playoff cut-off sits near the mid-90s with its own uncertainty, and strength of schedule within division changes the remaining path.
stages.distribution: Sum of 82 game outcomes with 3-point structure (win in regulation 2, OT/SO win 2, OT/SO loss 1); points sd about 7-9; tiebreak counts (regulation wins) are a separate lattice.

stages.name: Qualification boundary, seeding and bracket path
stages.description: The top three teams in each division plus two wild cards per conference qualify; division winners face wild cards, so seeding determines opponent and home ice, and the same strength gives different championship odds by path. League tiebreakers (regulation wins, then regulation-plus-overtime wins, total wins, head-to-head points, goal differential) decide close races, and a team's Cup probability depends on which seed it ends in and on rivals' seeds.
stages.distribution: Qualification is a threshold on a noisy points total; bracket path is a combinatorial function of the final standings with discrete seeds.

stages.name: Playoff series, goaltending variance and injuries
stages.description: Each series is best-of-seven with 2-2-1-1-1 home ice; the better team's single-game win probability is only 55-65 percent, so series are high variance, and goaltending hot streaks and injuries are large contributors beyond rating. The playoff environment changes penalty rates, depth usage and overtime format, and series state (games played, rest) updates probabilities. KXNHLSERIES (rules recovered: named matchup and round) is read directly off this recursion from the current series state, and KXNHLEAST/KXNHLWEST compose three and KXNHL four such series along the bracket. Goalie identity per remaining game uses the playoff branch of nhl.goalie_start_forecast (starter-change hazard after a poor game, given series state).
stages.distribution: Series win probability from best-of-seven recursion with single-game p near 0.55-0.62 and extra variance from goalie performance beyond binomial.

stages.name: Team counting, argmax and streak contracts
stages.description: KXNHLSEASONPTS, the four division winners, KXNHLPRES, KXNHLRECORDWORST and KXNHLWSTREAK use the regular-season layer only. Each remaining game yields a regulation win, extra-time win or extra-time loss with probabilities from the rating posterior, so a team's points are banked points plus a compound sum with a loser-point stream. A threshold contract is the upper tail of that pmf; division and Presidents' Trophy contracts are argmax events over correlated totals, with Presidents' Trophy ties broken by its stated order (regulation wins first) and division ties by the league order, which the division texts do not state (sf9); KXNHLRECORDWORST is the argmin of the same correlated totals with league tiebreaks then a 1/N dead heat; the longest streak is the maximum run length over 32 teams, which depends on the order of home stands, back-to-backs and strong opponents and on any streakiness beyond strength. For KXNHLRECORDWORST, bottom-of-table teams' post-trade-deadline points rates are adjusted by nhl.standings_stakes (elimination status, lottery position, deadline sell-off) with the marginal lottery value of losing taken from nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing; the incentive is weak because the worst team's first-draw odds are 18.5% and the 10-spot move-up cap guarantees it a top-3 pick.
stages.distribution: Points: near-Gaussian with sd about 7-9 for the remainder of the season; argmax events: categorical over a few contenders; streak maximum: geometric-type tail in run length with dead-heat mass at the top.

stages.name: National-team tournament outright (KXNHL4NATIONS)
stages.description: The 4 Nations Face-Off outcome is generated by four national rosters of NHL players, not by clubs. Each country's strength is the TOI-weighted value of its named skaters plus its starting goalie, minus injury withdrawals; the format is a single round robin (three games each) with standings points, then a one-game final between the top two. With only four games for the champion, the result is dominated by single-game variance and goaltending, and overtime/3v3 rules decide a large share of games. Win probability per game comes from the roster-strength gap through the same goal model used for club games.
stages.distribution: Categorical over four teams; per-game outcomes near 55-65 percent for the stronger side, so even a clear favourite rarely exceeds about 50 percent to win; heavy dependence on which goalie starts the final.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Schedule path plus late-season stakes: elimination/lottery-position tanking adjustment (s5) for KXNHLRECORDWORST and bottom-table totals.

coaching_scheme.note: No input captures coach quality or in-season coaching changes as a driver of team strength and playoff performance; coaching change effects on ratings are unquantified and enter only through the news input.

officiating_rules.note: Playoff officiating tendencies (fewer calls, differing power-play counts) are only represented through the playoff context flag; there is no quantified input that translates officiating regime into series win probability.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Long-horizon contracts resolved on the official NHL regular season, playoffs or a named tournament: KXNHLPLAYOFF pays YES if the named team qualifies for the 2026-27 playoffs; KXNHLWEST/KXNHLEAST if it wins the 2026-27 conference final; KXNHL if it wins the 2026-27 Stanley Cup Finals; KXNHLSERIES if it wins a named playoff series (sampled: Montreal vs Buffalo 2026 2nd Round, historical market). KXNHLPRES pays if the team wins the Presidents' Trophy, ties in points broken by regulation wins, then regulation-plus-overtime wins, total wins, head-to-head points, goal differential and goals scored; KXNHLATLANTIC/METROPOLITAN/CENTRAL/PACIFIC pay if the team wins its division (no tiebreak text); KXNHLSEASONPTS pays if the team earns at least the stated standings points (e.g. 95, greater_or_equal), loser points included; KXNHLWSTREAK pays if the team has the longest regular-season winning streak, shared longest streaks paying $1/(number tied) rounded down; KXNHLRECORDWORST pays on the worst record after league tiebreaks, then dead heat 1/N. KXNHL4NATIONS (historical, finalized) paid if the named country won the 4 Nations Face-Off. Source of truth is the NHL's official standings, streak records and playoff/tournament results; no text addresses season or tournament cancellation.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NHL standings (points, RW, ROW), streak records and playoff bracket results.
variants_and_edge_cases: Mixed mechanisms in one archetype: points thresholds (KXNHLSEASONPTS), argmax over a division or the league (division winners, Presidents' Trophy, worst record), qualification (KXNHLPLAYOFF), bracket outcomes (conference, Cup, series winner) and a run-length extremum (KXNHLWSTREAK); each needs a different functional of the same season simulation.

Tiebreaks differ by contract: KXNHLPRES lists its own six-step order, KXNHLRECORDWORST defers to league procedures then 1/N, KXNHLWSTREAK pays 1/N with no tiebreak, and division contracts have no secondary text at all.

Rules text is now recovered for every series, but most are one sentence: KXNHL, KXNHLEAST, KXNHLWEST, KXNHLPLAYOFF, KXNHLSERIES and KXNHL4NATIONS say nothing about cancellation, a shortened season or a forfeited series.

Time horizon: markets trade for months, so information (injuries, trades at the deadline, goalie form) arrives with jumps, and a team eliminated from a race resolves its contracts early only in effect, not by rule.

KXNHL4NATIONS is a finalized historical market on the February 2025 best-on-best event (Canada, USA, Sweden, Finland); it is driven by national rosters and a three-game round robin plus a one-game final, and may not recur under this ticker.
KXNHLFINALSEXACT (exact Cup final score) was re-filed to unreg:playoff_series_aggregate and is no longer modelled here.

season_awards_and_stats.label: Season awards and season player stat leaders
season_awards_and_stats.target: Winners of league awards (Hart, Vezina, Norris, Calder, etc.) or leaders/totals for season player stats.
season_awards_and_stats.mechanism: For stat markets, the outcome is rate x opportunity accumulated through the end of the season with health risk, so rest-of-season projection and competitor distribution matter. For awards, voters respond to production, team success and narrative under a specific electorate and ballot timing; a historical voter model with finalist announcements as information events is the natural structure. Both are slow, low-frequency markets where small information steps move prices.

inputs.why: To-date production and projection.
Voter pool and ballot timing determine what information can influence the award result.
A stable or rising role sustains per-game production for the rest of the season.
PP role is a stable driver of points that survives regression better than finishing.
Underlying chance quality for regression.
Finishing above skill regresses, so hot leaders should be discounted for rest-of-season projections.
Goalie awards and saves/wins leaderboards depend on goaltender quality and team defence.
Age and development priors anchor rest-of-season rate and the award narrative.
Games remaining depend on health; late injuries can end an award or leader race.
Team success correlates with award voting and with player opportunity.
Finalist and ballot dates decide when new information stops affecting the result.
Narrative-driving events can change voter preferences between close candidates.
Season totals are sums of over-dispersed per-game counts.
The core of the Jack Adams voter model and absent from the draft's player-production inputs.
Provides the first stage of the top-pick contract: which team will be on the clock.
Determines which franchise's selection a top-pick contract depends on, with conditionality evaluated on simulated standings.
Gives the second stage of the draft contracts: what the team on the clock does.
Gives the season-points contracts a market-free chain (rate, role, games played) instead of leaving them to a single-game or goals-only mechanism.
Gives the Vezina contract a goalie-specific production chain (rate, starts share, shrinkage) that skater inputs do not provide.
Supplies the rookie-specific prior and role inputs for the Calder contract that veteran production inputs lack.
Needed for the six award and stat title contracts because they resolve by voters, not by team quality.
KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS pays on the round's goal leader with 1/N ties; this simulation is the only input producing that functional.

interactions.hypothesis: Projected stat total = rest-of-season rate x games remaining x health: PP role and TOI trend determine the rate, while injury hazard determines games.
Award probability = production rank x team rank x narrative under ballot rules; finalists and ballot deadlines create step changes.
Hot finishing mean-reverts: a leader whose goals exceed ixG is likelier to slide, which interacts with the remaining schedule.

A coach's vote probability depends on over-performance conditional on adversity: a team beating projection while missing top players is valued above the same delta with a healthy roster, so injuries amplify the narrative only when the team is still above expectation.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit historical finalists on delta with an interaction with injury games lost and check coefficient sign.

interactions.hypothesis: Information after the ballot deadline cannot change the vote, so the effect of late-season form on the award is zero beyond the cut-off date, whereas before it each point of final points shifts candidate probabilities; the timing creates a threshold in the usefulness of data.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare award outcomes against standings at the ballot date versus at season end across 15 seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: The Art Ross leader is the maximum over correlated contenders: the league scoring level multiplies every contender and largely cancels in who leads, while games missed are idiosyncratic, so a two-week injury to the favourite transfers probability to the next contenders far more than a league-wide scoring drop does.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test leader probabilities with and without the common league factor and with games-played uncertainty switched off, scoring the Ross and Richard winners of past seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: Hart voters rarely pick a player whose team misses the playoffs, so for equal projected points the win probability is much lower below the playoff line; the team-strength effect acts as a gate on the candidate, not as an additive bonus.
interactions.how_to_test: In 20 seasons of Hart voting regress vote share on points with an interaction for team playoff qualification and compare with an additive model.

interactions.hypothesis: General managers voting the Vezina weight wins and save percentage, which depend on team defence and starts share as well as on goalie skill, so a strong goalie behind a weak defence or in a tandem is under-rewarded relative to his GSAx; the effect of GSAx on vote share is conditional on starts and team results.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress Vezina vote share on GSAx, starts and team points percentage with interactions over 15 seasons and compare with GSAx alone.

interactions.hypothesis: Series length is a common exposure that raises every candidate's expected goals together, but a longer series also increases the spread between top scorers and reduces tie probability, so the favourite's payout gains less from extra games than his count suggests while 1/N splits shrink.
interactions.how_to_test: In historical playoff rounds, regress the number of tied leaders and the leader's goal count on series length.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold for finalist selection
nonlinearities.why: A coach with a delta below roughly one to two standard errors of the leaders is rarely among the three finalists, so the vote probability is near zero below a threshold and rises steeply above it.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic in the projected gap to the nearest rival
nonlinearities.why: Leader probability for Art Ross is a smooth step in the projected points gap whose width is set by rest-of-season sd; once a contender leads by more than about two sds late in the season the probability saturates near one.

nonlinearities.shape: Winner-take-most: convex in vote-score lead
nonlinearities.why: Win probability depends on the candidate's rank in a multinomial over a few finalists, so small leads in the voter score translate into large win-probability gaps once the field narrows.

mechanism_review.summary: These contracts resolve through two processes. Voted awards (Hart, Norris, Calder, Vezina, Lindsay, Jack Adams) are a choice by an electorate over a few candidates: each candidate's projected end-of-season line (points, goals, ice time, goalie save quality and starts, rookie role) plus team success and narrative feeds a vote model, and coaches are judged on results versus expectation. Statistic-decided trophies (Art Ross, Rocket Richard) go to the league leader in points or goals, so the probability is the chance a player's random season total exceeds every rival's, which depends on rate, games played and the common league scoring level. Ballot deadlines, finalist announcements and injuries make step changes in information, and tie rules (1/N, league tiebreaks, shared Richard) matter near the top. A third process, the round-specific KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS contract, is a short-horizon leaderboard: the maximum of goal counts over the rosters still playing in that round, with series length as common exposure and frequent 1/N ties.

stages.name: Candidate pool and eligibility
stages.description: For each award the candidate pool is defined by eligibility and realistic contention: every head coach in office for the Jack Adams, rookies meeting the age and prior-games limits for the Calder, defencemen for the Norris, goalies for the Vezina, all skaters for Hart, Lindsay and the stat titles. Mid-season firings, injuries and trades change the pool, and early in the season the realistic pool is still wide, so the probability mass outside the top five candidates is material.
stages.distribution: Short list of 3-6 serious candidates with heavy-tailed probabilities; the remaining candidates share a small residual.

stages.name: Performance relative to expectation (coaching award)
stages.description: The award rewards over-performance: realised points percentage minus what a preseason projection predicted, the year-over-year change, and whether the team did it despite injuries or roster loss. Team strength estimates and their uncertainty determine the expected result; the outcome distribution of final points is wide (sd of 7-9 points), so a leader in November is only mildly informative about the final ranking of coaches.
stages.distribution: Final points of each team ~ Gaussian around the projection with sd 7-9; the coach ranking is the ranking of expectation gaps, so the maximum of many noisy gaps.

stages.name: Electorate, ballot timing and narrative
stages.description: Voters weigh narrative as much as the numbers: first-year coaches, turnarounds and managing through injuries; the electorate (the NHL Broadcasters' Association, verified on NHL.com award announcements; 5-3-1 points for a three-name ballot, individual ballots not published) casts ballots at the end of the regular season, so what happens in the playoffs is irrelevant and the finalist list narrows to three. Award timing introduces step changes in information when finalists are named.
stages.distribution: Multinomial choice over finalists with a few candidates holding most mass; vote shares typically spread across 3 finalists.

stages.name: Jack Adams coach-level choice model (KXNHLADAMS)
stages.description: The Jack Adams winner is one of roughly 32 head coaches (plus any coach fired or hired mid-season who ran 41+ games of a team), chosen by NHL Broadcasters' Association members on a 5-3-1 ballot cast after the regular season. The probability for each coach is a conditional (softmax) logit over all eligible coaches on his simulated final coach expectation delta (realised points pct minus preseason expectation), the change in that delta versus the prior season and a first-year-with-team flag, averaged over joint simulations of the remaining regular season from nhl.team_season_points_distribution, so correlated team outcomes and a coach's firing hazard are carried through. This is the coach branch of nhl.award_vote_share_model; it does not reuse player features. Ties settle 1/N under the KXNHLADAMS rules.
stages.distribution: Categorical over ~32 coaches; mass concentrated on 3-6 coaches with the largest positive deltas but early-season tails are wide because the final delta sd is ~0.09 points pct; winner margins can be tiny (226 vs 223 NHLBA points in 2025-26).

stages.name: Voted player awards (Hart/MVP, Norris, Calder, Vezina, Lindsay)
stages.description: Each voted player award is a vote model applied to a projected season line: skaters through points projection, ice time and power-play role, defencemen additionally through usage for the Norris, goalies through GSAx rate and starts share for the Vezina, rookies through role and pedigree for the Calder. Writers reward team success for the Hart, general managers vote the Vezina and players vote the Lindsay, whose vote shares are not known to be published, so its model rests on finalists and winners only. Missing games pushes a candidate out of contention in steps rather than linearly.
stages.distribution: Multinomial over a small candidate set with heavy-tailed vote shares; each candidate projection is a rate times games distribution with an injury left tail.

stages.name: Statistic-decided leaders (Art Ross, Rocket Richard)
stages.description: Art Ross and Rocket Richard pay the player with the most regular-season points or goals, so a contender's probability is the share of simulated seasons in which his banked total plus a random rest-of-season count beats every rival's. All contenders must be simulated jointly: the league scoring level shifts everyone together and largely cancels, while games missed and individual rate uncertainty decide the leader. Richard is goals-only (shot volume times shooting talent), Ross is points; ties at the top are resolved by the league tiebreak for Ross and by a shared award for Richard.
stages.distribution: Leader identity: categorical over 3-8 contenders from the maximum of correlated compound counts; tie mass at the top of order a few percent for goals, smaller for points.

stages.name: Playoff-round goal leader (KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS)
stages.description: For a single playoff round the goal leader is the player with the most goals across that series (for the Finals, two rosters only). Each skater's goals are his per-game goal rate (shots x finishing x opposing goalie, PP role) times the number of games he plays, and the number of games is the shared, random series length (4-7) that scales every candidate together; injuries and lineup changes during the series alter exposure. With low totals, ties at the maximum are frequent and settle 1/N, while a player who enters no game of the round is settled at a fair market price.
stages.distribution: Per-player goals are overdispersed Poisson-gamma over 4-7 games (leaders typically 3-5); the maximum over roughly 36 skaters has large tie mass, so the payoff distribution includes fractional 1/N outcomes.

coaching_scheme.note: Jack Adams path: stage s4 coach-level conditional logit on nhl.coach_expectation_delta (coach branch of nhl.award_vote_share_model), NHLBA electorate.

game_context_script.note: Single-game scripts average out over a season; team success, which voters reward, enters through nhl.ratings and the coach expectation delta rather than through any within-game state.

opponent_matchup.note: All contracts resolve on season-long totals or votes; opponents average out over 82 games and no pairing between teams or players decides any of them.

environment.note: Rink, weather and travel conditions have no direct effect on an award vote or a season or playoff-round leaderboard beyond their small influence on team results, which the ratings already contain.

pace_volume.note: Rate times games and ice time drive the stat-title races and skater award projections.

efficiency_conversion.note: Goalie GSAx and skater finishing convert volume into the goals and save numbers that decide Richard and Vezina.

officiating_rules.note: Officiating has no direct bearing on a vote or a season leaderboard beyond power-play volume already inside the player projections; the rule-like elements are eligibility and tiebreaks, handled as settlement inputs.
