required_data.timestamp_requirement: Daily snapshots; preseason projection frozen before the season.

required_data.dataset: Award history with finalists and winners
required_data.timestamp_requirement: After the announcements.

required_data.dataset: Rookie prior-league statistics and Calder eligibility
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Dated ranking snapshots.

required_data.dataset: Player game logs for leaderboard simulation
required_data.timestamp_requirement: All games before the contract date; injury status as of the same date.
required_data.history_needed: Three seasons for rate priors; ten seasons of games missed for the hazard.

required_data.dataset: Playoff series player goal logs and series state
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Only games completed before the market timestamp; lineups as announced pregame.
required_data.history_needed: Playoffs since 2009-10 for round-leader calibration and tie frequency.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Each series pays YES if the named person wins the named 2026-27 NHL award: voted awards KXNHLHART (and its title-only duplicate KXNHLMVP), KXNHLNORRIS, KXNHLCALDER, KXNHLVEZINA, KXNHLLINDSAY (player-voted) and KXNHLADAMS (coach), and statistic-decided trophies KXNHLROSS (points leader) and KXNHLRICHARD (goals leader). Where the secondary text is sampled (Adams, Calder, Lindsay, Norris, Richard, Ross, Vezina), a tie for the award pays Yes $1/N rounded down to the cent and No $1 minus that; the sampled Hart text carries no tie clause. Settlement follows the league's announced winner, so whether a league tiebreak (Art Ross) precedes the 1/N rule is not stated. KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS (historical, 'Playoffs Goal Leader (by Round)') pays YES if the named player records the most goals in the specified playoff round (sampled: the 2026 Stanley Cup Finals); a player who enters no game of that round resolves at a fair market price, and tied leaders pay $1/N rounded down.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NHL award announcements (league and voting bodies, NHLPA for Lindsay) and official NHL regular-season statistics for Art Ross and Rocket Richard.
variants_and_edge_cases: Voted versus counted: Hart, Norris, Calder and Vezina are decided by voters (writers; general managers for Vezina), Lindsay by players, Jack Adams by broadcasters (to be verified, aw2), while Art Ross and Rocket Richard go to the statistical leader, so two different generating processes share this archetype.

Ties: Rocket Richard has been shared when players tied in goals, so the 1/N clause is live for it; Art Ross uses a league tiebreak (more goals first, from memory) so a shared award is rare; voted-award ties are rare; the sampled Hart text has no tie clause at all.
Coach award: a head coach can be fired or replaced mid-season, a case the sampled text does not address (interim coaches' eligibility unspecified).

Timing: ballots for voted awards are cast at the end of the regular season and winners announced weeks later, so playoff results do not matter, while stat titles are fixed at the last regular-season game.
KXNHLMVP is a title-only duplicate of KXNHLHART with no listed markets; if it lists, it must be priced identically to Hart for the same player.

KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS is a round-specific playoff goal-leader contract (sampled on the 2026 Finals, historical): the candidate pool is the two finalists' rosters, exposure is the unknown series length, and multi-way ties at the top are common, so 1/N settlement is a large part of the payoff.

player_h2h.label: Player head-to-head comparisons
player_h2h.target: Whether player A records more of a stat (points, shots, saves) than player B, with tie and DNP rules per the contract.
player_h2h.mechanism: The outcome is the sign of the difference of two correlated count variables. Expected values come from the single-player models (TOI, rates, role, opponent), correlation comes from the shared game environment (same team: script, goalie; opponents: opposing script), and ties are common for small counts so tie handling heavily influences prices. Lineup news on either player can void or flip the comparison.

inputs.why: Minutes of each player by state.
Per-60 shot rates are the base for comparing two players on shots on goal.
Chance quality for points/goals comparisons.
Difference in PP roles gives one player a large share of the high-yield minutes.
Linemate and deployment differences.
Players face different opponents or positions; the matchup difference shifts the expected gap.
Opposing goalie for each player.
Correlation between the two players' counts.
Distribution for tie probability.
Either player's lineup news (linemate absence, injury) shifts the comparison.
The contract may void or settle on a scratched player, which changes the effective probability.
Tie handling and DNP treatment decide who wins ties, which are common for small counts.
Trailing teams shoot more; leading teams protect leads, shifting both players' volume.
Provides the exact difference distribution and tie mass that the head-to-head contract settles on.
The positive correlation of linemates is the main reason a teammate comparison is tighter than an opponent comparison with equal means.
For a points comparison the credit share relative to team on-ice goals separates roles with equal TOI, e.g. a playmaking centre versus a defenceman on the same line.
For a shots comparison the share of team volume is more stable than raw per-60 rate and controls for the opponent shot volume that both players share.
A goalie comparison needs each goalie's exposure distribution: pulled or non-playing goalies drive tie and void probability.
Two opposing goalies face different opponents; the saves difference is dominated by the difference in opponent SOG-for volumes.
Gives the contract a market-free script latent (state mixture and entering-state matrix) so that benchmark prices remain an independent yardstick.

interactions.hypothesis: Teammate comparisons: shared game script and linemates mean correlation reduces difference variance; opposing players have different correlation sign via script.
Tie probability matters for small-count stats: with discrete means small, P(tie) can be large; the rules decide who wins ties.
PP roles: the comparison hinges on who gets PP minutes, so penalty expectation interacts with each player's PP slot.

The correlation between the two players' counts changes sign with pair type: linemates share goals and script so rho is positive and the difference has low variance, whereas opponents share pace but face opposed script so rho is near zero or negative; a pooled correlation misprices both.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate rho separately for same-line, same-team, and opposing pairs and compare out-of-sample deviance with a pooled value.

interactions.hypothesis: Tie mass of the difference is a function of the two marginal means: when both players expect counts near zero (points for depth players, saves with few shots) the tie mass is large and the contract mostly prices P(A>B) against a big atom; as means grow the atom shrinks, so the same mean gap implies a larger win probability for high-volume pairs.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin pairs by the sum of expected counts and compare the empirical tie share and P(A>B | no tie) with the fitted discrete difference; how a tie settles is a separate rule question (hh1) and is not tested here.

interactions.hypothesis: If both players are on the same power-play unit they receive the same power-play opportunities, so penalty-count uncertainty shifts both counts together and mostly cancels in the difference, whereas for players on different units it adds variance of opposite effect; unit overlap decides whether penalty uncertainty matters for the contract.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare variance of D for same-unit and different-unit pairs conditional on penalties.

interactions.hypothesis: On a linemate pair the same goal credits both, so points are positively dependent in a way that depends on each player's credit share; for a playmaker versus a shooter the co-credit probability is high and the difference is rarely large.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the distribution of D for linemates with the independent-count prediction and estimate the co-credit term.

interactions.hypothesis: A lineup change that moves one player down a line or off the PP crosses a threshold in expected TOI that reverses the sign of the expected difference; the priced effect is a step at confirmation time rather than a gradual drift.
interactions.how_to_test: Measure the change in difference in expected counts at lineup confirmations and the resulting change in the outcome probability.

nonlinearities.shape: Spike at zero in a discrete difference
nonlinearities.why: For small counts the pmf of the difference has a sharp peak at zero, so the win probability for A is not a smooth function of the difference in means near equality; a normal approximation misstates the tie mass.

nonlinearities.shape: Pair-type dependent with sign change
nonlinearities.why: Correlation is positive for linemates and near zero or negative for opponents, so the variance of the difference is a non-monotone function of pair type, and a constant correlation parameter is not valid.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise with PP minutes weighted more heavily
nonlinearities.why: A shift of one PP minute between players changes the expected count by much more than an even-strength minute, so differences in total TOI are less informative than differences in PP minutes.

mechanism_review.summary: A head-to-head contract compares two counts, so the outcome is the sign of D = X_A - X_B, and the relevant object is the joint distribution of the pair, not the two marginals. Each marginal comes from a single-player model: minutes by state, per-minute rate and credit structure for points, shot volume and conversion for shots, exposure and shot flow for saves. The pair is then coupled through shared factors: teammates share script, goalie, linemates and goals; opponents share pace and have opposed scripts; two linemates also co-earn points on the same goal. The discrete difference has large tie mass for low counts, so the tie rule and the DNP rule (both unobserved, no series exists) would change the contract's probability by several points. Lineup news on either player can void the comparison or flip the sign of the expected difference.

stages.name: Participation and lineup state for both players
stages.description: The contract is defined only if both players take part, and the rule for a non-playing player (void, fair price or loss) determines how much availability risk is priced. Lineup news on either player changes roles: a linemate's absence promotes one and not the other, and an injury during the game truncates one count. The joint availability states (both play, A only, B only, neither) have separate distributions of D.
stages.distribution: Four joint participation states with probabilities mostly concentrated on both-play; the remaining mass is a fair-price or void component set by the rule.

stages.name: Marginal expectation and dispersion of each player's stat
stages.description: Each player's mean comes from a single-player model: for skater points on-ice goal exposure and the credit share, for skater shots team volume and shot share, for goalies shot flow and exposure minutes. Role differences such as PP1 membership produce much of the gap in expected counts between two similarly rated players. Dispersion differs across stats and roles and determines the tie mass and the spread of D.
stages.distribution: Marginals: points zero-inflated NB with mean 0.4-1.2; shots NB with mean 1.5-4 and dispersion 1.3-1.8; goalie saves NB with mean 24-30.

stages.name: Dependence between the two counts
stages.description: For two teammates the counts share the game's script, the goalie they face and, for points, the very same goals (a linemate scores and the other is assisted), so correlation is positive and the variance of D is lower than the sum of variances. For opponents the shared pace gives mild positive correlation in shots while the opposed script creates negative correlation (the leader's player loses minutes and shots), and goalies on opposing sides have saves that move with the same game total but with opposed script. The sign and size of correlation depends on pair type.
stages.distribution: Bivariate discrete dependence with pair-type-specific correlation: teammates rho about +0.2 to +0.4 for points, opponents rho about -0.05 to +0.1; shared goals produce joint jumps.

stages.name: Difference distribution, tie mass and contract probability
stages.description: The probability of a win for A is P(D>0) possibly renormalised by the tie rule; with small means the discrete mass at D=0 is large, so the distinction between P(A>B) and P(A>B | no tie) is of the order of the price itself. The model must therefore produce an exact pmf of D from the joint count model rather than a normal approximation to the difference of means.
stages.distribution: Discrete pmf of D with a spike at zero; tie probability about 30-40 percent for points, 12-20 percent for shots, about 7-9 percent for goalie saves.

environment.note: Both players compete in the same rink on the same night, so rink, weather and altitude effects cancel in a difference, and the residual arena effect is common to both players' counts.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching changes act on the two players through their lines and PP units, which are modelled directly as role inputs; coach identity is the same for teammates and enters opposing pairs only through team context.

officiating_rules.note: Referee crew affects power plays for both teams; the pair's relative PP exposure is already captured by PP role and unit overlap, so a separate officiating feature adds nothing for the difference.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and standings stakes affect whether a player plays, handled by the availability inputs; conditional on playing, schedule has no pair-specific effect on the difference.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Features from games before the as-of date.

required_data.dataset: Goal events with credit and on-ice skaters
required_data.timestamp_requirement: As recorded after the game.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Store vintages; the official lineup at warmups.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Prior games.

contract_review.settlement_definition: No live Kalshi series exists for NHL player head-to-head, so there is no rules text. The blueprint describes a contract that pays YES if player A records more of a named stat (points, shots on goal or saves) than player B in the listed game, with tie handling and the treatment of a non-playing player to be set by the rules. By analogy to the live prop ladders a skater who is active but never enters would settle at the last fair price; whether a tie is a push, a No, or a fair-price void is unknown, and that single rule changes the effective probability materially.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Assumed: official NHL box score player statistics (points, shots on goal, saves); rule for ties and non-participation unobserved.
variants_and_edge_cases: Tie treatment: for low-count stats (points, saves of goalies with few shots against) a tie is likely, a large share of pairs for points (the magnitude is an unsourced guess, to be measured); if ties settle No, the contract is about P(A>B) not P(A>B | no tie), and each reading changes fair price by several points.

Pair composition: teammates (shared script, goalie, goals) versus opponents (opposing script, shared pace) have correlation of opposite sign, so the same marginal means give different outcome probabilities by pair type.

Stat type: points (credit-based, discrete, zero-heavy), shots on goal (volume count, overdispersed) and saves (goalie exposure) have different distributions; goalies as opponents also face the exposure and pull rules.
Participation: either player not playing or leaving early (injury after one shift) needs a stated rule; the blueprint says DNP rules per contract, none observed.

parlay_combo.label: Parlay / combo contracts
parlay_combo.target: Joint outcome of multiple legs (team results, totals, player stats) in one contract.
parlay_combo.mechanism: The contract price must equal the joint probability, which depends on marginal accuracy of each leg and on common latent drivers: game pace, script, goalie quality shocks and lineup changes. Positive correlations (team win and own player's points) make the joint probability exceed the product of marginals, negative correlations the opposite, and leg-void rules change the effective payoff. Modelling this requires a game-level simulation that generates all legs from shared latent variables.

inputs.why: Empirical and simulated correlation between legs.
Marginal distributions per leg.
Latent game script shared across legs.
Team and total goals correlation.
A goalie change shifts opposing scoring, totals and win legs in a correlated manner.
A late scratch changes several legs simultaneously, so lineup state is a shared latent factor.
Team scoring level for the goal-related legs.
Opponent scoring drives the totals and win legs in the opposite direction from own scoring.
Player volume for player legs.
Each leg's settlement and whether a voided leg reduces the combo changes the payoff structure.
Leg-level prices in the ladder must be consistent before combining; inconsistent legs give spurious edge.
Forms the bridge between team-goal legs and player-stat legs so that win, total and points legs come from the same simulated goals.
Provides the joint discrete shocks across legs; voided legs and shifted marginals happen on these same states.
Corrects the Gaussian-correlation shortcut that is the main source of error in joint tails.
Determines what the combo is worth when a leg voids, which can swing price by more than any modelling edge.
Prevents impossible or double-counted combinations in the combo price.
Provides the shared score-path latent for all legs from ratings only, so the benchmark prices stay an independent yardstick.

interactions.hypothesis: Team win x player points: the correlation is via team goals; conditioning on total expectation and the player's PP share sets the joint uplift over independence.
Goalie shock moves all legs in the same direction (opposing scoring, totals, win legs); correlated shocks need a latent goalie-quality variable.
Script-based negative correlation: favourite wins by large margins reduce its stars' late shots, so a win leg and a shots leg are less correlated than assumed.

P(team wins and star records 2+ points) is much larger than the product of marginals because a win by two or more requires goals and the star is credited on a share of them; the uplift is convex in the number of team goals and falls when blowouts compress the star's minutes.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(win and points>=2) by team goals bins and compare with the product and with the simulation.

interactions.hypothesis: Hypothesis only: a backup goalie start and a missing star skater on the same team may be linked through back-to-back scheduling and would then move the team win, total and player legs together, so the joint probability of lineup states would not be the product of marginals; the size of the link is not evidenced and should be estimated before use.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the odds ratio between backup-goalie starts and star absences on back-to-backs versus rested games from 5 seasons of lineup data; set the joint tree to independent if the ratio is within noise of one.

interactions.hypothesis: In the blowout regime (margin three or more) the legs on total, margin and star points are strongly dependent, whereas in the centre the dependence is weak; a single correlation parameter underprices the tail combinations that parlays most often bundle.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit conditional exceedance for pairs at u = 0.8 and 0.9 and compare to the central-correlation Gaussian prediction.

interactions.hypothesis: The relation between a goalie's saves leg and the game total leg is non-monotone: high pace lifts both, but a weak goalie lifts the total and lowers saves, so the sign of dependence depends on which latent factor drives the game.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress saves on total goals separately within bins of goalie save percentage shock and of opponent shot volume.

interactions.hypothesis: The payoff after a void depends on the map; with nested or implied legs a void can make a leg redundant and change which legs are binding, so the effective probability depends jointly on the map and the logical relations.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute combo price under each candidate void map and flag combos for which the maps differ by more than a tick.

interactions.hypothesis: Win and star shots legs are negatively linked only in the blowout regime where the leader's stars lose minutes; below a two-goal lead there is no link, so the dependence is a threshold in the lead.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the correlation between team win margin and star SOG for margins below two versus three or more.

nonlinearities.shape: Tail-dependent, stronger in the upper tail
nonlinearities.why: Combined events such as large win margin with high total with star points occur in a small set of high-scoring games, so joint exceedance probabilities grow faster than a constant correlation implies.

nonlinearities.shape: Hypothesised piecewise: star minutes may fall only beyond a two-goal margin (threshold to be estimated)
nonlinearities.why: Compression of stars' minutes appears in blowouts only, creating a kink in the relation between margin and star counts and a negative dependence regime absent in close games.

nonlinearities.shape: Error amplification across legs
nonlinearities.why: Probability errors on each leg multiply in an intersection, so a five percent relative error per leg becomes about 20 percent over four legs; the effect is multiplicative in log-probability, not additive.

mechanism_review.summary: The fair price of a combo is the probability of an intersection, which equals the product of marginals times a dependence factor that depends on shared latent drivers. In an NHL game those drivers are few and identifiable: the goal intensity of each team (pace and quality), the goalie states (starter identity and a within-game quality shock including pulls), the number of power plays, the lineup state of key skaters, and the score path that decides empty-net goals and minutes compression. Player legs follow from team goals via an allocation of goals and assists to the skaters on ice, so the right architecture is one game-level simulation that draws latent states, generates team goal events, allocates credit to players, and reads all legs from the same draw. Dependence is not constant: it grows in the tails (blowouts), switches sign for some leg pairs (goalie saves versus totals), and mis-specification compounds because errors in each leg multiply. Settlement of voided legs changes the payoff structure.

stages.name: Leg catalogue and logical structure
stages.description: Each leg is a threshold on a game statistic: win, margin, total, a team's total, a skater's goals, assists, points or shots, a goalie's saves. Some legs imply or exclude each other: points of two or more imply points of one, a team's win excludes the opponent's win, and a team total over implies a minimum for the game total. These deterministic relations determine part of the joint probability exactly and must be imposed before any correlation is estimated.
stages.distribution: Deterministic implications and exclusions among discrete legs; no free parameter, only structural constraints.

stages.name: Shared latent game drivers
stages.description: The legs are tied by a small set of latent variables: total goal intensity (pace times shot quality), goal differential driven by team strength and script, goalie quality shocks (including an early pull), and the number of power plays. A positive shock to total intensity lifts goals, assists and totals together, while a goalie shock moves the opposing team's scoring and the goalie's own saves in different directions. Their joint distribution defines the correlation structure of all legs.
stages.distribution: Low-dimensional latent vector with heavy tails: goal intensity lognormal-like, goalie shock mixture (normal game versus pulled), power plays Poisson.

stages.name: Conditional player legs given team goals
stages.description: Given the simulated team goals and strength states, each goal is allocated to skaters on the ice with probabilities set by their shot shares and credit shares, so a skater's goals, assists and points are conditional on the team's goals and on his minutes. This creates the positive correlation between a team's win leg and its star's points leg and between team total and player points, and it respects the maximum of three points per goal. Minutes compression in blowouts adds a negative link between margin and star shot counts.
stages.distribution: Allocation is multinomial per goal; conditional on g team goals, a skater's points are a thinned binomial-like count with credit probability near 0.6-0.8 for top forwards.

stages.name: Lineup scenarios and settlement mapping
stages.description: Lineup states are discrete and correlated across legs: a starter goalie change or a star scratch moves several legs at once, and a non-playing prop leg may be voided. The scenario tree gives joint probabilities of these states at the contract's decision time. Payoff then depends on the settlement map for voided legs, which changes the combo from an intersection into a conditional-intersection contract.
stages.distribution: Discrete scenario tree with 4-12 leaves; payoff map piecewise over leg statuses (win, lose, void).

opponent_matchup.note: Matchups between specific teams and players are properties of each leg's marginal model; the combo adds nothing matchup-specific beyond the shared latent drivers, which are captured by team means in the simulation.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching effects enter each leg through team rates, lines and minutes, already part of the marginal leg models; a combo contract does not add a separate coaching mechanism beyond what is in its legs.

environment.note: Rink and travel effects act through team means of each leg and are common across legs in the same game, so they affect the marginals but not the dependence structure beyond what team means carry.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and standings stakes affect lineup and strength states that the scenario tree and team means already carry; no combo-specific schedule mechanism exists.

officiating_rules.note: Referee tendencies shift penalty counts which are part of the shared latent drivers; the combo adds no officiating mechanism of its own beyond the leg-level rules.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Known after games; training only on past games relative to as-of date.

contract_review.settlement_definition: No live NHL parlay or combo series appears in the ledger, so there is no rules text. The blueprint describes a single contract that pays only if every named leg (team result, spread, total, player stat) occurs in the same game or slate; its fair price is the joint probability of all legs. Whether a voided or fair-priced leg (for example a non-playing skater) removes the leg, collapses the combo to a fair price or settles it No is unknown and is the single most important settlement unknown, since a prop leg in an NHL game has a non-trivial chance of being voided at fair price under sibling rules. All dependence machinery below (credit kernel, copula, scenario tree) is conditional on the unverified assumption that combos bundle legs of the SAME game; if Kalshi combos are cross-game or cross-sport collections of existing markets, the required inputs reduce to leg marginals, leg logical relations and the void payoff map (pc5).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Per-leg official NHL game and player statistics; combo-level resolution rules unobserved.
variants_and_edge_cases: Leg void handling: sibling prop rules settle an active-but-never-enters player at the last fair price; if a combo inherits this, the contract payoff after a void is a different function of the remaining legs, not simply the product of the others.

Logically related legs: nested ladder rungs (points 2+ inside points 1+), a team win with the opponent's spread, or a team total leg with the game total leg are not independent and some combinations are impossible, so the pricing must respect implications and exclusions.

Same-game versus cross-game combos: legs from different games are independent except for shared news, whereas same-game legs share latent game drivers; the structure of the contract decides which model is needed.

Leg settlement differences: a shootout adds one goal to totals and team totals but affects margins differently, and third-period legs exclude overtime; each leg inherits its own rule, so a combo is only as clean as its worst-defined leg.

offfield_markets.label: Non-hockey and office/personnel markets
offfield_markets.target: Event in the league or organization outside the game (transactions, announcements, business questions).
offfield_markets.mechanism: These markets are driven by organizational decisions and news flow, not on-ice performance; there is little statistical structure and the best-supported hypotheses are reference-class base rates, calendar constraints (deadlines, draft, free agency) and insider-report timing relative to the stated resolution source. Many of these markets are effectively unpredictable from sports data and should be treated as novelty markets.

inputs.why: Reference-class frequency is the prior for novelty markets with no statistical model.
Fixed league dates bound when events can occur and concentrate hazard near them.
Insider reporting and official announcements.
Resolution source and wording.
Price reaction after reports shows how much information the market assigned to the news.
Thin volume means quoted prices are noisy, which limits any inference from them.
Close time relative to the event date defines how much of the hazard is inside the window.
Other venues' prices on the same event provide a cross-check when they exist.
Historical realized frequency for this market type provides a calibration check on listed strikes.
Sets the support of the destination distribution and the timing of movement for the next-team contract.
Provides the probability vector across teams that the contract's partition requires.
Defines whether the formal decision step can occur inside the window, which dominates the probability for the expansion contract.
Controls the weight to put on news in markets that settle only on official events.

The Ted Lindsay Award is voted by an electorate different from the writers' awards, so the vote-share model must be fit separately with peer-vote proxies, but the same structure (finalists, production, team success, reputation) applies.
Gives the season-points contracts a market-free chain (rate, role, games played) instead of leaving them to a single-game or goals-only mechanism.
Replaces the audited-WEAK pooled base rate by per-class hazards so that rare-event markets have a defined central quantity.
KXNHLRETIRE settles on a qualifying retirement announcement before the season start; this hazard is the input that generates it.
KXNHLNEXTGM settles on which person is named GM of the club before the date; the candidate pool is the outcome space.

interactions.hypothesis: Base rate x time remaining: hazard rises toward deadline dates, so reference-class frequency must be time-conditioned.
Insider report to official announcement: price after reports measures their credibility and the rules decide what counts.
Thin liquidity makes quotes noisy; volume interacts with price moves to separate information from noise.

Hazard is concentrated at calendar points (free agency opening, trade windows, Board meetings), so the probability of an event inside a window is the sum of mass at the dated gates inside it, not a constant hazard times duration.
interactions.how_to_test: Build the calendar of gate dates inside the window and compare realised event timing over past seasons with a constant-hazard model.

interactions.hypothesis: A report of an agreement raises probability, but the contract settles only on an official step and a lag between the two, so the effect depends on the credibility of the source and on whether the official step falls before the contract closes.
interactions.how_to_test: Label past reports by type and measure the share followed by the official action within the window length.

interactions.hypothesis: A destination needs both a feasible contract status (consent, expiry, window) and a suitor with space and need; the probability for a team is the product of feasibility and fit, so a team with ideal fit but a closed window has nearly zero probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised destinations with the product of feasibility and fit scores versus fit alone over past star moves.

interactions.hypothesis: Expansion before the deadline requires an expansion process to have reached a Board vote; unless a meeting with the vote is scheduled inside the window the probability is near zero, a threshold on the governance stage rather than a gradual hazard.
interactions.how_to_test: Record the stage of past expansion bids at each month before announcement and compare with the time to the Board vote.

interactions.hypothesis: An expired contract without an offer turns a moderate age hazard into a high one, whereas a signed final year keeps a veteran playing almost regardless of age; the retirement probability jumps at the contract-expiry state rather than rising smoothly with age.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the retirement hazard with and without an age x contract-years interaction on 33+ players since 2005 and compare log loss.

nonlinearities.shape: Spiked hazard at dated gates
nonlinearities.why: Free agency opening and trade deadlines produce a very high short-term hazard compared with the remainder of the window, so the probability of a change of team is a step function of calendar position, not linear in time.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in proximity to contract expiry
nonlinearities.why: The probability a player moves rises sharply in the final contract year and at the free-agency date; years remaining is a convex, non-linear predictor, and clauses create hard zeros for non-consenting destinations.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic in report type and source reliability
nonlinearities.why: A report of agreed terms from a reliable source moves the probability close to one while a report of talks barely moves it; the map from report to probability is sigmoid in a credibility score.

mechanism_review.summary: These markets are not produced by on-ice play; they are produced by institutions with calendars, constraints and information channels. For a destination market the outcome is a draw from a discrete set of teams constrained by the player's contract status (expiry year, no-move clauses, signing windows), by the cap space and needs of potential suitors, and by the time window; the default is the status quo and the main hazard is concentrated at a few calendar points. For a governance event like expansion the outcome requires a formal board decision after preparatory steps (city readiness, ownership, arena, fee, announced timeline), so the event is gated by the calendar of meetings. In all cases information arrives through insider reports that are informative but not settling events, so the model must weight credibility and lag between report and official announcement. Retirement and GM-hire markets add two person-level processes: an age- and contract-driven retirement hazard before a season deadline, and a candidate choice by a club's leadership once a GM vacancy exists.

stages.name: Event class and reference-class hazard
stages.description: Each contract is first placed in a reference class with its own base rate: a star defenceman changing teams within a given window, a league expanding within a year, a veteran of a given age and contract status retiring before a season, a vacant GM chair being filled by a given candidate type. The reference class must be narrow because pooling destination, governance and voting events gives meaningless base rates. The hazard inside the window depends on how many calendar events fall within it.
stages.distribution: Rare event with a time-varying hazard; for destination markets the base probability of a move inside a short window is a few percent for incumbents under contract and high for free agents at the market open.

stages.name: Institutional gates and constraints
stages.description: A player can only move if his contract allows it: expiry, no-trade and no-move lists, signing windows and arbitration status define the set of feasible destinations; suitors need cap space and roster room. An expansion award needs a Board of Governors approval after an expansion process, which is only possible at a scheduled meeting or special session. The contract wording decides what counts (official announcement, signing, not reports).
stages.distribution: Feasible-set logic: the destination distribution is supported on a subset of teams; governance outcomes are gated binary events conditional on a meeting.

stages.name: Information flow from insiders to official announcements
stages.description: Public reports from league insiders arrive before official announcements and move beliefs, but their reliability varies by reporter and report type (pending talks versus agreed terms); the lag between the report and the official step determines how much of the hazard is realised inside the contract window. Rules requiring an official announcement make unconfirmed reports non-settling.
stages.distribution: Bayesian update with report-specific likelihood ratios; lag between report and announcement ranges from hours to months with heavy tails.

stages.name: Personal career and front-office decisions (retirement, GM hire)
stages.description: KXNHLRETIRE is a single person's decision before a deadline: the hazard rises with age, an expiring or expired contract, declining production or chronic injury, and falls with milestones still within reach and a signed contract year left; statements by player and agent are informative but only a qualifying announcement settles. KXNHLNEXTGM is a choice among a small candidate pool once a vacancy exists: internal assistant GMs, former GMs and executives tied to the club president or owner; the hire timing follows the search process, and insider reports of interviews and finalists move probabilities.
stages.distribution: Retirement is Bernoulli with a strongly age-dependent hazard that is concentrated in the off-season; the GM market is a categorical over a handful of named candidates plus a long 'other' tail, with timing mass after season end or a firing.

talent_strength.note: Only through the retirement contract: declining production lowers the value of continuing and raises the retirement hazard.

coaching_scheme.note: None of the contracts depend on on-ice tactics or coaching systems; the destination of a player can be influenced by a coach, but only as part of the news signal.

environment.note: Venue and travel conditions do not drive a transaction, a retirement, a GM hire or a governance decision; the only environmental factor is arena readiness for expansion, handled in the governance input.

game_context_script.note: No game state or score path affects these events, which resolve through institutional processes rather than within-game play.

pace_volume.note: There is no counting process of plays or shots behind these contracts; the only volume-like quantity is the number of calendar opportunities in the window, covered by the calendar input.

efficiency_conversion.note: No conversion rate (shooting, saving) settles these contracts; a veteran's declining production enters only the retirement hazard, carried under talent_strength.

officiating_rules.note: No on-ice officiating applies; the rules that matter are the settlement text and league governance procedures, covered under the contract and governance inputs.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Four unrelated event types share this archetype. KXNHLNEXTTEAM pays YES for the named team if it is the player's next team before the stated date (the sample is 'before Nov 1, 2026'); a player who retires or has no team resolves a 'Retires / No Team' contract, a player who remains on his issuance team resolves that team, and signing with any team including the previous one after free agency counts. KXNHLEXPANSION pays YES if the NHL officially announces an expansion franchise award to a named city before Jan 1, 2027, requiring formal approval naming the city. KXNHLRETIRE (historical) pays YES if the named player announces his NHL retirement before the stated season start date, the retirement intended to be effective immediately or before the next season. KXNHLNEXTGM (historical) pays YES for the named person if he is appointed, elected, named, designated or succeeded to the named team's General Manager position before the stated date (sample: Toronto, before Nov 1, 2026). Neither text addresses interim titles or later reversals.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NHL announcements for expansion awards and club announcements for GM appointments; NHL transaction records for next team; the player's or club's official retirement announcement for KXNHLRETIRE.
variants_and_edge_cases: Four different generating processes: a transaction destination (partition over 32 teams plus retire/no team), a governance event (expansion approval by the Board of Governors), a personal career decision (retirement announcement before a season) and a front-office hire (partition over GM candidates), so no single base rate covers them.

Next-team window: the sampled market is 'before Nov 1, 2026', a date already passed on the review date (Nov 7, 2026), so the sample is stale or expired; the text 'is a free agent ... for any period of time' means a re-signing with the same team counts as YES for that team after free agency.
Expansion contract requires the announcement to come after market issuance and to name the city; relocation counts only if designated expansion, and the team need not begin play before the date.

KXNHLRETIRE: an announcement effective after the next season (a farewell season) does not count; KXNHLNEXTGM: 'designated' or 'succeeded' is broad enough that an interim appointment might settle YES, which the text does not resolve.

team_and_player_season_counting.label: NHL season point/goal totals and counting leaders
team_and_player_season_counting.target: A player's season total (goals, points) or team points relative to a threshold.
team_and_player_season_counting.mechanism: Season totals are games played times per-game rates, where rates depend on ice time, power-play role, linemates and shot quality, and games played depend on injury hazard. Over-dispersion and age curves matter; early-season to-date totals are weak evidence relative to talent priors.

inputs.why: Count distributions over a season.
Time on ice by strength state.
Power-play unit role multiplies even-strength ice time into points; PP1 players earn a large share of their totals there.
Individual expected goals rate.
Finishing talent versus luck: shrunk shooting percentage predicts goals better than raw totals over a season.
Line combinations determine linemates and ice time, so a promotion or demotion shifts the whole scoring rate.
Playing with elite centres or wingers raises assist and goal rates independent of the player's own talent.
Age curves set the expected change in rate from last season: young players rise and veterans decline on average.
Shot-attempt rate per 60 is the most stable component of goal scoring and anchors the projection.
Opportunity cap for all player season counting contracts, and the source of the left tail of the goal total.
The only contract in the archetype that depends on a run-length extremum rather than a total.
Common scale factor for season goals; failing to model it overstates certainty across all player thresholds.
The team points threshold includes the one-point extra-time losses, which are a partly random stream, so its rate and conditional win share determine the points distribution at a given win rate.

Team point totals and division and streak contracts depend on rating uncertainty: ignoring the spread of true strength understates the chance of an upset in the points race and of an unexpected long streak.
Gives the season-points contracts a market-free chain (rate, role, games played) instead of leaving them to a single-game or goals-only mechanism.
Supplies the schedule-path driver for longest-streak and division-race contracts that rating-only simulation ignores.
Defines the team-level chain (ratings to points to division and threshold) that this record previously used without definition.

interactions.hypothesis: Power-play share multiplies even-strength time on ice into points.
Expected goals with shrunk finishing talent beats raw goals for season totals.
Age declines show first in ice time, then production.

A season goal total equals games played times goals per game, so uncertainty in games and in rate multiply; a 60-goal pace needs both near-full health and a high rate, so the threshold probability is much lower than the product of marginal 'pace' and 'health' intuitions.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(>=60) by simulation with and without games-played variability and compare with a fixed-82-game model.

interactions.hypothesis: To-date goals above expected regress toward the xG-based talent, and the amount of regression depends on shots taken so far: with about 40 shots to date the prior should dominate and the to-date shooting percentage should be almost ignored.
interactions.how_to_test: Test predictive weight on to-date shooting percentage as a function of shots taken in rolling seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: The league scoring multiplier applies to all players simultaneously, so thresholds on goals for different stars move together; this makes cross-player outcomes positively correlated and a common-factor error mis-prices all goal ladders in the same direction.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate year-to-year league scoring change and compare with cross-player residual correlation in goals.

interactions.hypothesis: For an extreme points target (e.g. 110 for a defenceman) the required rate is near the top of the posterior, so even a two-week absence or a demotion from PP1 pushes the needed rest-of-season pace beyond plausible values; the probability drops in a step once games missed or role loss crosses that point rather than declining smoothly.
interactions.how_to_test: In historical player-seasons, compare threshold attainment for top-decile scorers by games missed bucket and PP1 continuity against a model linear in games missed.

interactions.hypothesis: Goals and points for the same player share the goal-scoring rate and the league factor, so the two contracts on one player are strongly dependent; assists add a second, less persistent component whose regression toward on-ice expectation is faster than for goals, so points thresholds regress more than goal thresholds after a hot start.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare split-half reliability of goals per game and assists per game across player-seasons, and the correlation of goal and point threshold outcomes for the same players.

interactions.hypothesis: Age affects goals first through ice time and PP role (a regime change when a player loses PP1) before it affects shooting rate; the response is a regime switch at the role change, not a smooth decline.
interactions.how_to_test: Track PP1 membership by age and compare goal rate changes before and after loss of PP1.

nonlinearities.shape: S-curve near the threshold, flatter than Poisson
nonlinearities.why: The probability of reaching the threshold is a logistic-like function of the expected total whose slope is set by the total sd (Poisson about 7.7 near 60 goals, roughly 9-12 once random rate and games played are included, to be fitted), so a model's mean error of a few goals is still a large probability error near the strike.

nonlinearities.shape: Truncated at 82 with a heavy left tail
nonlinearities.why: Games played cannot exceed 82 and the downside from injuries is a long tail; the expected value understates the cost, and the contract probability depends on the full distribution, not its mean.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in the rate posterior's right tail for extreme targets
nonlinearities.why: For rare totals such as 110 points the YES probability lives in the right tail of the rate posterior, so it rises convexly with the posterior sd; underestimating rate uncertainty prices these contracts far too low.

mechanism_review.summary: Player season counting contracts are sums over a fixed schedule, so the outcome is a rate times opportunities with uncertainty in both. For a player's goal total the rate is shots per game times shooting percentage, each with a talent component and a luck component; for points the rate adds assist credit on team goals while he is on the ice. The opportunities are games played (zero-inflated by injuries and rest) and minutes (role, power-play share), and the league scoring environment shifts everyone at once. Early in the season the to-date total is only a small piece of the total, so the talent prior and the age trajectory dominate, and the threshold probability is the upper tail of a compound count with random rate and random games.

stages.name: Talent prior and rate decomposition for the player
stages.description: A player's goal rate per game equals shot volume per game times shooting percentage. Shot volume is the most stable component and is anchored by shot rate per 60 and ice time; shooting percentage regresses strongly toward a player-specific talent estimate built from xG per shot. Age curves shift both and early-season data are weighted lightly. This stage produces the rate distribution for the rest of the season, not a point estimate.
stages.distribution: Rate distribution with posterior sd of order 10-15 percent of the mean for established scorers; shooting percentage has a binomial noise component of order sd 2.5-3 points over a season.

stages.name: Opportunity: games played, minutes and power-play role
stages.description: The number of games played is capped at 82 and reduced by injury and rest; for a star, the distribution has most mass at 78-82 and a long left tail from injuries. Minutes and PP unit role set the volume per game, and PP1 membership is more persistent than even-strength points. A player on a high-scoring PP unit has a rate floor that survives regression. These opportunities convert linearly into goals once the rate is fixed.
stages.distribution: Games played: 82 minus a zero-inflated heavy-tailed missed-games count (about 10-15 percent chance of missing 15+ games for veterans).

stages.name: Accumulation, to-date information and thresholds
stages.description: The season total is goals to date plus a rest-of-season sum; with about 68 games remaining the remaining sum is a compound count with random rate and random games. A threshold such as 60 goals (floor 59.5) requires a rate near 0.75 per game over 80 games; the probability is a steep function of the mean because the Poisson sd at a mean near 60 is already about 7.7 goals and the random scoring rate and games played raise the total sd to roughly 9-12 goals, so the curve is less steep than a pure Poisson implies (the exact sd must be fitted). The league scoring environment also moves the mean for all players together.
stages.distribution: Season goals ~ negative binomial or compound Poisson with mean mu and sd about sqrt(mu) times 1.2 plus rate and games uncertainty; P(>=60) rises smoothly with mu over a wide range (a total sd near 9-12 goals, to be fitted rather than assumed).

stages.name: Settlement mapping and boundary mass
stages.description: Resolution uses official counts: goals and assists credited to the skater (shootout-deciding goals are not credited to players), regular season only. The strike construction (floor 59.5 meaning 'at least 60', points thresholds inclusive) creates positive mass exactly at the boundary, and post-game scoring changes (assist corrections) can move a total by one late in the season.
stages.distribution: Discrete thresholds on integer counts; single-player contracts, so no dead-heat or 1/N rule applies; boundary events have positive probability mass.

stages.name: Player season points chain (KXNHLSEASONPPTS)
stages.description: A season points threshold such as 110+ for a defenceman is points banked plus a sum over remaining games of the per-game point process: on-ice goals for per 60, state-specific time on ice (especially power-play share), individual points percentage (credit on team goals), then the games-played distribution. Defencemen at 110 points sit in the extreme right tail of the rate posterior and depend on PP1 role security and health.
stages.distribution: Compound sum: negative-binomial per-game points over a games-played pmf with an injury left tail; the threshold probability lives in the right tail of the rate posterior for rare scorers.

opponent_matchup.note: A player's season total integrates over roughly 68 remaining opponents, so opponent quality averages out to a small common shift absorbed by the league scoring environment; no matchup-level mechanism is needed for goal or point thresholds.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and load management reach a player's season total only through games played, modelled by the games-played hazard; standings stakes change star usage only in the last weeks and are not a separate driver here.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching systems affect a player's season total only through ice time, PP unit and linemates, which are modelled as role inputs; a coaching change matters only through those role shifts.

game_context_script.note: Single-game script (score effects, empty-net timing) averages out across 82 games and enters season counts only through small average effects on rates; no game-level mechanism is needed for season totals.

officiating_rules.note: Penalty-calling tendencies affect season power-play opportunities, but their season-level effect is absorbed in the league scoring environment and team PP share, so no separate officiating input is needed.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Player season counting contracts resolved on official 2026-27 regular-season statistics: KXNHLPSEASONGOALS and KXNHLSEASONGOALS pay YES if the named player scores at least the stated number of goals (e.g. 60 or 40) during the regular season; KXNHLSEASONPPTS (reassigned here from the single-game points archetype) pays YES if the player reaches the stated points total, points being goals plus assists, regular season only. No minimum-games, trade or retirement clause is stated. The two goal series have empty secondary rules; only KXNHLSEASONPPTS states 'regular season stats only'.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official NHL regular-season player statistics (goals, assists, points).
variants_and_edge_cases: Two goal series (KXNHLPSEASONGOALS, KXNHLSEASONGOALS) price the same quantity with different thresholds and should be consistent for a player listed in both; points (KXNHLSEASONPPTS) add assists, which have a different persistence from goals.

Player goal totals: the official goals statistic counts empty-net and overtime goals but shootout-deciding goals are not credited to players (sc4); a traded player keeps his total; no minimum games clause is stated, so injury only lowers the total.
Strike construction: 'at least N' with floor_strike N-0.5; a player sitting exactly on the threshold at season end resolves YES, so late-season pace matters at the margin.

draft_selection.label: NHL draft selections (top pick and draft slot)
draft_selection.target: Whether a named prospect is selected at an exact overall slot, or within the top N overall slots, of the NHL Draft; determined by lottery and playoff-based draft order, pick ownership and sequential club choices.
draft_selection.mechanism: Draft order comes from two institutional pieces: slots 1-16 from the standings-weighted lottery among non-playoff clubs, slots 17-32 from playoff results, then pick ownership maps each slot to a club. Clubs choose sequentially from a shrinking board, so whether a named prospect lands at slot k depends on who was taken at slots 1..k-1; consensus is tight at the top and loose mid-round, where club need, general-manager habit, medical flags and late trades decide. Kalshi settles on the player and the overall slot, not on the club.

inputs.why: The lottery odds by final standing and ownership fix who owns each slot and the probability of moving up before selection.
Which club actually holds each first-round slot after trades, protections and forfeitures decides which team can select.
Rank-averaged public board plus its historical slot-agreement calibration is the prior over which prospect goes at each slot.
Cross-service disagreement about a prospect widens the distribution of the slot at which he is taken, beyond what the consensus gap alone implies.
Positional and pipeline need breaks ties between near-equal prospects at flat parts of the board.
A club's history of reaching for or following consensus changes how its pick is distributed.
A traded pick changes which club's preferences apply at a slot, and so which prospect is taken there, even though settlement is on the player.
Eligibility, medical and signing-path flags explain slides from the consensus rank.
The pre-lottery distribution of final standings determines the pool of lottery teams and their odds before the lottery is run.
Draft-week reports of a club's intentions are the main late signal on the top picks, and their reliability varies by source.
Lottery date, combine and draft day set when each information source arrives and when the contract can resolve.
Roster, coaching and front-office news changes club needs and may signal trades of picks before draft day.
Playoff clubs hold slots 17-32, ordered by playoff results, so slot contracts above 16 or top-N ladders with N>16 need the playoff-elimination order.
The set of prospects still available at slot k after slots 1..k-1 is the conditioning state that every exact-slot and top-N probability depends on.
League-adjusted scoring and combine testing explain where clubs deviate from the public consensus in the middle of round one.

interactions.hypothesis: A gap in mean consensus rank translates into a confident slot only when the services agree on each prospect; the same mean gap with high cross-service disagreement gives a much flatter slot distribution.

The probability a club selects at a slot is the lottery probability of that slot times the chance the club still owns the pick after protections resolve; protections only bind for specific lottery outcomes, so ownership and draw outcomes are jointly distributed, not independent.

Club need only decides the pick when the board is flat around the slot; below a dispersion threshold the consensus pick is taken regardless of need, so the need effect switches on at mid-first-round slots and is absent at the top.

A reach-prone general manager makes insider reports of an off-board choice more credible, and a consensus-following manager makes them less credible; credibility of the report and the club's historical reaching multiply rather than add.
Need acts only on the prospects left on the board: an early off-consensus pick removes a name and moves every later club's need-weighted choice, so need effects propagate down the order.

The consensus mean-rank gap between two prospects predicts their relative slots well only when services agree on each; with high cross-service disagreement the same mean gap carries little information and the slot distribution flattens.
interactions.how_to_test: Conditional logit with consensus gap, cross-service SD and their product as covariates; test the product term by held-out log-loss on drafts ~2012-present, split slot 1-3 vs 4-32.

interactions.hypothesis: The probability a club selects at a slot is the lottery probability of that slot times the chance the club still owns the pick after protections resolve; protections only bind for specific lottery outcomes, so ownership and draw outcomes are jointly distributed, not independent.
interactions.how_to_test: Enumerate lottery draw outcomes for a historical year with a protected pick and compare the marginal-by-product probability vs the joint enumeration of draw-and-protection outcomes.

interactions.hypothesis: Club need only decides the pick when the board is flat around the slot; below a dispersion threshold the consensus pick is taken regardless of need, so the need effect switches on at mid-first-round slots and is absent at the top.
interactions.how_to_test: Add need x flatness interaction and test whether the need coefficient is zero for slots 1-3 and positive for slots 8-20 in a conditional logit over remaining prospects.

interactions.hypothesis: A reach-prone general manager makes insider reports of an off-board choice more credible, and a consensus-following manager makes them less credible; credibility of the report and the club's historical reaching multiply rather than add. Untestable until insider reports are captured over several drafts (d7).
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test reported-pick accuracy by source for reach-prone vs consensus-following clubs and test an interaction term in the pick model.

interactions.hypothesis: Before the lottery, trade hazard concerns picks of unknown slot and is low for top slots; after the lottery and especially on draft day it concentrates on known slots, so the hazard regime changes at the lottery date and again on draft day.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate pick-change frequency separately in windows before lottery, between lottery and draft day, and on draft day, and test slot x window interaction.

interactions.hypothesis: Need matters only over the prospects left: if an earlier club takes the defenceman a later club needed, that club's choice moves to the next need fit, so an off-consensus pick propagates down the order and the named prospect's slot pmf shifts as a whole.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare a sequential simulation with need terms against independent slot-by-slot predictions, by log-loss of each prospect's actual slot, on drafts with one or more top-10 reaches.

nonlinearities.shape: Probability the consensus rank-k prospect goes exactly at k falls convexly with k: near 0.8-0.9 at k=1, quickly below 0.3 by k=5-10
nonlinearities.why: Historical agreement between consensus and actual slot is high only at the very top; a linear rank effect overstates mid-round confidence for exact-slot contracts.

nonlinearities.shape: Odds of winning a draw are concentrated in the worst few clubs and capped by the 10-place rise limit
nonlinearities.why: The published odds are not proportional to standing; the two draws and movement cap make the mapping from points rank to slot piecewise.

nonlinearities.shape: Need effect saturates: beyond a modest positional deficit extra need adds little because clubs rarely reach more than a few slots
nonlinearities.why: Clubs trade need off against board value; a large need does not translate into proportionally larger reach, so the effect is bounded.

nonlinearities.shape: Top-N probability is a CDF in N: flat near 0 until slots where the prospect becomes available, steep near consensus rank, then saturating
nonlinearities.why: Top-N rungs are nested; P(by N) must be non-decreasing in N and the exact-slot pmf is its first difference, so ladder rungs must be priced from one joint simulation.

mechanism_review.summary: A draft-slot contract on a named prospect is the end of a sequential chain. Slots 1-16 belong to the non-playoff clubs in reverse standings order, reshuffled by a two-draw weighted lottery (maximum rise of 10 places, no club winning more than twice in five years); slots 17-32 belong to playoff clubs, set by how far each went in the playoffs. Trades, protections and forfeitures map each slot to a holding club. Public services and club staff form boards; each holder chooses from whatever is left, so the probability the prospect goes exactly at slot k equals P(still available at k) times P(chosen | available, holder at k), and top-N is the cumulative sum over k<=N. The chain is institutional, sharp at the top of the board and diffuse mid-round, and information arrives in jumps (lottery night, combine, draft week).

stages.name: Standings and playoff results set the pre-lottery order
stages.description: Non-playoff clubs (16 of 32) hold slots 1-16 in inverse order of regular-season points percentage and tiebreakers, which also fixes their lottery odds. Playoff clubs keep their own picks and hold slots 17-32: conference-final losers pick 29-30, the Cup finalist 31 and the winner 32, with first- and second-round losers ordered by regular-season points under a rule whose division-winner detail is unverified (d5). Before the season ends this stage is a season and playoff simulation; afterwards it is deterministic.
stages.distribution: Discrete permutation of 32 clubs; slots 1-16 fixed at season end, slots 17-32 fixed only as playoff rounds finish.

stages.name: Lottery draws and ownership assignment
stages.description: The lottery holds two weighted draws among the 16 non-playoff clubs; a winner may rise at most 10 places, and the remaining lottery clubs fall in standings order. After the draws, pick ownership (trades, top-N protections, conditional swaps, forfeitures) assigns each slot to a holding club; protections resolve only once the lottery result is known, so the draw and ownership are joint.
stages.distribution: Weighted random draw without replacement; only top slots random, remaining slots a deterministic order with ownership overlay.

stages.name: Prospect board formation and consensus
stages.description: Scouting services and club staff rank the eligible prospects. The public board is summarised by mean consensus rank, the agreement among services on each prospect, and league-adjusted production and combine testing that clubs weigh differently from the services. Eligibility, injuries and signing paths demote some players. Agreement is high at the top and low across slots 8-25.
stages.distribution: Ranked order with slot-dependent dispersion; tight at the top, wide in the middle and late first round.

stages.name: Club decision rule: board, need and staff style
stages.description: Each holding club chooses from the remaining board using its own ranking (partly consensus, partly staff-specific preferences), roster and pipeline need, and an appetite for risk. Between close prospects need and staff habit decide; at the top the choice is nearly forced by consensus. Clubs also decide whether to trade the pick or trade up, which changes the selecting club.
stages.distribution: Categorical choice over the remaining board; concentrated at slot 1-3, spread across 3-8 names in the middle of round one.

stages.name: Sequential depletion of the board and ladder settlement
stages.description: Picks are made in order, so the choice at slot k is a conditional choice over prospects not taken at 1..k-1. One off-consensus pick early shifts every later slot by one name. The exact-slot contract therefore needs the joint path of the first k picks, simulated (e.g. Plackett-Luce or conditional logit over the remaining board with club-specific utilities), and the top-N contract is the cumulative availability-and-choice probability summed over slots 1..N, monotone in N.
stages.distribution: Joint categorical path over the first k slots; the named prospect's slot pmf is unimodal near consensus rank with a long right tail of slides.

stages.name: Late information and announcement
stages.description: In draft week insider reports, combine medicals and trade rumours move the likelihood of particular selections in jumps; the outcome settles when the pick is announced at the draft. The sampled rules settle on the player selected at an overall slot, so post-selection trades of the player do not matter, while a pre-selection trade of the pick changes which club's board applies.
stages.distribution: Binary resolution after a discrete announcement; late reports shift probabilities in jumps, not smoothly.

talent_strength.note: Prospect quality enters as the public consensus order and league-adjusted production; not on-ice performance of the selecting club.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent in a draft selection; the only interaction is between the holding club's needs and the remaining board, handled under role_personnel.

role_personnel.note: Club needs and decision-maker habits determine the selection among close prospects.

availability_news.note: Medical, eligibility and draft-week reporting change who is available at a slot.

coaching_scheme.note: On-ice coaching tactics do not decide draft choices; the relevant staff effect is the general manager and scouting director behaviour captured in gm_draft_behavior_history.

environment.note: Venue, weather and travel have no bearing on a draft selection made at a league event; no environmental variable alters the outcome.

game_context_script.note: No game is played; there is no score state, pace or overtime. The comparable timeline structure is the lottery-then-draft sequence in the calendar.

pace_volume.note: No count of events accumulates; the outcome is one selection per slot, not a volume of shots, possessions or plays over a window.

efficiency_conversion.note: No conversion rate generates the outcome; how often consensus translates into the actual pick is a calibration held in prospect_consensus_ranking.

distribution_variance.note: Cross-service disagreement and the sequential-depletion path set the width and right tail of the prospect's slot pmf.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Standings stakes determine the pool, and the timeline of lottery and draft day sets when trades and information arrive.

officiating_rules.note: League lottery rules (two draws, max rise 10, two wins in five years), the playoff-slot ordering rule and pick-ownership rules govern the process.

settlement_contract.note: Rules settle on player + overall slot (exact or top N); the slot pmf/CDF from the board path maps directly to both. Source of truth and forfeiture numbering unresolved (d1).
